title: Venue Radar related-venue search
method: Eight searchers (one per topic family) proposed venues; a separate reviewer checked each batch against official and society pages and tried to reject it; a completeness critic looked for gaps. ICORE ranks were re-matched against the official ICORE2026 export on 2026-10-31; CCF, Google Scholar, size and acceptance figures are the reviewers' notes and were not independently re-verified. The shared web-search budget ran out partway through the run, so later facts rely on direct fetches of official pages.

tiers.recommend: Legitimate, well regarded and central to the catalog scope
tiers.strong: Legitimate, often top-ranked, only partly inside the catalog topics
tiers.consider: Legitimate; weaker fit, lower tier or thinner evidence
tiers.longshot: Legitimate but niche, low-tier or far from the core

statuses: added 2026-10-31 = in the catalog (see data/conferences.yml); owner maybe = owner marked Maybe; candidate = not added; rejected after vetting = reviewer rejected

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Algorithmic Learning Theory
candidates.verdict_reason: Long-running learning-theory venue with PMLR proceedings, ICORE2026 B and CCF C. It is the established companion to the tracked COLT. The only drawback is timing: the 2027 deadline has passed.
candidates.subtopics: learning theory; online learning and bandits; statistical learning; optimisation
candidates.organizer: Association for Algorithmic Learning Theory (AALT, founded 2018; a sister organisation of the body that runs COLT). ALT 2027 PC chairs are Surbhi Goel and Nikita Zhivotovskiy.
candidates.publication: PMLR every year since 2017 (ALT 2026 = vol. 313; ALT 2025 = vol. 272)
candidates.size: 69 papers at ALT 2026 (Toronto, PMLR v313); 51 papers at ALT 2025 (Milan)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (portal id 106); CCF 2026 C (AI); not in the Google Scholar top-20 lists for AI or Theoretical CS
candidates.next_meeting: ALT 2027: Leiden, Netherlands, 9–12 Mar 2027 (in person only)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: 12 Oct 2026 AoE (confirmed, already passed). The ALT 2028 deadline is not announced; by pattern it falls around Oct 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Core ML theory, filling the gap next to COLT and AISTATS. The scope is central to ml-ai, not adjacent.
candidates.concerns: No open submission until the ALT 2028 cycle. Presentation must be in person. Below COLT in standing.

candidates.full_name: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning
candidates.verdict_reason: Unranked because it is young (2022). Still clearly legitimate: PMLR volumes every year, OpenReview review with ACs and rebuttal, and a strong advisory board. It is the dedicated causal-ML venue, and the 16 Nov deadline is open.
candidates.subtopics: causal discovery and inference; causal representation learning; causal ML
candidates.organizer: CLeaR organising committee and advisory board (includes Judea Pearl, James Robins, Léon Bottou, Max Welling and Peter Spirtes). 2027: General Chair Fabrice Carrat (Sorbonne); PCs Karthika Mohan and Shohei Shimizu.
candidates.publication: PMLR every year: v177 (2022), v213, v236, v275 and v323 (2026). Authors may instead opt for a 1-page extended abstract that points to the reviewed full paper.
candidates.size: 53 papers at CLeaR 2026 (Cambridge MA, PMLR v323); 58 at CLeaR 2025 (Lausanne, v275)
candidates.rankings: none found (absent from the ICORE2026 export and CCF 2026; GS h5 not checked)
candidates.next_meeting: CLeaR 2027: 3–5 May 2027, International Conference Center, Sorbonne University (Pierre and Marie Curie campus), Paris
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (12 PMLR pages plus appendices) on OpenReview: 16 Nov 2026, 11:59pm AoE
candidates.why_fit: Fills the probabilistic/causal ML subtopic with a specialist venue. Peer of UAI and ProbML, with no identity overlap.
candidates.concerns: Young, small and unranked, so standing rests on its PC and advisory board rather than on rankings. The official site is JavaScript-rendered, so facts were read from its bundled content.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Parallel Problem Solving from Nature
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier European evolutionary-computation conference (ICORE2026 A, CCF B, GS h5 22) and a natural peer of the tracked GECCO and EuroGP. The only weakness is practical: there is no edition before 2028.
candidates.subtopics: evolutionary computation; iterative optimisation heuristics; theory of EC; EC + ML
candidates.organizer: PPSN steering committee of the European EC community. 2026 host: University of Trento (Conference Chair Giovanni Iacca). The 2026 site does not list the steering committee.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (2026: five volumes, LNCS 16985–16989)
candidates.size: About 165 papers in 8 poster sessions at PPSN 2026 (official booklet); submission IDs reach ~825
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (no official figure; booklet IDs suggest selective review, but that is not a rate)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A (portal id 1676); CCF 2026 B (AI); GS h5-index 22 (#11 in Evolutionary Computation)
candidates.cadence: Biennial, even years, late Aug–early Sep
candidates.next_meeting: PPSN 2028: host city and dates not announced (2026 was Trento, 29 Aug–2 Sep)
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown: the PPSN 2028 full-paper call is not published (historically spring of the conference year)
candidates.why_fit: Core venue of the EC community already represented by GECCO and EuroGP, and explicitly invites EC+ML work.
candidates.concerns: Nothing to schedule until 2028. The claim that a 2028 host call is open could not be verified. Papers are presented only as posters.

candidates.full_name: SIAM Conference on Mathematics of Data Science
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate SIAM activity-group meeting with a relevant scope. But it is non-archival and unranked, its selectivity is unknown, its deadlines could not be verified, and the next open call is the 2028 meeting.
candidates.subtopics: mathematical foundations of ML; high-dimensional data; optimisation; geometric and algebraic data analysis
candidates.organizer: SIAM Activity Group on Data Science
candidates.publication: none (minisymposium and contributed abstracts; non-archival)
candidates.size: unknown (attendance not found; siam.org returned 403)
candidates.rankings: none found (not in the ICORE2026 export or CCF 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: MDS26: 16–20 Nov 2026, Salt Palace Convention Center, Salt Lake City, held jointly with IS26 and the tracked SDM26. MDS28 is not announced.
candidates.next_deadline: MDS26 abstract deadlines have passed (exact dates not verifiable; siam.org is blocked by a WAF). MDS28 deadlines are unknown.
candidates.why_fit: Math-of-ML meeting in the SIAM abstract style the catalog already uses. Note: the tracked SIAM DS is Dynamical Systems, not data science, so MDS is not its counterpart.
candidates.concerns: Non-archival, with low or unknown selectivity typical of SIAM minisymposia. Co-located with the tracked SDM in 2026. Official pages could not be read directly; dates come from SIAM's engage.siam.org event listing.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on the Applications of Evolutionary Computation (part of EvoStar)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate (ICORE2026 B, GS h5 19, Springer LNCS, SPECIES/EvoStar). But it is applied EC run through themed special sessions of uneven depth, and it would add a near-duplicate EvoStar entry with the same deadline as the tracked EuroGP.
candidates.subtopics: applied evolutionary computation; swarm intelligence; EC for ML, games, sustainability and health
candidates.organizer: EvoStar, organised by the SPECIES society. 2027 PCs: Josefa Díaz-Álvarez and Jamal Toutouh.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS; double-blind review with at least 3 reviewers per paper
candidates.size: About 67 accepted papers in 2026 (Toulouse): ~40 long and ~27 short talks
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (portal id 2218); not in CCF 2026; GS h5-index 19 (#15 in Evolutionary Computation)
candidates.next_meeting: EvoStar 2027: Mainz, Germany, 31 Mar–2 Apr 2027 (hybrid)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: 16 Nov 2026 (extended from 1 Nov; AoE per organiser post)
candidates.why_fit: Same event and deadlines as the tracked EuroGP; EC is within ml-ai through GECCO and EuroGP.
candidates.concerns: Nine themed special sessions in 2027, so quality varies by track. Adjacent rather than central (applied EC). Redundant with the EuroGP entry for calendar purposes.

candidates.full_name: European Conference on Evolutionary Computation in Combinatorial Optimisation (part of EvoStar)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and ICORE2026 B, but very small (10 papers in 2026). Its combinatorial-optimisation / operations-research focus is only adjacent to the catalog. Lowest priority of the EvoStar options.
candidates.subtopics: metaheuristics; combinatorial optimisation; landscape analysis
candidates.organizer: EvoStar, organised by the SPECIES society. 2027 chairs: Nelishia Pillay and Bing Xue.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS; 14-page papers, double-blind review
candidates.size: 10 accepted papers in 2026 (official accepted-papers list)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (portal id 2195); not in CCF 2026; not in the GS Evolutionary Computation top 20
candidates.next_meeting: EvoStar 2027: Mainz, Germany, 31 Mar–2 Apr 2027 (hybrid)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: 16 Nov 2026 (extended from 1 Nov)
candidates.why_fit: Optimisation sibling of the tracked EuroGP at the same event.
candidates.concerns: Tiny programme and narrow, OR-flavoured scope. Little overlap with the catalog's ML, neuroscience and dynamics core. Another duplicate EvoStar entry.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate. It is an IEEE CIS flagship that has run since 1994, it is ranked ICORE2026 B and CCF C, and its 2027 dates and deadlines are confirmed. It sits at the same tier as the tracked IJCNN and next to GECCO and EuroGP.
candidates.subtopics: evolutionary computation; swarm intelligence; EC-based optimisation; evolutionary ML
candidates.organizer: IEEE Computational Intelligence Society. CEC 2027 general chairs are Amir Hussain and Xin Yao; programme chairs are Ke Li and Bing Xue.
candidates.publication: IEEE conference proceedings (IEEE Xplore); a companion proceedings for short papers
candidates.size: Attendance and accepted-paper counts are not published on the official site. Output is very large: GS h5 94, 3rd in Evolutionary Computation and above GECCO (49).
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (portal id 2061); CCF 2026 C (AI); GS h5-index 94 (Evolutionary Computation)
candidates.cadence: Annual. Standalone in odd years; in even years it runs inside WCCI, co-located with the tracked IJCNN.
candidates.next_meeting: CEC 2027: Edinburgh International Conference Centre, Edinburgh, UK, 25–28 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper 28 Feb 2027 (no extension); short paper 15 Mar 2027; notification 7 Apr 2027
candidates.why_fit: Main IEEE venue for evolutionary computation and swarm intelligence. It sits beside the tracked GECCO, EuroGP, IJCNN and SSCI.
candidates.concerns: Very large, high-volume congress; no acceptance rate is published. Even-year editions duplicate the dates of IJCNN/WCCI. Broad within EC; quality depends on the track.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE CIS flagship; 33 editions since 1994; well-known chairs; EDAS submission; IEEE-sponsored

candidates.full_name: ACM/SIGEVO Conference on Foundations of Genetic Algorithms
candidates.verdict_reason: Highly regarded and ranked ICORE2026 A, organised by ACM SIGEVO since 1990. Its scope is narrow evolutionary-algorithm theory, peripheral to the catalog's ML core, and FOGA 2027 has not been announced.
candidates.subtopics: theory of evolutionary algorithms; runtime analysis; black-box optimisation
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGEVO (same organiser as the tracked GECCO)
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings (ACM DL)
candidates.size: 26 accepted papers (2025)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A (portal id 546); not in CCF 2026; not in the GS Evolutionary Computation top 20
candidates.cadence: Biennial, odd years, late Aug or early Sep
candidates.next_meeting: FOGA 2027 not announced. FOGA 2025 was Leiden, 27–29 Aug 2025.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper around early May 2027, estimated (4 May in 2023 and 5 May in 2025, both after extensions)
candidates.why_fit: Theory counterpart of the tracked GECCO; covers runtime analysis and black-box optimisation theory
candidates.concerns: Small and theory-only. Its relevance to the ML, neuroscience and dynamics core is weak. No official 2027 site, venue or dates.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM SIGEVO; 35-year history; ACM proceedings; credible keynotes (Glasmachers, Knowles) and organisers (Doerr, Bäck)

candidates.full_name: Conference on Parsimony and Learning
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and well staffed, with PMLR proceedings, strong chairs and strong keynotes. It is only three editions old, has no ICORE or CCF rank, and its organising committee rotates with no published steering committee.
candidates.subtopics: sparsity and low-rank structure; efficient deep learning; optimisation; parsimonious representations
candidates.organizer: Rotating CPAL organising committee. 2027 general chairs are Yi Ma (HKU) and Taiji Suzuki (UTokyo/RIKEN AIP), with five programme chairs. No steering committee is listed.
candidates.publication: PMLR, proceedings track only (vols 234, 280, 328); the spotlight track is non-archival
candidates.size: 54 PMLR proceedings papers (2026), plus the spotlight track; attendance not published
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.cadence: Annual, March: Hong Kong 2024, Stanford 2025, Tübingen 2026, Tokyo 2027
candidates.next_meeting: CPAL 2027 (4th): Hitotsubashi Hall, Tokyo, 23–26 Mar 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Proceedings-track full paper 5 Dec 2026 AoE; non-archival spotlight track 18 Jan 2027
candidates.why_fit: ML venue for sparsity, low-rank structure and efficient learning, at the boundary of ML theory, optimisation and signal processing
candidates.concerns: Young (since 2024) and unranked, with no acceptance statistics. The archival deadline is about five weeks away.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: PMLR every year. Keynotes include Belkin, Sugiyama, Fukumizu and Chi (2027), and Ganguli, Baraniuk and Unser (2025). Hosts have been HKU, Stanford Data Science and ELLIS/MPI-IS Tübingen. Reviewing on OpenReview.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-standing community meeting, ranked ICORE2026 C, with PMLR proceedings. Its rank is modest and NeSy 2027 has not been announced, so dates are estimated only.
candidates.subtopics: neurosymbolic AI; learning and reasoning; logic and neural networks; knowledge graphs
candidates.organizer: Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning Association. The 2025 volume editors included Pascal Hitzler and Eleonora Giunchiglia.
candidates.publication: PMLR for main-track full and short papers (vol 284 for 2025). Extended papers can go to an IOS Press special issue of Neurosymbolic Artificial Intelligence.
candidates.size: 58 PMLR papers (2025); attendance not published
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 C (portal id 2340); not in CCF 2026; GS h5 not checked
candidates.cadence: Annual, September. A workshop from 2005; a conference since 2024.
candidates.next_meeting: NeSy 2027 not announced. NeSy 2026 (20th) was Lisbon (FCUL), 1–4 Sep 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Phase-1 abstract around late Feb 2027 and full paper around early Mar 2027, estimated from 2026 (24 Feb and 3 Mar); a later phase 2 around June
candidates.why_fit: Main venue for combining learning with symbolic reasoning, next to the tracked KR, IJCAI and AAAI
candidates.concerns: Small, with a modest rank. The association homepage looks stale. Identity trap: PMLR vol 288 'Neurosymbolic Systems 2025' is a different event.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 20 editions; dedicated association and journal; PMLR proceedings; two-phase peer review

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Probabilistic Graphical Models
candidates.verdict_reason: Solid, single-track community conference with PMLR proceedings since 2016, an IJAR special issue and a strong PC. It is unranked and biennial, and PGM 2028 has no announced venue or dates.
candidates.subtopics: graphical models; probabilistic inference; causal discovery; Bayesian networks
candidates.organizer: PGM research community, with venues chosen edition by edition and no formal society. 2026 PCs were Varando, Leonelli and Camps-Valls. The 67-member PC includes Larrañaga, Bielza, Druzdzel and Studený.
candidates.publication: PMLR (vols 52, 72, 138, 186, 246); IJAR special issue for extended papers
candidates.size: 32 PMLR papers (2024); the 2026 programme had about 48 papers/posters, single-track, plus 5 invited talks
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.cadence: Biennial, even years, September; editions since 2002
candidates.next_meeting: PGM 2028 not announced. PGM 2026 (13th) was Valencia, 9–11 Sep 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract around 22 May 2028 and full paper around 30 May 2028, estimated from 2026
candidates.why_fit: European home venue for graphical models, probabilistic inference and causal discovery; complements the tracked UAI and AISTATS
candidates.concerns: Unranked and small. The next edition is about two years away with no announcement.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 13 editions since 2002 at established universities; PMLR plus IJAR; credible PC; OpenReview reviewing; AIJ sponsorship

candidates.full_name: Symposium on Conformal and Probabilistic Prediction with Applications
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate: the field's founders are honorary chairs and it has published in PMLR every year. It is the home venue of conformal prediction, central to ML uncertainty quantification, and its 2027 dates and deadline are confirmed.
candidates.subtopics: conformal prediction; uncertainty quantification; calibrated and probabilistic prediction
candidates.organizer: Conformal-prediction community, led from Royal Holloway. Honorary chairs are Vovk, Gammerman and Vapnik; 2027 general chairs are Carlevaro (CNR) and Nguyen (RHUL).
candidates.publication: PMLR every year since 2017 (2026: vol 329), covering full papers and poster abstracts
candidates.size: 65 PMLR papers including poster abstracts (2026); attendance not published
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: COPA 2027 (16th): University of Genoa, Via Balbi 5, Genoa, Italy, 14–16 Sep 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (up to 20 pp, JMLR format) 1 May 2027; 2-page poster extended abstract 1 Jul 2027
candidates.why_fit: Core venue for conformal prediction and calibrated uncertainty quantification, a mainstream ML topic
candidates.concerns: Niche, small and unranked. Poster abstracts appear in the same PMLR volume as full papers, so counts overstate full papers.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 15 editions since 2012 at universities; founders of the field involved; PMLR; Chervonenkis best-paper awards

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and top-tier for reasoning (ICORE A). It fits only the Knowledge Representation & Reasoning and optimisation side of ml-ai, and only about 10 of 62 papers in 2026 involved ML. It is the strongest option if the owner wants reasoning coverage beyond KR and ICAPS.
candidates.subtopics: constraint programming; combinatorial optimisation; CP+ML (neurosymbolic search, learned heuristics)
candidates.organizer: Association for Constraint Programming (ACP); sponsored by EurAI and AIJ in 2026
candidates.publication: LIPIcs (Dagstuhl) since 2021; Springer LNCS 1995–2020
candidates.size: 62 accepted papers in 2026 (59 regular, 3 short); attendance not stated (held inside FLoC 2026)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A; CCF2026 B (PDF p.28, software/PL category); GS h5-index 20
candidates.cadence: Annual, summer (Jul–Sep). CP 2026 was in Lisbon (FLoC), 20–23 Jul 2026
candidates.next_meeting: CP 2027 is not announced: no cp2027.a4cp.org site, and the ACP home page does not mention it
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract registration about early March 2027, full paper about mid-March 2027 (CP 2026: 2 Mar and 14 Mar)
candidates.why_fit: A peer of the tracked KR and ICAPS for the Knowledge Representation & Reasoning and optimisation topics. ML and generative AI is a primary keyword, and ML-guided search papers appear.
candidates.concerns: Core community is constraint reasoning and operations research, and ML is a minority. The 2027 edition is not announced. The bare a4cp.org host has a TLS certificate mismatch, so use www.a4cp.org.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by a society (ACP), with 30+ editions in Springer LNCS and then LIPIcs, and EurAI and AIJ sponsorship. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: International Joint Conference on Learning & Reasoning
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and well regarded by the symbolic/relational ML community, with a strong steering committee and Springer LNAI plus an MLJ special issue. It is small, unranked under its own name, and has no announced 2027 edition.
candidates.subtopics: inductive logic programming; statistical relational AI; neurosymbolic learning; program synthesis
candidates.organizer: IJCLR steering committee (Muggleton, Bundy, Schmid, Malerba, Tamaddoni-Nezhad, Dai, Ferri); absorbs ILP, AAIP and CogAI
candidates.publication: Springer LNAI for long and short papers; invited MLJ post-conference special issue; late-breaking work on the website
candidates.size: About 35 programme papers in 2026 (including late-breaking, recently published and demos) plus 4 keynotes (provisional programme)
candidates.rankings: IJCLR none found. Its ILP strand is ICORE2026 B and CCF2026 C (PDF p.60). NeSy, now a separate conference, is ICORE2026 C. No GS h5-index found.
candidates.next_meeting: IJCLR 2027 is not announced
candidates.next_deadline: Main-track paper about late May to mid-June 2027 (2026: 31 May, extended to 15 Jun)
candidates.why_fit: Covers ML combined with reasoning (ILP, program synthesis, statistical relational and neurosymbolic learning). It complements the tracked KR for the Knowledge Representation & Reasoning topic.
candidates.concerns: Small meeting with a mixed track that includes recently published papers. It is unranked under the IJCLR name. The 2026 site shows AIJ sponsorship, not EurAI. NeSy now runs as its own conference, so the neurosymbolic overlap is partial.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-standing ILP lineage, a well-known steering committee, Springer LNAI and an MLJ special issue. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and growing: PMLR proceedings, double-blind review, strong international keynotes and about 280 attendees. It is regional, hosted by one university centre with no society behind it, unranked, and has a low h5-index (9).
candidates.subtopics: deep learning; computer vision; ML for the sciences and health
candidates.organizer: UiT The Arctic University of Norway / SFI Visual Intelligence
candidates.publication: PMLR since 2024 (vols 233, 265, 307); Septentrio 2020–23; extended abstracts are non-archival
candidates.size: 279 attendees from 35 countries in 2026; about 37 papers in PMLR vol 307
candidates.rankings: None found in ICORE2026 or CCF2026. GS h5-index 9 (listed as 'Proceedings of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Workshop').
candidates.cadence: Annual (January, Tromsø), run with a winter school; 2026 was the 7th proceedings edition
candidates.next_meeting: Tromsø, 12–14 Jan 2027 (with the winter school, 11–15 Jan)
candidates.next_deadline: NLDL 2027 full papers (14 Aug 2026) and abstracts (Sep 2026) have passed. NLDL 2028 full papers expected about mid-August 2027.
candidates.why_fit: A general deep-learning meeting with ML-for-science and imaging content. It is a smaller, AALTD-like option next to the tracked big ML venues.
candidates.concerns: Regional, single-host meeting with no steering society. Unranked, with a low citation profile and only about 37 papers. The 2027 deadlines have passed, so the first usable deadline is in 2027 for the 2028 meeting.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Seven PMLR or Septentrio proceedings volumes, OpenReview double-blind review, and keynotes such as Schölkopf, van der Schaar, Gretton and Kutyniok. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on the Integration of Constraint Programming, Artificial Intelligence and Operations Research
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and long-running (ICORE B, h5-index 18, Springer LNCS), and its deadlines are confirmed on the official site, contrary to the 'aggregators only' flag. It leans towards operations research and optimisation, so it is a weaker fit than CP.
candidates.subtopics: CP/AI/OR integration; combinatorial optimisation; ML for optimisation
candidates.organizer: CPAIOR community; 2027 chairs are S. Roussel (ONERA) and C. Artigues (LAAS-CNRS). No steering committee is listed on the 2027 site.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS for regular long and short papers; extended abstracts (1–2 pages) are non-archival
candidates.size: Unknown; the 2026 accepted-paper count was not shown
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B; not in CCF2026; GS h5-index 18
candidates.next_meeting: Toulouse, France, 1–4 Jun 2027 (28th meeting, 24th with proceedings)
candidates.next_deadline: Regular papers: abstract 1 Dec 2026, full paper 7 Dec 2026 (AoE). Non-archival extended abstracts: 25 Mar 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Combines optimisation and reasoning with growing ML-for-combinatorial-optimisation content. Relevant to the Evolutionary Computation & Optimization and Knowledge Representation & Reasoning topics.
candidates.concerns: Operations-research centre of gravity. Lower tier than CP. The 2027 programme committee is still TBA.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 21+ Springer LNCS volumes, French national-lab chairs in 2027, and ICORE B. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Theory and Applications of Satisfiability Testing
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably legitimate and top-ranked (ICORE A, CCF B), but it is the weakest scope fit here. CCF classes it as theoretical computer science, and ML is peripheral to its SAT/SMT, proof-complexity and verification core. Add it only if the owner wants automated-reasoning coverage.
candidates.subtopics: SAT/SMT/MaxSAT solving; proof complexity; automated reasoning
candidates.organizer: SAT Association (also publishes JSAT)
candidates.publication: LIPIcs (Dagstuhl); the SAT 2026 proceedings ISBN is from Dagstuhl
candidates.size: Unknown (accepted-paper count not verified)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A; CCF2026 B (PDF p.42, theory category); GS h5-index 20
candidates.cadence: Annual (summer); SAT 2026 was in Lisbon (FLoC), Jul 2026
candidates.next_meeting: 30th edition: Barcelona, Spain, 5–9 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract about early March 2027, full paper about mid-March 2027 (SAT 2026: 2 Mar and 10 Mar). The 2027 CFP page says 'details will be announced'.
candidates.why_fit: Covers the automated-reasoning part of the Knowledge Representation & Reasoning topic, including some ML-for-solvers work.
candidates.concerns: Logic and verification focus with little ML. Out of the catalog's core ML, neuroscience and dynamics identity. The 2027 CFP, dates and proceedings pages are still empty.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Overseen by the SAT Association, with LIPIcs proceedings and ICORE A. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering
candidates.verdict_reason: Elite and legitimate (ICORE A*, CCF A, h5-index 82), but scope fit is weak. Its 2027 CFP says ML papers without a data-engineering focus are out of scope and may be desk-rejected. It is a database-systems flagship rather than an ML or data-mining venue.
candidates.subtopics: data management; data engineering; ML for data systems; data-centric mining
candidates.organizer: IEEE (Computer Society TCDE series; TCDE is not named on the 2027 home page)
candidates.publication: IEEE proceedings via Conference Publishing Services (IEEE Xplore); best papers invited to IEEE TKDE
candidates.size: Large (hundreds of papers per year); exact 2026 counts not verified
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A*; CCF2026 A (PDF p.35, databases); GS h5-index 82 (#9 in Databases & Information Systems)
candidates.cadence: Annual (Apr–May), with 2 submission rounds. 2026 Montréal, 5–8 May
candidates.next_meeting: 43rd edition: Copenhagen, Denmark, 17–21 May 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Research papers, round 2 (full paper, 12 pages): 11 Nov 2026, 5:00 PM Pacific. Round 1 closed 11 Jun 2026.

candidates.full_name: Pacific Rim International Conference on Artificial Intelligence

candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long series since 1990 with Springer LNAI proceedings, ICORE B and CCF C ranks, double-anonymous review and credible keynotes (e.g. C. Bhattacharyya, Weiru Liu). No predatory signals found.

candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Founded by Marco Dorigo's IRIDIA group, with an eminent steering committee, Springer LNCS proceedings, a special issue in the Swarm Intelligence journal, and credible keynotes (e.g. Guido de Croon). No predatory signals found.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Distributed Artificial Intelligence
candidates.verdict_reason: Not predatory: prominent chairs and keynotes, ACM ICPS proceedings, CCF C. It is young (2019), not ICORE-ranked, with no citation evidence found and an experimental AI-authored paper track. Previously deferred.

candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Membership society of vision scientists with an elected board and a Board-appointed Abstract Review Committee. Abstracts are published in Journal of Vision.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate, long-running and the top venue for document analysis. Its scope is a specialised application of vision, similar to the tracked IJCB and FG, rather than central to the catalog.
candidates.subtopics: document image analysis, OCR/handwriting recognition, document understanding
candidates.organizer: IAPR-sponsored series (TC10/TC11 community) with rotating local organisers. The 2026 edition was hosted by TU Wien.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (four volumes in 2026), plus an ICDAR-IJDAR journal track.
candidates.size: 2026 (Vienna): about 140 main-track papers plus IJDAR-track and competition papers; over 500 participants (official site). The 2027 site expects about 450.
candidates.acceptance_rate: Unknown for 2026. The scout's ~45% (142/314) for 2025 was not re-verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A (scout's figure; the CORE portal returned 403, so not re-verified). CCF C (ccf.atom.im mirror). GS h5 30, median 49.
candidates.next_meeting: 21st ICDAR, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, Aug 18-22, 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Main-track full paper Feb 28, 2027 (AoE). The IJDAR journal-track full paper is due Nov 15, 2026.
candidates.why_fit: Document vision, OCR and document understanding overlap with vision-language models. It matches the tracked specialised IAPR/vision venues (IJCB, FG, ICPR).
candidates.concerns: icdar2027.org runs on a website builder and does not yet name a committee or IAPR, although Wikipedia corroborates Kuala Lumpur 2027. WASET-style look-alike 'ICDAR' listings exist, so trust only the icdarYYYY.org sites. Narrow application scope.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run since 1991 under IAPR sponsorship. Double-blind review with rebuttal, LNCS proceedings and a companion IJDAR journal track.

candidates.full_name: DAGM German Conference on Pattern Recognition
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, society-run and long-standing, but a small regional venue. Its citation impact is well below the tracked BMVC, and it is not ranked by CORE or CCF.
candidates.subtopics: computer vision, pattern recognition, machine learning
candidates.organizer: DAGM e.V. (Deutsche Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Mustererkennung, the German pattern-recognition society)
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS. Best papers are invited to an IJCV special issue. 2026 also offered a non-archival 4-page extended-abstract track.
candidates.size: Over 200 participants (official). The 2025 programme had 17 orals plus four poster sessions. The scout's count of 40 of 85 full papers (2025) was not re-verified.
candidates.acceptance_rate: Unknown (the scout's ~47% for 2025 was not re-verified)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 none found (scout; portal blocked, not re-verified). CCF not listed. GS h5 23, median 38.
candidates.cadence: Annual (DAGM symposia since 1978; named GCPR since 2013). Joint with VMV in even years.
candidates.next_meeting: Bielefeld, Germany, Sep 21-24, 2027 (tutorials Sep 21, main conference Sep 22-24)
candidates.next_deadline: Regular full papers due June 2027 (day not yet set). Fast-review track and Nectar-track proposals due July 2027.
candidates.why_fit: General computer vision, pattern recognition and ML venue, comparable in style to BMVC on a smaller, regional scale.
candidates.concerns: Small, regionally focused audience. The official dates page gives only months. 2026 keynotes were strong (Heide, Ricci, Mitra), but the venue carries limited international weight.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: National society (DAGM) with a nearly 50-year history, LNCS proceedings and an IJCV special-issue partnership.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Computational Photography
candidates.verdict_reason: Small but elite venue at the core of computational imaging and vision, with top-tier organisers and a TPAMI special-issue track. The 2027 deadline is confirmed.
candidates.subtopics: computational imaging, cameras/optics, neural and physics-based rendering
candidates.organizer: ICCP steering committee with IEEE Computer Society TCPAMI sponsorship. 2027 program chairs: C. Metzler, A. Pediredla, A. Watnik, G. Wetzstein.
candidates.publication: One double-blind review leads to either an IEEE TPAMI special issue on Computational Photography or the ICCP proceedings (both confirmed for 2027). Submission is through OpenReview.
candidates.size: Small single-track meeting where all accepted papers are talks. The 2026 programme had about 13 paper sessions, i.e. a few dozen papers.
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (scout's figure; not re-verified). CCF not listed. No GS h5 found (papers are split between TPAMI and the proceedings).
candidates.next_meeting: University of Maryland, College Park, MD, USA, Aug 2-4, 2027 (summer school Jul 31-Aug 1)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper Mar 16, 2027, 5 PM Pacific (OpenReview; submissions open Mar 1)
candidates.why_fit: Computational imaging, neural and differentiable rendering, and physics-informed ML sit squarely within the vision family (CVPR, ICCV, 3DV).
candidates.concerns: Very small. Page charges apply beyond 12 pages, and papers over 18 pages go only to the proceedings track.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE CS TCPAMI-affiliated, held annually since 2009 at major universities (Princeton 2026, Toronto 2025, EPFL 2024). Double-blind review with rebuttal and a TPAMI special issue.

candidates.full_name: European Conference on Visual Perception
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-standing and well regarded, and it matches the abstract-meeting style. Its centre of gravity is psychophysics and perception science, adjacent to the catalog's computational-neuroscience core.
candidates.subtopics: visual perception, psychophysics, vision neuroscience
candidates.organizer: The ECVP community (continuity committee contact ccc@ecvp.eu) with rotating local organisers. Venues are voted at the business meeting two years ahead.
candidates.publication: Abstracts appear in Perception (SAGE) abstract supplements and collections; the ecvp.eu index runs through 2024.
candidates.size: The 2026 programme lists about 620 items (talks, posters, symposia, keynotes). No attendance figure is published.
candidates.rankings: None found (abstract meeting). Perception (journal) GS h5 23.
candidates.next_meeting: Padova, Italy, Aug 29-Sep 2, 2027. The scout's '2028 Paris' does not appear on ecvp.eu.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract: symposium proposals around Dec 2026-Jan 2027 and individual talk/poster abstracts around spring 2027 (by analogy with 2026, when symposia ran Dec 18-Jan 25).
candidates.why_fit: European vision-science meeting (counterpart to VSS) that overlaps with the vision neuroscience in CCN, CogSci, Bernstein and COSYNE. Same abstract-based format as the tracked neuroscience meetings.
candidates.concerns: Psychophysics-centred rather than computational. Light abstract screening, and registration is required before submitting (one first-author abstract each). ecvp.org had an expired certificate; ecvp.eu works.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Nearly 50 years of continuous meetings at European universities. Abstracts are published by SAGE (Perception), and named lectures (Perception Lecture, Rank Prize Lecture) are given by leading vision scientists.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on MultiMedia Modeling
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, with a credible steering committee and a long history, but mid-to-lower tier (CCF C, GS h5 26). It overlaps the tracked ICMR and ACM MM.
candidates.subtopics: multimedia analysis and retrieval, multimodal models, interactive video search
candidates.organizer: MMM steering committee (chair Phoebe Chen, co-chair Cathal Gurrin; members include Tat-Seng Chua, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Benoit Huet)
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (LNCS format required; the 2027 call references Springer policies)
candidates.size: Unknown for 2027 (programme TBA)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B (scout's figure; not re-verified). CCF C (ccf.atom.im mirror). GS h5 26, median 39 (Multimedia #18).
candidates.next_meeting: MMM 2027: Siem Reap, Cambodia, Jan 5-8, 2027. MMM 2028 has not been announced.
candidates.next_deadline: MMM 2028 full paper around mid-to-late August 2027 (2027 cycle: Aug 16, extended to Aug 30, 2026).
candidates.why_fit: Multimedia analysis and retrieval with multimodal models. It hosts the Video Browser Showdown and sits next to the tracked ICMR and ACM MM.
candidates.concerns: Lower tier than the venues already tracked in this area. The 2027 call has closed and the 2028 host is unknown.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-running series with a stable international steering committee, double-blind review and Springer LNCS proceedings.

candidates.full_name: International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, society-run and the leading venue in its field (GS h5 42). Music and audio is adjacent to the catalog's signals coverage (ICASSP, Interspeech) rather than central to it.
candidates.subtopics: music/audio ML, music information retrieval
candidates.organizer: International Society for Music Information Retrieval (non-profit; members vote at the annual business meeting)
candidates.publication: Society-published ISMIR proceedings, with the open-access TISMIR journal alongside
candidates.size: 2026: about 140 accepted papers (accepted-papers page)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 none found (scout; not re-verified). CCF not listed. GS h5 42, median 70 (Multimedia #12).
candidates.next_meeting: London, UK, Sep 12-16, 2027 (venue TBA)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (with abstract registration a week earlier) around March-April 2027. The 2026 cycle used Apr 20 for abstracts and Apr 27 for full papers; the 2027 call is still TBA.
candidates.why_fit: Audio and music ML, representation learning and multimedia retrieval overlap with the signals and retrieval families.
candidates.concerns: Domain-specific (music), and not ranked by CORE or CCF. The 2027 edition is two months earlier than 2026, so its deadline may also come earlier.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A dedicated scholarly society with its own journal (TISMIR), double-blind review with at least three reviewers plus a meta-review, and 25+ years of history.

candidates.full_name: Eurographics Conference on Visualization
candidates.verdict_reason: This is the strongest candidate in the batch. It is clearly legitimate and selective, with a confirmed deadline, but visualization sits next to the catalog's ML, neuroscience and dynamics core rather than inside it. It would fill the existing 'Computer Graphics & Visualization' leaf, which only SIGGRAPH covers today.
candidates.subtopics: visualization, visual analytics, state-of-the-art reports
candidates.organizer: Eurographics Association. Historically a joint Eurographics/IEEE VGTC symposium; ICORE still lists it as 'Eurographics/IEEE Symposium on Visualization'. The 2027 hosts are the University of Stuttgart (VISUS) and HFT Stuttgart.
candidates.publication: Full papers appear in a special issue of Computer Graphics Forum (Wiley/EG) and in the EG Digital Library.
candidates.size: 2026: 52 full papers accepted from 195 reviewed submissions (CGF frontmatter, via ccfddl). Attendance unknown.
candidates.acceptance_rate: About 27% for full papers (52/195 in 2026; 46/167 in 2025)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: B. CCF 2026: B. Google Scholar: no venue-level h5, because papers appear in Computer Graphics Forum (h5 64 for the whole journal).
candidates.founded: Full-paper proceedings in CGF since 2008. Its predecessor, the EG/IEEE VisSym symposium, ran from 1999.
candidates.next_meeting: EuroVis 2027: Stuttgart, Germany, May 31 to Jun 4, 2027 per the official site. The EG calendar says May 31 to Jun 6, probably counting co-located events.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: Dec 2, 2026 AoE, with a mandatory abstract by Nov 23, 2026. STARs: Dec 7, 2026.
candidates.why_fit: European flagship of the visualization and visual-analytics community. It matches the catalog's graphics/visualization leaf and its archival-paper style, and is comparable in standing to the tracked specialist venues.
candidates.concerns: The scope is adjacent (data visualization and HCI-leaning), not ML, vision or neuroscience. The deadline is only about a month away, and IEEE VIS, the field's larger flagship, is not tracked either.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Eurographics society conference with two-stage journal-style review and CGF publication. ICORE B and CCF B. No red flags found.

candidates.full_name: Pacific Conference on Computer Graphics and Applications (Pacific Graphics)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and long-running Asia-Pacific graphics flagship with CCF B. Graphics is only an adjacent fit, and the 2027 edition has not been announced, so a 2027 entry would rest entirely on estimates.
candidates.subtopics: computer graphics, rendering, geometry, animation, neural 3D
candidates.organizer: PG organisers supported by Asia Graphics and the Eurographics Association (an EG 'in cooperation' event). Rotating chairs; 2026 was hosted by SMU Singapore with chairs including Niloy Mitra and Holly Rushmeier.
candidates.publication: Journal track in a special issue of Computer Graphics Forum, plus a conference track in the EG Digital Library. Both tracks share one double-blind review.
candidates.size: 2025: 97 full papers (journal and conference tracks) accepted from 257 submissions (EG frontmatter, via ccfddl).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: 'Journal Published' (not ranked as a conference). CCF 2026: B. Google Scholar: papers appear in Computer Graphics Forum (no venue h5).
candidates.next_meeting: PG 2027: unknown, not announced. PG 2026 took place Oct 6-9, 2026 at SMU Singapore per the official site; the EG calendar's Oct 20-23 is wrong.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: estimated early June 2027, with the abstract about a week earlier. The 2026 dates were an abstract on Jun 1 and a full paper on Jun 8.
candidates.why_fit: Main regional graphics venue alongside the tracked ACM SIGGRAPH. Increasingly covers neural rendering and 3D learning, which overlaps with 3DV-style vision.
candidates.concerns: Graphics is outside the catalog's core. It has a two-track, partly journal-published model and no 2027 host or dates yet. Official sources disagreed on the 2026 dates, a minor data-quality caution.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 33-year history, Eurographics cooperation, CGF journal track, credible international chairs. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: Scandinavian Conference on Image Analysis
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-standing Nordic IAPR-society vision conference with Springer LNCS proceedings and strong 2027 keynotes. Its scope is central, but it is small and has no ICORE or CCF rank, about the tier of the tracked ACPR and S+SSPR.
candidates.subtopics: image analysis, computer vision, medical imaging, pattern recognition
candidates.organizer: Rotating among the Nordic IAPR member societies. 2027 is organised by NOBIM (the Norwegian image processing and ML society) with NTNU Colourlab in Gjøvik; general chair is S. A. Amirshahi.
candidates.publication: Full papers in Springer LNCS ('Image Analysis' volumes). An abstract-only route also exists, but those abstracts are not in the proceedings.
candidates.size: LNCS papers per edition: 61 in 2025 (Reykjavik, 2 volumes), 69 in 2023, 41 in 2019, 87 in 2017.
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE 2026, CORE 2023/2021/2018 or CCF 2026. Google Scholar h5 not found.
candidates.founded: Springer LNCS editions date from at least 2003; the often-cited 1980 founding is unverified.
candidates.next_meeting: SCIA 2027: Gjøvik, Norway (NTNU), Jun 8-11, 2027, with tutorials and workshops on Jun 8.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (LNCS, 12 pages, double-blind): Jan 26, 2027; the submission window opens Dec 1, 2026. Abstract-only (non-archival): Feb 28, 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Core image analysis and computer vision with ML, medical imaging and foundation-model topics. A respected regional IAPR meeting, comparable to GCPR, ACPR or S+SSPR.
candidates.concerns: Small regional meeting with no formal rank. The official site does not list a programme or steering committee. Edition numbering and founding year (often cited as 1980) were not verified on an official page.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by national IAPR member societies (NOBIM in 2027), Springer LNCS, double-blind review, keynotes Efros, Süsstrunk and Feragen. No predatory signs.

candidates.full_name: SIAM Conference on Imaging Science
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably legitimate society meeting in the same minisymposium and abstract style as the tracked SIAM DS. However, IS26 opens in about two weeks with its submission window closed, IS28 is unannounced, and the official SIAM page is blocked (403), so for now only the meeting dates can be added.
candidates.subtopics: mathematical imaging, inverse problems, computational imaging, imaging ML
candidates.organizer: SIAM, through the SIAM Activity Group on Imaging Science (SIAG/IS)
candidates.publication: none (abstract-based meeting with minisymposia, contributed talks and posters; no proceedings)
candidates.size: IS26: 61 numbered minisymposium slots (some multi-part), 5 plenaries, 2 minitutorials, 3 contributed sessions and a poster session (official program). Attendance unknown.
candidates.rankings: None found: abstract meeting, not in ICORE 2026 or CCF 2026.
candidates.next_meeting: IS26: Nov 15-19, 2026 per the official SIAM program. The program page names no city; aggregators say Salt Lake City, and its room names fit a convention centre.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. The IS26 minisymposium and contributed-abstract deadlines have passed, and IS28 (2028) is not announced.
candidates.why_fit: Mathematical imaging, inverse problems, optimization and imaging ML. It is the mathematical counterpart of the tracked vision venues and shares the SIAM society and style of SIAM DS.
candidates.concerns: The official siam.org pages returned HTTP 403, so the city and the IS26 call were unverified. The web-search budget ran out during this review, so the facts come from direct fetches. Scope leans applied mathematics, and there is no open submission route until IS28.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Official SIAM society meeting. IS26 plenaries include Stefano Soatto (UCLA), Felix Herrmann (Georgia Tech), Audrey Repetti (Heriot-Watt), Fred Roosta (UQ) and Xiaoqun Zhang (SJTU).

candidates.full_name: Eurographics Symposium on Geometry Processing
candidates.verdict_reason: Premier, highly selective specialist venue, ranked B by both ICORE and CCF. It is very small (about 24 papers in 2026) and narrowly focused on geometry processing, so it is only peripherally related to the catalog. Lowest priority of the graphics trio.
candidates.subtopics: geometry processing, 3D shape analysis, meshing, geometric learning
candidates.organizer: Eurographics Association (historically co-sponsored with ACM SIGGRAPH). In 2027 it is part of the 4th International Geometry Summit (IGS) with SMI, SPM, GMP and SIAM GD.
candidates.publication: Regular electronic issue of Computer Graphics Forum, after two-stage journal review.
candidates.size: 2026 (Bern): about 24 technical papers in 7 sessions, plus posters and 3 keynotes.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: B. CCF 2026: B. Google Scholar: papers appear in Computer Graphics Forum (no venue h5).
candidates.next_meeting: SGP 2027: Singapore, Suntec Convention Centre, within the IGS 2027 week of Jun 21-25, 2027. SGP's own days are not yet published.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: estimated as two rounds around early Feb and mid-Apr 2027. The 2026 rounds were Feb 4 and Apr 15, with recommended abstracts 2 days earlier.
candidates.why_fit: 3D shape analysis and geometric learning overlap with the tracked 3DV and SIGGRAPH.
candidates.concerns: Narrow scope and tiny size. geometryprocessing.org failed with a TLS error, and SGP 2027 has no call or website yet; only the IGS umbrella site is live. The co-location with IGS may change its usual schedule.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Eurographics symposium with CGF publication, ICORE B and CCF B, and an unbroken annual history since 2003. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Image Analysis and Processing
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and established (24th edition), run by the Italian IAPR society with a well-known steering committee, OpenReview double-blind review and Springer LNCS. Its scope is central vision, but ICORE rates it only nationally (Italy), so it is a regional-tier option.
candidates.subtopics: image analysis, computer vision, video understanding, vision-language, medical imaging
candidates.organizer: CVPL (Italian IAPR member society) with AImageLab, University of Modena and Reggio Emilia. The steering committee includes Cucchiara, Del Bimbo, Sebe, Roli and Murino.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (main conference, typically 2 volumes) plus separate LNCS workshop volumes.
candidates.size: Main-conference LNCS papers: 103 in 2025 (Rome), 92 in 2023 (Udine), 170 in 2022 (Lecce); workshop volumes are additional.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: National: Italy (it was B in ERA2010). Not in CCF 2026. Google Scholar h5 not found.
candidates.cadence: biennial, odd years (an extra 2022 edition after COVID)
candidates.founded: 1980s (24th edition in 2027); Springer LNCS since at least 1997
candidates.next_meeting: ICIAP 2027: Modena, Italy, Sep 13-17, 2027. Workshops and tutorials Sep 13-14; main conference Sep 15-17.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (LNCS, 12 pages, OpenReview), round 1: Feb 11, 2027 AoE. Round 2: Apr 15, 2027 AoE.
candidates.why_fit: Broad image analysis, vision, video, vision-language, 3D and medical imaging tracks. It is the Italian counterpart of the regional IAPR venues the catalog already tracks (ACPR, S+SSPR).
candidates.concerns: National-level rank. The candidate reports a WASET look-alike, 'ICIAP Boston 2027', on conferenceindex.org; this review did not re-check that listing. Only the unimore.it site is genuine.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by an IAPR national society with a steering committee of senior Italian vision researchers, OpenReview double-blind review, a reviewer-service requirement and Springer LNCS.

candidates.full_name: Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-running society conference and Latin America's main graphics/vision venue. It is regional and has no ICORE or CCF rank, so it is a lower-tier, regional-coverage addition.
candidates.subtopics: computer vision, image processing, pattern recognition, computer graphics, visualization
candidates.organizer: Brazilian Computer Society (SBC) special interest group CEGRAPI; the 2026 local host was Universidade Federal de Goiás.
candidates.publication: Main-track proceedings in IEEE Xplore (stated on the 2026 site). Separate tracks feed a Computers & Graphics special section and IEEE GRSL.
candidates.size: Paper counts not published on the site. The 2026 edition was co-located with SVR, SBGames and ICAT-EGVE.
candidates.rankings: GS h5 22 (#13 in Computer Graphics). ICORE2026: none found (portal returned 403, so this comes from the discovery pass and was not re-checked). CCF 2026: none found (PDF text not extractable).
candidates.next_meeting: 40th edition, 2027: city and dates not announced. Estimated late Sep/early Oct 2027, Brazil.
candidates.next_deadline: Main-track full paper, about mid-June 2027 (estimated; the 2026 hard deadline was Jun 17, 2026).
candidates.why_fit: Covers vision, image processing, pattern recognition and graphics, so it overlaps the Vision & Multimedia family. It adds Latin American coverage, as Dynamics Days LAC does.
candidates.concerns: Regional, with mostly Brazilian authors. Graphics and games make up a large share. The 2026 edition is already over, so nothing is actionable until about mid-2027.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by SBC, the national computing society, with 39 consecutive editions. Double review with a rebuttal round, IEEE Xplore proceedings, and journal tracks with Elsevier C&G and IEEE GRSL.

candidates.full_name: Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate national flagship run by India's IAPR member society, with double-blind OpenReview review. Low citation impact (GS h5 10) and no ICORE/CCF rank make it a low-tier, regional addition.
candidates.subtopics: computer vision, graphics, image processing
candidates.organizer: IUPRAI (Indian IAPR affiliate). The 2026 edition is hosted by ISI Kolkata with TCG CREST.
candidates.publication: ACM International Conference Proceedings Series (ICPS). An open-access APC may apply; organisers are seeking a waiver.
candidates.size: Accepted-paper and submission counts not published on the 2025 or 2026 sites.
candidates.rankings: GS h5 10. ICORE2026: none found (discovery pass; portal returned 403, not re-checked). CCF 2026: none found.
candidates.next_meeting: ICVGIP 2026, Kolkata, Dec 21–24, 2026 (workshops Dec 21).
candidates.next_deadline: 2026 papers closed Aug 21, 2026. ICVGIP 2027 full paper (8 pages) about Aug 2027 (estimated).
candidates.why_fit: A core computer vision, image processing and graphics venue, comparable in role to ACPR or S+SSPR in the catalog.
candidates.concerns: Regional, with mostly Indian authorship. Low h5 and no acceptance statistics. Possible ACM APC for authors.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IAPR-affiliate society, hosted by IITs and ISI, double-blind review on OpenReview with a rebuttal. Credible keynotes in 2025 (Paul Thompson, Nicu Sebe, C. V. Jawahar, P. Anandan).

candidates.full_name: Conference on Robots and Vision (formerly Computer and Robot Vision / Vision Interface)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-running national meeting of Canada's IAPR member society. It is small, single-blind, without ICORE/CCF rank, and 2027 is unannounced, so it is a low-tier, low-priority addition.
candidates.subtopics: computer vision, robot vision, robotics perception
candidates.organizer: CIPPRS (a SIG of the Canadian Information Processing Society and Canada's IAPR member), co-located with Canadian AI.
candidates.publication: Open-access proceedings on PubPub (crv.pubpub.org, CC BY 4.0); no commercial publisher named.
candidates.size: Small. Counts not published; the 2026 PC listed 37 members.
candidates.rankings: GS h5 17 (as 'Canadian Conference on Computer and Robot Vision'). ICORE2026: none found (discovery pass; portal returned 403). CCF 2026: none found.
candidates.cadence: annual (Vision Interface 1983–2004, CRV since 2005; 23rd CRV-numbered edition in 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 not announced. Canadian AI 2027 (40th) has a placeholder page, so CRV is likely late May/June 2027 in Canada (estimated).
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4–8 pages), about mid-Feb 2027 (estimated; 2026 was Feb 13, 2026).
candidates.why_fit: Computer vision plus robot vision overlaps the Vision and Robotics families. It is Canada's national vision meeting.
candidates.concerns: Small regional meeting with single-blind review and no acceptance statistics. Proceedings moved from IEEE to self-hosted PubPub. No 2027 details yet.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: National IAPR member society with an unbroken annual series since at least 2004 (archive lists every year). Hosts the CIPPRS John Barron Dissertation Award.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Machine Vision Applications
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate Japanese society-backed series with a confirmed upcoming deadline. Weak scientific signals: 4-page papers, 54% acceptance in 2025, mostly Japanese authors and only a national ranking. This is the weakest of the vision set.
candidates.subtopics: applied machine vision, sensing, recognition, industrial and robot vision
candidates.organizer: IEICE PRMU technical committee with the MVA Organization; sponsor IEICE-ISS; technical co-sponsor IPSJ-CVIM. It has IAPR invited talks, but IAPR sponsorship is not stated.
candidates.publication: IEICE Proceeding Series, submitted to IEEE Xplore (2025 is in Xplore). Optional concurrent route to IEICE Trans. Inf. & Syst. letters.
candidates.size: 2025: 122 submissions, 64 accepted (20 oral). 58% of submissions came from Japan.
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 'National: Japan' (discovery pass; portal returned 403, not re-checked). CCF 2026: none found. GS: no clear entry (an h5-11 'Conf. on Machine Vision and Applications' may be a different venue).
candidates.cadence: biennial in odd years since 2005 (20th edition in 2027; series since 1988, always in Japan)
candidates.next_meeting: MVA 2027, Fukuoka (Kyushu University), May 12–14, 2027.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4 pages excluding references) Jan 14, 2027, 23:59 JST. Confirmed on the official site.
candidates.why_fit: Applied machine vision, including sensing, recognition, foundation models/VLMs and robotics applications. It sits inside the Vision family but on the applied side.
candidates.concerns: High acceptance (53.8% in 2025) and short 4-page papers. National in reach. The discovery note 'now regular' is wrong: the series is strictly biennial.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Organised by the IEICE and IPSJ vision technical committees, with 19 editions since 1988 and IEEE Xplore proceedings. International chairs and invited speakers in 2025 (Ming-Yu Liu, Katerina Fragkiadaki, Yasuyuki Matsushita).

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Scale Space and Variational Methods in Computer Vision
candidates.verdict_reason: Small but clearly well-regarded venue for mathematical imaging and vision, with a near-term confirmed deadline. Its scope (variational, PDE and geometric methods) is adjacent to the catalog's ML-centred vision core rather than central to it.
candidates.subtopics: variational and PDE methods, scale space, mathematical imaging, geometric learning
candidates.organizer: SSVM community steering committee. Recent organisers include Carola Schönlieb and Tatiana Bubba (2025); 2027 is supported by NWO, ASML, 4TU.AMI, Springer and JMIV.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (2025 in two volumes; the 2027 call requires the LNCS format). Double-blind review of 12-page papers.
candidates.size: 2025 proceedings filled two LNCS volumes; exact paper and attendee counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: GS h5 12. ICORE2026: not verified (portal returned 403). CCF 2026: none found.
candidates.cadence: biennial in odd years (since 2007, succeeding Scale-Space from 1997 and VLSM; 10th edition in 2025)
candidates.next_meeting: SSVM 2027, Veldhoven, Netherlands, Jun 6–10, 2027.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (12 pages, LNCS, double-blind via CMT) Dec 20, 2026, 23:59 CET. Confirmed on the official site.
candidates.why_fit: Mathematical foundations of imaging and vision, now including learning in imaging, 3D vision and medical imaging. It is the kind of small, community-respected meeting the owner welcomes.
candidates.concerns: Niche mathematical audience. The input listed only dblp, but the official 2027 site now exists. ICORE rank could not be checked.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-standing academic series with Springer LNCS proceedings and double-blind review. Strong 2027 keynotes (Bronstein, Citti, Felsberg, Steidl) and support from JMIV and national funders.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier, clearly legitimate flagship (A*/CCF A, h5 52). Its scope is XR/HCI rather than ML or vision, similar to the already-deferred HCI venues (UIST, IUI, CSCW), so it fits the catalog weakly.
candidates.subtopics: VR/AR/XR, 3D user interfaces, perception, graphics
candidates.organizer: IEEE Computer Society and its Visualization and Graphics Technical Committee (VGTC).
candidates.publication: Papers go either to an IEEE TVCG special issue or to IEEE VR proceedings (IEEE Xplore). Posters are published as 2-page abstracts in IEEE Xplore.
candidates.size: Large flagship XR meeting; exact paper and attendance counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 A* and CCF 2026 A (discovery pass; ICORE portal returned 403 and the CCF PDF was not extractable, so not re-checked). GS h5 52 (#15 in HCI).
candidates.next_meeting: IEEE VR 2027, Melbourne, Australia, Feb 27–Mar 3, 2027.
candidates.next_deadline: Main papers closed Aug 31, 2026; VR 2028 papers about late Aug 2027 (estimated). Open now: 2-page poster extended abstract due Dec 7, 2026, with abstract registration Dec 2 (confirmed).
candidates.why_fit: Graphics, 3D interaction and perception overlap the Vision & Multimedia family, the way ACM SIGGRAPH does.
candidates.concerns: Core audience is XR/HCI, not ML or vision. Adding it would set a precedent for ISMAR, VRST and other HCI venues that the backlog deferred for focus.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE Computer Society/VGTC flagship with a TVCG journal track and a two-round review including revisions. Top ICORE/CCF ranks.

candidates.full_name: Reinforcement Learning Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: The only dedicated archival RL conference. Its advisory board includes Barto, Sutton-era leaders, Stone, Singh, Levine and Van Roy, and its papers are peer reviewed into its own journal. It is central to the family despite being young and unranked.
candidates.subtopics: Reinforcement learning: theory, algorithms, empirical RL, applications
candidates.organizer: RLC Organization Committee with an advisory committee (Barto, Stone, Singh, Brunskill, Littman, Levine, Bowling, Van Roy and others) and a board (Niekum, A. Zhang, M. White, A. White, Berseth, Vinitsky).
candidates.publication: Reinforcement Learning Journal (RLJ), peer-reviewed, ISSN 2996-8577 online. Double-blind OpenReview review with area chairs.
candidates.size: About 148 papers in RLJ 2026, counted from the official RLC 2026 paper schedule. Attendance unknown.
candidates.acceptance_rate: About 39% in 2025 (115/295), from a secondary report only. Not on official pages.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed (checked against the ICORE2026 export). CCF: none found. GS Metrics: none found (too new).
candidates.next_meeting: RLC 2027 at two sites: Brown University, USA (early August) and Odense, Denmark (late August, run as one event with EWRL). Exact dates TBA. The organisers say the split is one-time; 2028 will be at a single site outside North America.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract plus full paper, about early March 2027 (2026 cycle: abstract Mar 1, paper Mar 5 AoE).
candidates.why_fit: The field's own flagship, the RL-only counterpart to the tracked NeurIPS, ICML and CoRL. It matches the catalog's archival-paper style.
candidates.concerns: Only 3 editions (2024-2026). Not yet ranked anywhere. The two-site 2027 edition and the joint Odense event with EWRL complicate edition modelling. The ~39% (115/295) 2025 acceptance rate is a secondary figure, not re-verified.

candidates.full_name: Multi-disciplinary Conference on Reinforcement Learning and Decision Making
candidates.verdict_reason: Highly regarded interdisciplinary meeting, steered by founders of computational RL and decision neuroscience. It fits the catalog's COSYNE/CCN-style abstract meetings and bridges two families.
candidates.subtopics: RL and decision making in humans, animals and machines; computational psychiatry; neuroeconomics
candidates.organizer: RLDM Executive Committee (2025 listing: Peter Dayan, Cate Hartley, Yael Niv, Satinder Singh, Peter Stone, Richard Sutton). 2027: General Chair Anne Collins; Program Chairs David Abel and Matt Nassar.
candidates.publication: None. Self-described as non-archival. Abstract booklet of ≤2,000-character summaries; optional 1-4 page extended abstracts posted only with author permission.
candidates.size: Unknown; official pages give no counts. Single-track talks plus posters, workshops and tutorials.
candidates.rankings: none found (non-archival; not in ICORE 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: 7th RLDM, July 6-9, 2027, Maison de la Chimie, Paris, France
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract (summary plus 1-4 page extended abstract), probably Jan-Feb 2027. The 2022 deadline was Feb 15. The 2027 call has not been posted yet.
candidates.why_fit: Shares the computational-neuroscience/RL community of COSYNE, CCN and Bernstein. Covers RL and decision making in brains and machines.
candidates.concerns: Non-archival. Irregular cadence, so editions are hard to anticipate. The 2027 call for abstracts and its deadline are not yet published, and the organizers page still shows the 2019 committee.

candidates.full_name: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: Society-run robotics flagship ranked ICORE A, with GS h5 92. It is the natural sibling of the tracked ICRA.
candidates.subtopics: Robotics, robot learning, perception, manipulation, locomotion, planning and control
candidates.organizer: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society with the Robotics Society of Japan, SICE, IEEE IES and NTF. 2027 is hosted under the auspices of the University of Florence.
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings, archival, up to 8 pages. The RA-L+IROS option was dropped in 2026.
candidates.size: Several thousand attendees and well over a thousand papers per year (approximate). The 2026 site's '1200+' figures look like placeholders.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: A (verified in the ICORE2026 export). CCF 2026: C (reported; not re-verified here). GS Metrics Robotics: h5 92, #7.
candidates.next_meeting: IROS 2027 (40th), Sep 27-Oct 1, 2027, Fortezza da Basso, Florence, Italy
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper, about early March 2027 (IROS 2026 was Mar 2, 2026, with edits allowed until Mar 5). Not yet on the 2027 site.
candidates.why_fit: Main robotics venue next to ICRA, with large robot-learning, RL and control tracks.
candidates.concerns: Very large and broad, with much mechanism and hardware work outside ML. Moderate selectivity, with no official rate found. The 2027 site has no CFP yet.

candidates.full_name: IFAC World Congress
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably legitimate as the flagship of IFAC, the international control federation. However, it meets only every three years, the next real deadline is around late 2028, and its scope is very broad. It is low-value for the calendar until then.
candidates.subtopics: All of automatic control: nonlinear, optimal and learning-based control, robotics, system identification
candidates.organizer: International Federation of Automatic Control (IFAC)
candidates.publication: IFAC-PapersOnLine (Elsevier, open access), with a journal-option route into IFAC journals.
candidates.size: 3,000-4,000 participants per edition (IFAC's own figure). Paper counts not published on the pages checked.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed. CCF: none found. GS Metrics: IFAC-PapersOnLine not listed; none found.
candidates.next_meeting: 24th IFAC World Congress, Amsterdam, 2029 (dates not published; ifac2029.org was unreachable). The 25th is in Honolulu in 2032. The 23rd was in Busan, Aug 23-28, 2026, and is past.
candidates.next_deadline: Regular/survey/demo full papers, about late Nov to early Dec 2028. The 2026 cycle used Dec 5, 2025, with the journal option on Nov 2, 2025.
candidates.why_fit: Top international control meeting, sibling to the tracked CDC, ACC, ECC and IFAC SYSID. Includes learning-based control and system identification.
candidates.concerns: Broad all-of-automatic-control scope, including process, automotive and social systems. Very large. Nothing actionable until about 2028.

candidates.full_name: European Workshop on Reinforcement Learning
candidates.verdict_reason: Long-running and respected European RL meeting. In 2027, however, it runs as one event with RLC's Odense site, so it would duplicate RLC for that edition, and its standalone identity after 2027 is unclear.
candidates.subtopics: Reinforcement learning theory, bandits, RL algorithms and applications
candidates.organizer: EWRL, now a European non-profit association, with rotating local organising teams (2026: Inria Scool / Univ. Lille, incl. E. Kaufmann and O.-A. Maillard).
candidates.publication: None for 2026 ('no proceedings'). Regular track: 9-page papers, double-blind review, may be under review elsewhere. Fast track for papers already accepted at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, RLC or AAAI. Historic proceedings: LNAI 2011, JMLR 2012.
candidates.size: About 140 posters in 2026 (poster numbers run to 142).
candidates.rankings: none found (non-archival; not in ICORE 2026)
candidates.cadence: annual since 2022; irregular before that (19 editions since 1994)
candidates.next_meeting: EWRL 2027, joint with RLC in Odense, Denmark, late August 2027 per the RLC site. EWRL's own page says 2027 organisers are still being sought.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown for 2027. As a joint event it may follow RLC's early-March deadline. The 2026 regular-track deadline was May 29 (AoE).
candidates.why_fit: Standalone RL meeting in the AALTD/ML4H workshop style, with a strong European RL theory and bandits community.
candidates.concerns: Non-archival. The 2027 edition merges with RLC and the 2028 plan is unknown, so tracking both series risks double-counting. The fast track re-presents papers from other venues.

candidates.full_name: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier and legitimate (ICORE A*), but centred on HRI, social robotics and user studies rather than RL or control. It is only a partial scope fit, bridging robotics and the CHI/human-AI side.
candidates.subtopics: Human-robot interaction, social robotics, human-AI interaction
candidates.organizer: Joint ACM/IEEE conference with a steering committee. 2027 GCs: Dylan Glas (Amazon) and Henny Admoni (CMU). PCs: Robinette, Tanaka, Rossi.
candidates.publication: Archival proceedings in the ACM Digital Library and IEEE Xplore. ACM open-access format; non-ACM-Open authors pay an APC ($500-750).
candidates.size: unknown (no official counts found)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: A* (verified in the ICORE2026 export). CCF: not verified. GS Metrics Robotics: h5 52, #19.
candidates.next_meeting: HRI 2027 (22nd), Mar 8-12, 2027, Santa Clara, CA, USA
candidates.next_deadline: The HRI 2027 full-paper deadlines have passed (abstract Sep 11, paper Sep 18, 2026). Late-breaking reports close Dec 8, 2026 (confirmed). The next main deadline is an HRI 2028 abstract plus full paper around mid-September 2027 (estimated).
candidates.why_fit: Main venue where robotics meets human-AI interaction, a subtopic of the responsible-ai family. Complements the tracked CHI and ICRA.
candidates.concerns: HCI/social-robotics focus with little RL or control content. Officially 'highly selective', but no rate was verified. The next actionable full-paper deadline is about 11 months away.

candidates.full_name: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical and Autonomous Systems (merged HSCC + ICCPS)
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and long-running, with a strong PC. Its centre of gravity is hybrid-systems verification and CPS rather than learning or control, and the series changes identity in 2027.
candidates.subtopics: Hybrid systems, CPS verification and control, safe learning-enabled autonomy
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGBED (ACM proceedings), within CPS-IoT Week (ACM, IEEE, IEEE CS). 2027 PC chairs: T. T. Johnson, J. Sprinkle and M. Kochenderfer. Working group: Abate, I. Lee, Pajic, Mitra, Sankaranarayanan.
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings (Regular 10 pp, Short 6 pp, Tool papers), with optional artifact evaluation
candidates.size: unknown: no submission or acceptance counts on the official site
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: B for HSCC (Theory, p.42). ICORE 2026: neither HSCC nor ICCPS is listed. GS h5: not checked.
candidates.next_meeting: May 17-20, 2027, Boulder, Colorado, USA (CPS-IoT Week 2027)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper Nov 5, 2026 AoE. Abstract registration closed Oct 29, 2026.
candidates.why_fit: Its AI-enabled Autonomy and Foundations tracks cover safe learning-enabled control, so it sits next to the tracked L4DC and CDC.
candidates.concerns: Identity changes in 2027: the two series merge under a new name, edition 30 continuing HSCC's count. It leans heavily toward formal methods and embedded CPS. No general chairs or steering committee are posted yet, and the 2027 paper deadline is only days away.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 30th HSCC and 18th ICCPS. Part of CPS-IoT Week with SenSys and RTAS. ACM/SIGBED proceedings. Double-anonymous review.

candidates.full_name: Conference on Lifelong Learning Agents
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and credibly organised: PMLR proceedings and Mila/DeepMind-led chairs. It is young, small and unranked, and its scope is continual-learning ML more than RL or control.
candidates.subtopics: Continual/lifelong learning, meta-learning, continual RL, model editing/unlearning
candidates.organizer: CoLLAs organizing committee and board. 2026 general chairs include S. Chandar and R. Pascanu; PCs M. Mundt and E. Triantafillou.
candidates.publication: PMLR for the archival main track (vols 199, 232, 274, 330), plus a non-archival workshop/sister-venue track
candidates.size: 37 papers in PMLR v330 (2025, UPenn). 2026 count unknown.
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE 2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: unknown: 2027 not announced. 2026 was Bucharest, Sep 14-18.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract about Apr 10 and full paper about Apr 15, 2027, inferred from 2026 (Apr 12 / Apr 16, 11:59 UTC, on OpenReview)
candidates.why_fit: Main standalone venue for continual and lifelong learning, including continual RL and adaptation.
candidates.concerns: Founded in 2022 with a small output (~30-40 papers per year). Acceptance rate unknown: OpenReview stats were behind a bot challenge. The site renders only with JavaScript. The scope has drifted toward LLM adaptation and unlearning.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: PMLR proceedings every year. Double-blind OpenReview. Chairs from Mila, Google DeepMind, Bremen and Tübingen.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Development and Learning
candidates.verdict_reason: The established IEEE (CIS + RAS) venue of the developmental-robotics community. Its credible chairs and keynotes, and its embodied-learning, neuro and cognition scope, sit naturally beside the tracked SAB, ALIFE and CogSci.
candidates.subtopics: Developmental robotics, intrinsic motivation, embodied cognition, open-ended learning
candidates.organizer: IEEE, IEEE Computational Intelligence Society and IEEE Robotics & Automation Society. 2026 chairs: T. Taniguchi, Y. Nagai and S. Murata.
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore for 6-page full papers. Late-breaking results and journal presentations are not archived.
candidates.size: 2026: about 146 presentations (25 orals plus about 121 posters across full papers, late-breaking results and journal presentations), 5 keynotes
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE 2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: Sep 21-24, 2027, Campinas, Brazil
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper about mid-March 2027, inferred from 2026 (Mar 13, extended to Apr 3). The 2027 CFP is not yet posted.
candidates.why_fit: Embodied and developmental learning, intrinsic motivation and open-ended learning link robotics/RL with cognitive and neuroscience work.
candidates.concerns: Unranked, with no published acceptance rate. Series history (since 2000; ICDL-EpiRob 2011-2020) comes from background knowledge, not an official page. Beware unrelated 'ICDL' acronym listings on event-aggregator sites.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Sponsored by IEEE CIS and RAS. Single-blind OpenReview review. 2026 keynotes: Kamitani, Martius, Verbelen and others.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Conference on Control Technology and Applications
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate IEEE CSS-sponsored conference and a sibling of the tracked CDC and ACC. It is applications-oriented and lower profile, with no ranking or selectivity data.
candidates.subtopics: Applied control, learning-based control, robotics, energy/process control
candidates.organizer: IEEE Control Systems Society (flagship sponsor). 2027 co-sponsors: SICE, JAAC and the IEEE Robot Control TC.
candidates.publication: IEEE conference papers (6 pages final, up to 8 at submission). Xplore indexing is not stated on the 2027 page.
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE 2026 or CCF 2026). Below the GS top-20 cut-off (h5 47) in Automation & Control Theory.
candidates.next_meeting: Aug 23-25, 2027, Hiroshima, Japan (workshops Aug 22)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper Feb 7, 2027. Late-breaking posters due Jun 30, 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Third IEEE CSS conference, covering applied and learning-based control and robotics. It completes the CDC/ACC set.
candidates.concerns: Applications focus and weaker prestige than CDC/ACC. No acceptance statistics. The submission site opens only after CCTA 2026.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE CSS sponsorship. Invited sessions, tutorials and journal-based oral track (IEEE TCST).
