candidates.full_name: International Symposium on Mathematical Theory of Networks and Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: A 50-year-old flagship of mathematical systems theory with an eminent steering committee and IFAC-PapersOnLine proceedings. Small but highly regarded, and central to the dynamics-and-control family.
candidates.subtopics: Mathematical systems and control theory, networked systems, operator theory, optimization
candidates.organizer: MTNS Steering Committee (38 members, incl. Krstic, Parrilo, Rantzer, Sepulchre, Georgiou, van der Schaft), with IFAC and the Fields Institute. Hosts rotate.
candidates.publication: IFAC-PapersOnLine for full papers (6 pp). Extended abstracts (≤4 pp) are posted on the conference site.
candidates.size: 2026: 4 plenary and 8 semi-plenary talks, up to 4 parallel sessions. Attendance not published.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: C. CCF 2026: none. GS: not in top 20 for Automation & Control Theory.
candidates.next_meeting: unknown: 2028 host not announced. 2026 was Waterloo, Aug 17-21.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper about early Feb 2028 (extended abstract about a week later), inferred from 2026 (Feb 9 / Feb 16)
candidates.why_fit: Mathematical control, systems and network theory, at the same level and community as SIAM DS, CDC and ECC.
candidates.concerns: Small and mathematically oriented, with a weaker link to learning/RL. Mixed archival and non-archival formats. The 2028 edition is not yet announced.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Uninterrupted biennial series since 1973 (2020 cancelled). Large international steering committee. IFAC involvement and IFAC-PapersOnLine.

candidates.full_name: International Symposium on Combinatorial Search
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and well regarded (ICORE B, elected council, AAAI Digital Library), but a niche heuristic-search venue. It is adjacent to the tracked ICAPS rather than central to RL or control.
candidates.subtopics: Heuristic search, path finding, MAPF, planning as search
candidates.organizer: SoCS Council (president D. Harabor; members include Dechter, Felner, Likhachev, Ruml, Jiaoyang Li). Volunteer association with bylaws.
candidates.publication: AAAI Digital Library (OJS) since 2010. Long and short technical/position papers plus 2-page extended abstracts.
candidates.size: 2026: 46 accepted (23 long, 8 short, 4 position, 11 extended abstracts)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: B. CCF 2026: none. GS: not checked.
candidates.next_meeting: unknown: 2027 not announced. 2026 was Bremerhaven, Aug 14-16, before IJCAI-ECAI.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract about mid-March 2027, paper a week later, inferred from 2026 (Mar 16 / Mar 23 AoE, after extension)
candidates.why_fit: Heuristic search, path finding and multi-agent path finding, which complements ICAPS (tagged rl-control) for planning and search.
candidates.concerns: Small and specialist. Extended abstracts (including previously published work) are mixed into the proceedings. Weak link to learning and control.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Usually co-located with ICAPS/IJCAI/CP. Double-blind review. Proceedings free in the AAAI Digital Library. Elected council.

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Society for the Neural Control of Movement
candidates.verdict_reason: The motor-control community's own society meeting, running since 1991 with 291–600 attendees per edition. It is clearly legitimate, its 2027 deadlines are confirmed, and its computational motor-control strand matches the catalog's COSYNE/Bernstein-style abstract meetings.
candidates.subtopics: Motor control, sensorimotor learning, internal models, cerebellum, computational motor neuroscience, neurorehabilitation
candidates.organizer: Society for the Neural Control of Movement, a membership society with a board, career awards and scholarships
candidates.publication: None. Abstracts are not archival; team-session abstracts appear in the programme. The 2026 satellite led to an IEEE TNSRE special issue.
candidates.size: Attendance: 600 (Kobe 2026), 291 (Panama 2025), 520 (Dubrovnik 2024), 383 (Victoria 2023).
candidates.rankings: None found; rankings don't apply to an abstract meeting.
candidates.next_meeting: 36th Annual Meeting: Apr 27–30, 2027, Meliá Sevilla Hotel, Sevilla, Spain. Satellite on cerebellar computation: Apr 26, 2027.
candidates.next_deadline: Dec 1, 2026 for oral abstracts (individual and team); Feb 22, 2027 for poster abstracts. Both close at midnight PST.
candidates.why_fit: An abstract-based meeting where optimal feedback control, internal models and motor learning meet neurophysiology. The 2027 satellite is explicitly computational: cerebellar internal models and learning.
candidates.concerns: Mostly experimental and clinical motor neuroscience, and not archival. Submitters must be NCM members, with at most one oral per member per year. The rl-control tag is secondary to neuroscience.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A long-standing scientific society with membership, an elected board and career awards. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: SIAM Conference on Control and Its Applications
candidates.verdict_reason: An unquestionably legitimate SIAM biennial and a natural sibling of the tracked SIAM DS. However, the CT27 dates, city and deadlines could not be verified because siam.org returns 403, and the series has no ranking or h5 data.
candidates.subtopics: Mathematical, optimal and PDE control; data-driven control; differential games
candidates.organizer: SIAM, Activity Group on Control and Systems Theory (SIAG/CST)
candidates.publication: Minisymposium and contributed talks. Past editions had SIAM-published refereed proceedings volumes; not re-verified this run.
candidates.size: CT25: about 43 minisymposia, 7 contributed sessions, 3 minitutorials. CT23: about 41 minisymposia, 10 contributed sessions.
candidates.rankings: None found: no ICORE 2026 entry, absent from ccfddl/CCF, no Google Scholar h5 entry.
candidates.next_meeting: CT27 (2027) is registered in SIAM's meeting system, but its dates and location are unknown. CT25 ran Jul 27–30, 2025, alongside the SIAM/CAIMS AN25.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. SIAM usually sets minisymposium-proposal and contributed-abstract deadlines a few months before the meeting, so about early 2027 (estimate).
candidates.why_fit: Mathematical and data-driven control at the same society and level as the tracked SIAM DS and SDM. It bridges the catalog's control venues (ACC, CDC, ECC, L4DC) and its dynamics venues.
candidates.concerns: Mathematical control theory with modest ML/RL content. It may again be folded into a SIAM Annual Meeting. No official CT27 page could be read, so practical data are missing.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by SIAM through its SIAG/CST. The CT27 conference code exists in meetings.siam.org (CT29 returns nothing).

candidates.full_name: IFAC Symposium on Nonlinear Control Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate IFAC symposium and the main one on nonlinear control (13th edition in 2025, strong programme committee). But it is triennial and small, and the next edition is unannounced: nothing appears on IFAC's calendar through 2027.
candidates.subtopics: Nonlinear control and observers, geometric methods, stability, learning-based nonlinear control
candidates.organizer: IFAC TC 2.3 Non-Linear Control Systems (main sponsor), with 11 other IFAC TCs and the IEEE CSS TC on Nonlinear Systems & Control as co-sponsors
candidates.publication: IFAC-PapersOnLine (Elsevier, open access), the standard for IFAC symposia; not stated on the fetched 2025 page.
candidates.size: Unknown; paper counts are not published on the fetched pages. A small symposium.
candidates.rankings: None found: no ICORE 2026 or CCF entry, and no separate GS h5 because papers appear in IFAC-PapersOnLine.
candidates.founded: 1989 (inferred: 13th edition in 2025 at a triennial cadence)
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown. The 14th edition is expected around mid-2028 but is unannounced. NOLCOS 2025 was in Reykjavik, Jul 23–25, 2025.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. A mid-2028 meeting would have full papers due around late 2027 or early 2028 (estimate).
candidates.why_fit: Nonlinear dynamics and control theory, bridging the tracked NODYCON/NOLTA and the control flagships, with growing learning-based control content.
candidates.concerns: The audience is pure control theory. It adds no calendar entry until about 2028. The IFAC events ACNDC27, MICNON27 and NMPC27 overlap with it and are worth comparing.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IFAC TC sponsorship plus IEEE CSS co-sponsorship. The 2025 IPC chair was A. Teel and the NOC chair A. Astolfi.

candidates.full_name: IEEE-RAS International Conference on Humanoid Robots
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, long-running RAS conference (annual since 2000) with a 38.5% acceptance rate and GS h5 22. It is specialised, has no ICORE rank, and sits clearly below ICRA, IROS, RSS and CoRL.
candidates.subtopics: Humanoid robotics, legged locomotion, whole-body control, robot learning
candidates.organizer: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society (fully sponsored)
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings: 8-page full papers, double-anonymous review
candidates.size: 2026: 338 submissions, 130 accepted. The home page gives 382 submissions.
candidates.rankings: No ICORE 2026 entry; CCF none found; GS h5-index 22 (h5-median 37)
candidates.next_meeting: 25th edition: Dec 6–9, 2026, Santa Clara, CA; submissions are closed. The 2027 edition is unannounced.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown for 2027; about late July 2027 for full papers, estimated from the Jul 27, 2026 deadline.
candidates.why_fit: Legged locomotion, whole-body control and robot learning overlap the catalog's robotics and RL venues (ICRA, RSS, CoRL).
candidates.concerns: A narrow hardware-platform focus with modest citation impact. In GS Metrics, an unrelated low-tier 'Humanoid, Nanotechnology...' conference (h5 24) shares the name, so check identities. Separately, IROS (ICORE 2026: A, GS h5 92) is not tracked and would be a stronger robotics addition than Humanoids or CASE.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A fully sponsored IEEE-RAS conference with a senior editor, associate editor and reviewer process. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering
candidates.verdict_reason: IEEE RAS's flagship automation conference (GS h5 30) with a confirmed 2027 deadline. Its industrial-automation and manufacturing core is only adjacent to the catalog's ML, RL and control scope, making it the weakest fit of this batch.
candidates.subtopics: Automation, manufacturing robotics, scheduling, learning for automation
candidates.organizer: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society, which calls it its flagship automation conference
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings. T-ASE, RA-L, T-RO and RAM papers can also be presented.
candidates.size: Unknown; paper counts were not found on the fetched pages.
candidates.rankings: No ICORE 2026 entry; CCF none found; GS h5-index 30 (h5-median 36)
candidates.next_meeting: 23rd edition: Aug 23–27, 2027, Linz, Austria
candidates.next_deadline: Mar 1, 2027 for full papers (regular and special sessions). Special-session proposals are due Jan 15, 2027; work-in-progress and industry papers Apr 1, 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Reinforcement learning, data-driven optimisation and scheduling applied to automation; a RAS sibling of the tracked ICRA.
candidates.concerns: The core audience is industrial and systems engineering (manufacturing, logistics, production scheduling), and its ML content is applied. 2026 was themed 'Smart Industry'. There is a real risk of diluting the families.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A fully sponsored IEEE-RAS conference that RAS calls its flagship on automation.

candidates.full_name: International Symposium of Robotics Research
candidates.verdict_reason: A prestigious, small IFRR flagship with an open call (ICORE C). But it takes about 40 papers, gives attendance priority to authors and invitees, and meets every two years. The 2026 deadline has passed and 2028 is unannounced.
candidates.subtopics: Broad robotics research: manipulation, learning, planning, field robotics
candidates.organizer: International Foundation of Robotics Research (IFRR); ISRR is its flagship symposium
candidates.publication: Springer Proceedings in Advanced Robotics (SPAR) book
candidates.size: About 40 papers, single track over 3 days (2026); limited attendance.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: C; CCF none found; GS h5 none found
candidates.founded: 1983 (from the candidate brief; not re-verified because the IFRR site has an expired certificate)
candidates.next_meeting: Nov 16–20, 2026, Casa del Rio, Malacca, Malaysia. The next edition, about 2028, is unannounced.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown for 2028; about May 2028 for full papers, estimated from the May 15/31, 2026 deadlines.
candidates.why_fit: A high-level robotics research symposium, including robot learning, that complements the tracked RSS and CoRL.
candidates.concerns: A semi-closed format: invited contributions alongside the open call, with priority attendance. It fits the catalog's 'established symposium' style only partly. The ICORE C rank understates its prestige. The IFRR website had an expired TLS certificate, a maintenance problem rather than a predatory signal.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by IFRR, with single-blind review by a symposium programme committee and Springer SPAR proceedings.

candidates.full_name: Workshop on the Algorithmic Foundations of Robotics (WAFR)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and well regarded, and IFRR lists it as one of its symposia, but it is small, rated ICORE C, and has no edition before about 2028 (not yet announced). Better kept in the backlog until WAFR 2028 opens.
candidates.subtopics: Motion planning, algorithmic and geometric robotics, multi-robot planning
candidates.organizer: International Foundation of Robotics Research (IFRR) symposium with rotating co-chairs (2026: Caron, LaValle, Marcucci, Sakçak, Salzman)
candidates.publication: Springer Proceedings in Advanced Robotics (SPAR); selected papers are invited to journal special issues
candidates.size: About 60 researchers (IFRR); 47 papers in 2024 (2 volumes), 32 in 2022
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: C; CCF 2026: not listed; Google Scholar Metrics: no entry found
candidates.next_meeting: unknown (17th WAFR was Oulu, Jun 15-17, 2026; 2028 not announced)
candidates.next_deadline: unknown; the 2026 full-paper deadline was Feb 1, 2026
candidates.why_fit: The main venue for motion planning and algorithmic robotics theory, between the tracked ICAPS, RSS and CDC.
candidates.concerns: Small and single-track. Robotics theory rather than learning or neuro. Nothing to put on the calendar for about 18 months.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Listed as an IFRR symposium alongside ISRR, ISER, RSS and CoRL. Unbroken biennial series since 1994. Senior organisers. Springer SPAR proceedings.

candidates.full_name: International Symposium on Experimental Robotics
candidates.verdict_reason: An IFRR flagship symposium since 1989 and highly reputable, but deliberately tiny (<50 papers), unranked, and without an announced 2027 edition or deadline.
candidates.subtopics: Experimental robotics, field and soft robotics, robot learning on hardware
candidates.organizer: International Foundation of Robotics Research (IFRR); 2025 organisers H. Christensen, O. Khatib, C. Nieto
candidates.publication: Springer Proceedings in Advanced Robotics (SPAR)
candidates.size: Fewer than 50 papers by design (IFRR); 54 papers in the 2023 proceedings, 56 in 2020/21
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed; CCF 2026: not listed; GS h5-index 12 (h5-median 34)
candidates.next_meeting: unknown (expected 2027 but not announced; last edition Santa Fe, Jul 6-10, 2025)
candidates.next_deadline: unknown; the 2025 cycle took 6-page extended abstracts by Mar 15, 2025
candidates.why_fit: Robotics with physical-experiment validation, including robot learning on hardware. It complements the tracked RSS, CoRL and ICRA.
candidates.concerns: No official 2027 site; the proposed URL was only Springer's series page, so the IFRR page is used instead. The symposium is small and its scope is pure robotics.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by IFRR. Held at regular intervals since 1989. PC includes Carlone, Choset, Hutter, Siciliano and Sukhatme. Open CFP via PaperCept.

candidates.full_name: International Symposium on Distributed Autonomous Robotic Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, long-running niche symposium for multi-robot systems and swarms. However, it is unranked, has no Scholar entry, and its 2026 edition has just ended, so the next one is about 2028.
candidates.subtopics: Multi-robot systems, swarm robotics, distributed control and planning
candidates.organizer: Rotating hosts with long-standing advisors (2026: General Chair D. Kurabayashi, PC Chair T. Hatanaka; advisors A. Martinoli, H. Asama). The site names no steering committee.
candidates.publication: Springer Proceedings in Advanced Robotics (SPAR); 12-page full papers
candidates.rankings: none found (ICORE 2026, CCF 2026 and Google Scholar Metrics have no entry)
candidates.next_meeting: unknown (18th DARS was Tokyo, Oct 26-29, 2026; 2028 not announced)
candidates.next_deadline: unknown; the 2026 full-paper deadline was Mar 20, 2026
candidates.why_fit: Multi-robot coordination, swarms and distributed control: a physical-systems counterpart to the tracked AAMAS.
candidates.concerns: Niche and small, with weak bibliometric evidence. Its link to the language-agents family is tenuous. Nothing to schedule until about 2028.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Biennial since 1992 with single-track Springer SPAR proceedings. The swarm-robotics leaders Martinoli and Asama are involved.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Biomimetic and Biohybrid Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, peer-reviewed series that sits naturally next to SAB and ALIFE, but it has a low h5-index and is unranked. There is no 2026 edition, and the 2027 one has no date, city or CFP yet.
candidates.subtopics: Biomimetic robotics, biohybrid systems, neurorobotics
candidates.organizer: Rotating hosts with stable founders (General Chairs T. Prescott and P. Verschure) and an international advisory board; associated with the Convergent Science Network
candidates.publication: Springer LNAI proceedings (refereed full papers of 10-12 pp and short papers of 4-6 pp); late-breaking abstracts are not in the proceedings
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed; CCF 2026: not listed; GS h5-index 9 (h5-median 15)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027, dates and city unannounced (the site only says 'Upcoming Conference in 2027')
candidates.next_deadline: unknown; the 2025 full/short-paper deadline was Apr 14, 2025
candidates.why_fit: Biomimetic and neuro-inspired robotics bridging neuroscience and embodied control. Close in spirit to the tracked SAB, ALIFE and CNS*.
candidates.concerns: Small with a modest citation impact. The 2026 gap makes its continuity uncertain. No standing steering committee is listed.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 14 editions since 2012, all with Springer proceedings. Credible advisory board (Cutkosky, Laschi, Mazzolai, Quinn, Lepora). University-hosted, with no commercial organiser.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Conference on Games
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and IEEE CIS-sponsored, with an ICORE C rank and a confirmed 2027 deadline. But only about a quarter of its papers are game-playing AI; the rest is design, HCI, analytics and serious games.
candidates.subtopics: Game-playing AI, search and RL in games, procedural content generation, player modelling
candidates.organizer: IEEE Computational Intelligence Society (successor to IEEE CIG); 2027 General Chairs M. Mozgovoy, D. Perez Liebana, I. Mariani
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings (8-page full technical papers, double-anonymous review; plus auxiliary short, competition and vision papers)
candidates.size: About 88 regular papers in 2026 (about 25 in AI for Game-Playing)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: C (as COG, was CIG); CCF 2026: not listed; GS h5-index 27 (h5-median 42, listed under the old name CIG)
candidates.next_meeting: Aug 2-5, 2027, University of Aizu, Aizuwakamatsu, Japan
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: Mar 1, 2027 AoE (submission portal opens Nov 27, 2026); auxiliary papers: May 15, 2027
candidates.why_fit: A long-standing venue for game-playing agents, search, RL testbeds and procedural content generation.
candidates.concerns: Games-community scope with only partial ML/RL content. Its rank matches that of many regional venues.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE CIS technical sponsorship. Double-anonymous review. Established game-AI researchers as chairs (Perez Liebana, Yannakakis, Preuss). Continuous annual series.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on World Models
candidates.verdict_reason: Previously deferred. Its About page now names its creators (Balestriero, Zadeh, LeCun), but the CFP is still a 'working draft' with provisional dates. There is no PC, no stated scope and no stated archival status, and no OpenReview venue exists yet. Keep it deferred until these are confirmed.
candidates.subtopics: World models, predictive and model-based learning (detailed scope not yet stated)
candidates.organizer: Creators per the official About page: Randall Balestriero (Brown/AMI), Amir Zadeh (Lambda), Yann LeCun (NYU/AMI). No PC or steering committee is published, and the claim is not corroborated elsewhere.
candidates.publication: unknown (archival status unstated; fully public OpenReview review planned)
candidates.size: unknown (first edition)
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.next_meeting: Late May 2027, San Francisco Bay Area (no exact dates or venue)
candidates.next_deadline: Paper submission Nov 30, 2026 (provisional per the official CFP)
candidates.why_fit: World models are central to model-based RL, planning and embodied AI, linking the ML and control families.
candidates.concerns: First edition with an untested adaptive public-review model. The OpenReview group ICWM.cc did not exist on Oct 30, a month before the stated deadline. No independent corroboration of the organisers was found. Scope and proceedings unstated.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: High-profile named creators and a detailed review-process design. No commercial-organiser red flags, but no track record.

candidates.full_name: European Nonlinear Dynamics Conference (historically European Nonlinear Oscillations Conference)
candidates.verdict_reason: EUROMECH runs this series through its ENOCC committee, and it has been the flagship European nonlinear-dynamics meeting since 1992. It is a direct sibling of the tracked Dynamics Days Europe, NODYCON and NOLTA.
candidates.subtopics: nonlinear oscillations, bifurcations and chaos, slow-fast and non-smooth systems, reduced-order modelling and system identification, random dynamical systems, nonlinear dynamics in biology and robotics
candidates.organizer: EUROMECH (European Mechanics Society) through its ENOCC committee, chaired by S. Lenci. The 2027 local hosts are Pavlovskaia, Kapitaniak and Vaziri at the University of Aberdeen (CADR).
candidates.publication: 2-page abstracts only; ENOC2027 states it has no full-paper submission. No proceedings or special issue is announced.
candidates.size: Official pages give no attendance figure. The ENOC2020 site calls the series the largest high-quality nonlinear-dynamics event worldwide, and the 2027 programme lists at least 14 mini-symposia.
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026, no CCF entry, no GS h5 because it is abstract-only)
candidates.cadence: About every 2-3 years (2017 Budapest, 2020→2022 Lyon, 2024 Delft, 2027 Aberdeen)
candidates.next_meeting: 12th ENOC, 19-23 Jul 2027, P&J Live, Aberdeen, UK
candidates.next_deadline: 2-page abstract, January 2027. The official site gives the month but no day; submission opened Jul 2026 and notifications come in Mar 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Its central scope is nonlinear dynamics, chaos, bifurcations, synchronization and random dynamical systems. That overlaps the dynamics-control family and the tracked Dynamics Days and NODYCON meetings.
candidates.concerns: The programme is mechanics- and vibration-heavy (MEMS, structures, rotordynamics), and only one of 14+ mini-symposia covers biology. The 2027 submission page contains generic boilerplate text, and the exact deadline day is not yet posted.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The EUROMECH site lists the ENOCC committee and members' terms of appointment. The plenary speakers (Epureanu, Jeffrey and others) and mini-symposium organisers (Vakakis, Sieber, Schöll, Kuske) are established names in the field.

candidates.full_name: International Symposium on Forecasting
candidates.verdict_reason: It is the long-running flagship meeting of the forecasting society IIF (47th edition in 2027). It is central to the catalog's time-series coverage and clearly stronger than the tracked ITISE.
candidates.subtopics: probabilistic forecasting, hierarchical reconciliation, deep learning and foundation models for forecasting, forecast evaluation, nowcasting, energy/epidemiology applications
candidates.organizer: International Institute of Forecasters (IIF), a nonprofit founded in 1982 that publishes the International Journal of Forecasting and Foresight.
candidates.publication: 350-word abstracts published as submitted; proceedings or abstract books are posted per year. No archival papers.
candidates.size: Not stated on official pages; parallel academic sessions plus workshops.
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF; abstract-only, so no GS h5)
candidates.cadence: Annual in June/July, alternating between North America and the rest of the world
candidates.next_meeting: 47th ISF, 20-23 Jun 2027, Paphos, Cyprus
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract (350 words), 7 Mar 2027. Invited-session proposals are due 21 Feb and notifications come 28 Mar.
candidates.why_fit: It is the main community meeting for time-series forecasting, including probabilistic and hierarchical forecasting, deep learning, foundation models/LLMs and nowcasting. It complements ITISE, AALTD and TS4H.
candidates.concerns: Review is light (one abstract per person) and a large share of the programme is econometrics and practitioners. The year of the 7 Mar deadline is implied by the 47th-edition page rather than printed.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The official locations page lists every edition since 1981 with named general and programme chairs (Hyndman, Athanasopoulos, Petropoulos and others). The IIF has run it since the society's founding.

candidates.full_name: NetSciX: International School and Conference on Network Science
candidates.verdict_reason: The Network Science Society calls this its signature winter conference. It has run since 2015 and has a strong advisory board and keynote line-up, making it the natural companion to the tracked NetSci.
candidates.subtopics: network science, complex networks, network dynamics and control, networks meet AI (2027 focus)
candidates.organizer: Network Science Society (NSS). 2027 chairs are Jie Sun (Huawei HK) and Alec Kirkley (HKU); the advisory board is D'Souza, Kurths, Sayama and G. Chen, and Lambiotte sits on the organising committee.
candidates.publication: Non-archival 2-page extended abstracts (EasyChair), accepted for oral or poster presentation
candidates.size: Not stated; smaller than the flagship NetSci
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF; non-archival)
candidates.cadence: Annual in winter since 2015 (no 2021 edition); a call for NetSciX 2028 hosts is open
candidates.next_meeting: NetSciX 2027, 24-27 Jan 2027, Sheraton Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong SAR
candidates.next_deadline: 2-page extended abstract, 31 Oct 2026 AoE (extended; the deadline is today). The NetSciX 2028 dates and deadline are not yet announced.
candidates.why_fit: It covers the same community, topics and format as the tracked NetSci (network science, complex networks, network dynamics), with a 2027 special track on network science and AI.
candidates.concerns: The quality of the local organisation varies by host. The 2027 window is effectively closed, so the first actionable deadline will be for 2028. The data notes for NetSci already say 'Distinct from NetSciX', so the two must stay separate series.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The NSS site lists every NetSci-X edition from 2015 (Rio) to 2026 (Auckland). The 2027 keynotes include Cristopher Moore, Marta González and Mario di Bernardo.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Computational Social Science
candidates.verdict_reason: It is clearly legitimate and the leading venue in its field, with double-blind review of abstracts. Its centre of gravity is social science, which is close to the deferred ICWSM and CSCW, so its scope fit with the catalog is only partial.
candidates.subtopics: computational social science, social networks, collective behaviour, large-scale social experiments, simulation models, LLMs/NLP for social research
candidates.organizer: International Society for Computational Social Science (ISCSS). The 2026 host was the Vermont Complex Systems Institute at the University of Vermont.
candidates.publication: Non-archival 2-page extended abstracts, double-blind, reviewed by multiple PC members; accepted as lightning talk, oral or poster
candidates.size: Not stated on official pages
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (official pages call it selective but give no rate)
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF; non-archival)
candidates.next_meeting: 13th IC2S2 (2027): host and dates not announced (2027.ic2s2.net still shows the 2026 site)
candidates.next_deadline: 2-page extended abstract, about early March 2027 (estimated from 3 Mar 2026)
candidates.why_fit: It overlaps the tracked NetSci, CCS and COMPLEX NETWORKS through social networks, collective behaviour, simulation models and LLMs for social research.
candidates.concerns: Most of the programme is sociology, political science and economics. Retagging it as responsible-ai would be a stretch. The 2027 host and dates are unknown.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ISCSS was created to run IC2S2 and has published by-laws and governance. The editions are hosted by major institutions (Penn 2024, Linköping/IAS 2025, UVM 2026).

candidates.full_name: IUPAP International Conference on Statistical Physics
candidates.verdict_reason: It is a top-tier IUPAP flagship and plainly legitimate. Its scope is statistical physics at large (quantum many-body, soft matter), so it is adjacent rather than central, and it meets only every three years, with the next edition in 2028.
candidates.subtopics: non-equilibrium and stochastic processes, nonlinear physics and chaos, disordered systems and neural networks, biological physics, complex systems
candidates.organizer: IUPAP Commission C3 (Statistical Physics), which entrusts each edition to a national society. StatPhys30 is chaired by Suani Pinho (UFBA) and Celia Anteneodo (PUC-Rio).
candidates.publication: Book of abstracts plus a journal special issue (StatPhys29 had one; StatPhys30 lists one)
candidates.size: StatPhys29 (Florence 2025) had 1,808 abstracts, 350+ orals, about 1,200-1,400 posters and about 1,500 attendees
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (most abstracts are presented, many as posters)
candidates.rankings: none found (physics venue; not in ICORE2026 or CCF)
candidates.next_meeting: StatPhys30, 17-21 Jul 2028, Salvador Convention Center, Bahia, Brazil
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract, about January 2028 (estimated from 7 Jan 2025 for StatPhys29). Satellite proposals are due 31 Jan 2027.
candidates.why_fit: It is the theoretical backbone of complex systems: non-equilibrium physics, stochastic processes, nonlinear physics, biological and neural networks, and the physics of complex systems.
candidates.concerns: It is physics-heavy, and the abstract count against session slots implies near-universal acceptance as posters. The StatPhys30 site is partly placeholder text, and it is not actionable until 2027-28.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: It runs under the IUPAP C3 commission, awards the Boltzmann Medal at each edition, and the 2025 opening lecture was given by Giorgio Parisi.

candidates.full_name: International Sunbelt Social Network Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: It is a legitimate, long-running society conference (46th edition in 2026). Its core is social network analysis in sociology, which is only adjacent to the catalog's complex-systems and ML focus.
candidates.subtopics: social network analysis, statistical network models (ERGM/SAOM), personal and organisational networks, network data collection
candidates.organizer: International Network for Social Network Analysis (INSNA), which also publishes Social Networks and Connections
candidates.publication: Book of abstracts; non-archival
candidates.size: Not stated on official pages; multi-day with parallel sessions and a full workshop day
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF; non-archival)
candidates.next_meeting: Sunbelt 2027 (XLVII), 21-26 Jun 2027, Le Centre Sheraton, Montréal, Canada
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract, about February 2027 (estimated). The 2027 call is not posted and registration opens Jan 2027.
candidates.why_fit: It overlaps NetSci and COMPLEX NETWORKS on network methods (ERGMs, SAOMs, network statistics). Sunbelt and NetSci held a joint 'Networks 2021' meeting.
candidates.concerns: It is sociology-leaning, abstract review is light, and the 2027 call and deadline are unpublished. Its overlap with the tracked network venues is partial.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The INSNA archive lists every edition with keynotes such as Granovetter, Snijders, Carley, Brandes and Lazer.

candidates.full_name: Workshop on Modelling and Mining Networks (formerly Workshop on Algorithms and Models for the Web Graph)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and has a strong programme committee, and its topic sits squarely in network science. But it is very small and ranked only ICORE C, and a noticeable share of the talks come from the organisers' own groups.
candidates.subtopics: random graph models, community detection, hypergraphs, temporal networks, graph embeddings, network processes
candidates.organizer: Steering committee of Andrei Broder, Fan Chung Graham and Pawel Pralat. Co-chairs come from UCSD, TMU, SGH Warsaw and the Tutte Institute.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS proceedings (WAW 2026 is LNCS vol. 16630). There is also a non-archival route: 1-page abstracts posted on the website.
candidates.size: WAW 2026 had about 22 contributed talks, 5 plenaries (Moore, Eliassi-Rad, Lambiotte, Stegehuis) and tutorials in a single track. The full-paper count was not verified because the Springer page was blocked.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (retailer claim of 7/10 full papers not verified)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 C (as 'Workshop on Algorithms And Models For The Web Graph'); no CCF; no GS h5 found
candidates.cadence: Annual since 2009 (irregular earlier; no edition 2021-22), usually June
candidates.next_meeting: WAW 2027 (22nd): Inria Sophia Antipolis, France, 28 Jun-2 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (LNCS, ≤15 pp): 1 Feb 2027. Notification: 1 Mar 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Random graph models, community detection, hypergraphs, temporal networks and network dynamics. These are core topics of 'Complex Systems & Network Science' and 'Graphs & Graph Learning'.
candidates.concerns: Tiny and somewhat insular. Overlaps heavily with COMPLEX NETWORKS, CompleNet, NetSci and LoG, which are already tracked. The deadline for the abstract-only route is not stated.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Running since 2002 with LNCS proceedings. Credible PC (van der Hofstad, Porter, Boguñá, Brandes, Frieze, Ravi Kumar, Litvak). Hosted by the Fields Institute in 2026 and Inria in 2027.

candidates.full_name: DPG Spring Meeting of the Condensed Matter Section (SKM), incl. Dynamics & Statistical Physics (DY) and Physics of Socio-economic Systems (SOE) divisions
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate, run by the world's largest physical society, and its DY and SOE divisions are central to complex systems. But it is a broad national condensed-matter mega-meeting with essentially non-selective abstracts, and only a few divisions fit the catalog.
candidates.subtopics: nonlinear dynamics, statistical physics, complex networks, socio-economic systems, biological physics
candidates.organizer: Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft (DPG); programme set by the SKM divisions (DY, SOE, BP, etc.)
candidates.publication: Abstract book only (Verhandlungen der DPG); no proceedings
candidates.size: More than 4,800 physicists (Regensburg 2027 announcement). Each presenting author may submit only one contribution.
candidates.rankings: none found (not a CS venue; ICORE/CCF n/a)
candidates.next_meeting: 90th DPG Annual Conference / SKM Spring Meeting, University of Regensburg, Germany, 14-19 Mar 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract (contributed talk or poster): 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 CET. Programme and acceptance announced 3 Feb 2027.
candidates.why_fit: The DY division (nonlinear dynamics, statistical physics, networks) and the SOE division are the main German and European physics-of-complex-systems forum. This parallels Dynamics Days and CCS.
candidates.concerns: About 13 divisions, mostly condensed matter, so the catalog entry would need DY/SOE framing. The meeting is national-society based, mostly German participants, in-person only, and the review bar is low.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by the German Physical Society, a non-profit and the largest physical society in the world. Has a programme committee, Heraeus Foundation support, and runs as a long annual series.

candidates.full_name: SIAM Conference on the Life Sciences
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate SIAM activity-group meeting with a large minisymposium programme. Mathematical biology is adjacent to the catalog's dynamics and neuroscience scope rather than central to it, and the next edition is not until 2028.
candidates.subtopics: mathematical biology, dynamical models, biological networks, mathematical neuroscience
candidates.organizer: SIAM (Activity Group on Life Sciences)
candidates.publication: none (abstract-based talks; no proceedings)
candidates.size: LS26 had 89 active minisymposia and 14 contributed sessions. LS24 had 64 minisymposia and 13 contributed sessions.
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.cadence: Biennial, even years. LS24: 10-13 Jun 2024. LS26: 5-9 Jul 2026, co-located with SIAM AN26 in Cleveland.
candidates.next_meeting: LS28 (2028); dates and location unknown
candidates.next_deadline: Minisymposium proposals and contributed abstracts for LS28 are unknown. These are typically due several months before a mid-2028 meeting (estimated).
candidates.why_fit: Dynamical-systems modelling of biological systems, with some mathematical neuroscience. Its community overlaps with SIAM DS and CNS*.
candidates.concerns: siam.org pages return 403, so the call for papers was not read; facts come from the SIAM program system only. Its scope duplicates SMB, so the catalog likely needs only one of the two. Neuroscience is a minor strand.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by SIAM, a major applied-mathematics society. Joint plenary with the SIAM Annual Meeting in 2026.

candidates.full_name: Society for Mathematical Biology Annual Meeting
candidates.verdict_reason: The main meeting of a long-established scholarly society. Its biology-application focus makes it adjacent rather than central, and the 2027 call is not yet published.
candidates.subtopics: mathematical biology, population dynamics, reaction networks, collective behaviour, mathematical neuroscience
candidates.organizer: Society for Mathematical Biology (founded 1973; publishes the Bulletin of Mathematical Biology). 2027 programme co-chairs: Katira and Buchmann.
candidates.publication: none (abstract-based; society journal is separate)
candidates.size: unknown (not stated on official pages)
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.cadence: Annual, summer; sometimes joint (2026 with ECMTB/ESMTB in Graz, 13-17 Jul 2026)
candidates.founded: Society 1973; annual meetings at least since 2018 (Sydney) per society list
candidates.next_meeting: SMB 2027: San Diego State University and University of San Diego, CA, 27/28 Jun-2 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Abstracts and minisymposium proposals: submissions open Nov 2026; deadline not yet posted.
candidates.why_fit: Nonlinear dynamics in biology, population dynamics, reaction networks, and a Mathematical Neuroscience subgroup. Overlaps CNS* and SIAM DS at the edges.
candidates.concerns: Mostly biology applications (oncology, epidemiology, ecology). It is abstract-only and its scope duplicates SIAM LS. Two SMB pages give slightly different start dates (27 vs 28 Jun).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: An established non-profit society with a flagship journal and subgroup-organised programme. Meetings are held jointly with ESMTB and KSMB.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably legitimate and the flagship of its field, ranked ICORE B with GS h5 44. Information and coding theory is adjacent to the catalog's signal-processing and learning-theory scope, not central, and would pull the catalog toward communications.
candidates.subtopics: information theory, coding, statistical inference, learning theory, signal processing
candidates.organizer: IEEE Information Theory Society
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings (short full papers; exact 2027 page limit not verified)
candidates.size: unknown this pass (large single-track-per-room flagship, typically on the order of 1,000 attendees; not verified)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B; GS h5-index 44 (h5-median 57); companion ITW is ICORE2026 B, GS h5 19
candidates.founded: unknown (decades-old ITSoc flagship; Shannon Lecture venue)
candidates.next_meeting: ISIT 2027: Sorrento, Italy, 27 Jun-2 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper: 10 Jan 2027 (per the ITSoc event listing).
candidates.why_fit: Overlaps statistical signal processing, estimation and learning theory, matching IEEE SSP and COLT in the catalog.
candidates.concerns: Core content is coding and communications theory, which falls outside the catalog's families. The 2027 site returned 403, so the page limit and notification date were not verified. The companion ITW 2027 (Munich, 5-8 Apr) deadline has already passed (2 Oct 2026).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Flagship of IEEE ITSoc. Ranked ICORE2026 B and third in Google Scholar's information-theory venues (h5 44).

candidates.full_name: Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
candidates.verdict_reason: A long-running, respected signal-processing meeting (60th edition in 2026, GS h5 26). Selection is based on an extended summary, the programme leans heavily on invited special sessions and communications, and ICORE ranks it only 'National: USA'.
candidates.subtopics: signal processing, graph signal processing, adaptive systems and ML, array processing, biomedical and neural signals
candidates.organizer: Non-profit SS&C Conference Corporation, with IEEE Signal Processing Society as technical co-sponsor. 2026 chairs: Hegde (NYU) and Asif (UCR).
candidates.publication: Post-conference IEEE proceedings (Xplore); 5-8 page final papers, published early the following year
candidates.size: 2026: about 76 technical sessions across 8 tracks (roughly several hundred papers, estimated)
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 'National: USA' (as ACSSC); GS h5-index 26 (h5-median 40); no CCF found
candidates.cadence: Annual, late Oct/early Nov, always at Pacific Grove, CA
candidates.next_meeting: 61st Asilomar, Pacific Grove, CA, late Oct/Nov 2027 (dates not yet posted)
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract plus extended summary (500-1000 words): about 1 May 2027. Estimated from the 2026 deadline of 1 May; special-session proposals were due about 20 Feb.
candidates.why_fit: Signal processing and adaptive systems, graph signal processing, network science and biomedical/neural signal tracks. It complements ICASSP, EUSIPCO and IEEE SSP.
candidates.concerns: Communications and MIMO dominate the programme. Many sessions are invited, and review is of extended summaries rather than full papers. Final papers come after the conference, and there is a limit of four submissions per author.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 60 consecutive annual editions, IEEE SPS technical co-sponsorship, a credible track-chair panel (ETH, Princeton, TU Delft), and GS h5 26.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Workshop on Computational Advances in Multi-Sensor Adaptive Processing
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate IEEE SPS workshop with credible chairs and IEEE-format peer review, covering tensor, graph and sparse methods and ML. It is small and unranked, and the 2027 venue is not public.
candidates.organizer: IEEE Signal Processing Society (SAM Technical Committee lineage); 2025 general chairs A. G. Marques and G. Mateos, TPC chairs F. Ahmad and A. Bertrand
candidates.publication: IEEE conference proceedings (4+1-page papers, peer reviewed). IEEE Xplore inclusion is not stated on the 2025 pages but is customary for SPS workshops.
candidates.size: 2025 (10th edition): 16 technical sessions, 6 plenaries and 3 tutorials. Roughly 100-130 papers (estimated from the session count).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: none found. CCF 2026: none found. GS h5 6 (from the discovery agent, not re-verified).
candidates.cadence: Biennial in odd years, in December, traditionally at a Caribbean resort (2025: Punta Cana, 14-17 Dec)
candidates.next_meeting: CAMSAP 2027, expected December 2027; venue and dates not announced
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4 pages + 1 page of references), expected about July 2027 (2025 deadline: 15 Jul)
candidates.why_fit: Computational and statistical signal processing with tensor, graph-signal, sparse and ML methods. It sits close to the tracked IEEE MLSP and SSP and shares organisers with the GSP community.
candidates.concerns: Small resort meeting with no ICORE or CCF rank, and its citation metrics are weak. Sensing, comms and radar content is a large share. No 2027 page was found, and the web search budget ran out, so the 2027 host is unverified.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Sensor Array and Multichannel Signal Processing Workshop
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate SPS technical-committee workshop, but its core is array processing for radar, MIMO and ISAC. This is the weakest scope fit in this group; add it only if CAMSAP is added.
candidates.organizer: IEEE Signal Processing Society, Sensor Array and Multichannel (SAM) Technical Committee
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore, EI-indexed (4 pages + 1 page of references; only presented papers are published)
candidates.size: 14th edition, 2026. Paper count unknown.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: none found. CCF 2026: none found. GS h5 19 (from the discovery agent, not re-verified).
candidates.cadence: Biennial in even years, around June-July, alternating with CAMSAP
candidates.next_meeting: SAM 2028, not announced (2026: Shenzhen, 13-16 Jul 2026)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4+1 pages), expected about late January 2028 (2026 deadline: 28 Jan 2026)
candidates.why_fit: Statistical multichannel signal processing, with tensor and ML methods and source separation. It falls under the catalog's Signal Processing subtopic.
candidates.concerns: Dominated by beamforming, DoA, MIMO radar and massive-MIMO communications, which is peripheral to the catalog's ML, dynamics and neuro focus. The next deadline is over a year away.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Sampling Theory and Applications
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-running conference bridging mathematics and signal processing. Its steering committee is strong (Pfander, Eldar, Bölcskei, Rauhut, Krahmer) and it publishes in IEEE Xplore. The scope is niche and math-heavy, so it fits the catalog only adjacently.
candidates.organizer: SampTA Steering Committee (chair G. Pfander); founders include Unser, Gröchenig and Feichtinger. The 2027 host is Utrecht University with TU Delft.
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore (4-page IEEEtran papers, single-blind review; no-shows are not published)
candidates.size: 16th edition in 2027. Attendance and paper counts unknown; 9 plenary speakers announced for 2027.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: none found. CCF 2026: none found. GS h5 unknown.
candidates.cadence: Biennial in odd years, in July (2019 Bordeaux, 2023 Yale, 2025 Vienna)
candidates.next_meeting: SampTA 2027, Utrecht, Netherlands, 26-30 Jul 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4 pages), 31 Jan 2027. Notification 15 Apr 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Sampling theory, compressed sensing, harmonic analysis and reconstruction: the mathematical foundations of the Signal Processing subtopic
candidates.concerns: Applied-harmonic-analysis audience, with little ML, dynamics or time-series content. The IEEE and URASIP sponsorship is shown only as logos. The submission link is not yet open.

candidates.full_name: Graph Signal Processing Workshop
candidates.verdict_reason: Well regarded small community meeting with leading GSP researchers. It fits the graph-learning and signal-processing subtopics, but it is non-archival with no society, and the 2027 edition is not announced.
candidates.organizer: Informal GSP community committee (Marques, Leus, Segarra, Isufi, Mateos, Dong and others). Hosts rotate and are supported by ELLIS units; 2026 was hosted by Universidad Rey Juan Carlos.
candidates.publication: None: 2-page extended abstracts, explicitly with no published proceedings (in 2025 there was also a TMLR journal track)
candidates.size: 2026: 49 contributed items (35 talks, 14 posters) plus 5 invited speakers
candidates.rankings: None found (non-archival)
candidates.cadence: Annual since 2023 (6th Oxford 2023, Delft 2024, Montréal 2025, 9th Madrid 8-10 Jun 2026). Earlier editions 2016-2020 were irregular.
candidates.next_meeting: GSP 2027, not announced (expected around May-June 2027)
candidates.next_deadline: Extended abstract (2 pages), expected about March-April 2027 (2026 deadline: 6 Apr)
candidates.why_fit: The dedicated standalone meeting for graph signal processing and graph ML, with topology inference and time-vertex dynamics. It complements the tracked LoG and fits the established-workshop style (ML4H/TS4H).
candidates.concerns: No society or formal steering committee, and no proceedings. Small, and the host and date are set year by year, so there is a continuity risk.

candidates.full_name: Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing
candidates.verdict_reason: Historic, reputable meeting (62nd edition) for the control and information-theory community. However, it mixes invited sessions with lightly specified review, and its proceedings now sit only on the UIUC IDEALS repository.
candidates.organizer: Coordinated Science Laboratory, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2026 chairs B. Touri and Z. J. Zhao); IEEE ITS logo shown
candidates.publication: Proceedings hosted on IDEALS (UIUC repository) for 2025-2026; earlier editions were in IEEE Xplore (from memory, not re-verified). 8-page IEEE two-column papers.
candidates.size: 2026: 40 sessions, 165 papers
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: none found. CCF 2026: none found. GS h5 11 (from the discovery agent, not re-verified).
candidates.next_meeting: 63rd Allerton, expected September 2027 in Urbana, IL (not announced)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (up to 8 pages), expected about mid-June 2027 (2026 deadline: 15 Jun, extended)
candidates.why_fit: Control, learning, optimization, networks and statistical inference. It overlaps the tracked CDC, ACC and L4DC communities.
candidates.concerns: Many invited sessions (invited speakers need only an abstract), and the review process is not described. Proceedings are no longer in a major index. Communications and information-theory content dominates.

candidates.full_name: APS Global Physics Summit (successor to the APS March Meeting), statistical/nonlinear and soft/living-matter sessions
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably legitimate, but it is a general-physics mega-meeting where the relevant part is a small slice. Abstracts are accepted if they follow the guidelines (no scientific selection), submission requires APS or reciprocal-society membership, and the 2027 window has already closed.
candidates.organizer: American Physical Society
candidates.publication: None (abstracts only, in the APS Bulletin)
candidates.size: 14,000+ attendees and 220+ exhibitors (2027 figures stated by APS)
candidates.rankings: None (abstract meeting)
candidates.next_meeting: GPS 2027: Atlanta, GA and online, 11-16 Apr 2027. The 2028 dates and city are not announced.
candidates.next_deadline: Contributed abstract: the 2027 call closed 29 Oct 2026. The 2028 deadline is expected about late October 2027.
candidates.why_fit: The 'SPLASHY' district (soft, living, active, statistical matter) hosts statistical and nonlinear physics, and network sessions, adjacent to Dynamics Days and NetSci
candidates.concerns: Too broad: the relevant sessions are a tiny fraction of the meeting. Submission is limited to APS or reciprocal members, and there is essentially no review. The 2027 deadline passed two days ago.

candidates.full_name: AMIA Annual Symposium (American Medical Informatics Association)
candidates.verdict_reason: This is the flagship clinical-informatics meeting, run by a major society, and its peer-reviewed papers are archived in PMC. It is central to the healthcare family, but its dates must be checked in a browser before adding it.
candidates.subtopics: Clinical informatics, clinical NLP, EHR ML, decision support, health data science
candidates.organizer: American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA), a professional society with about 5,500 members
candidates.publication: AMIA Annual Symposium Proceedings (ISSN 1942-597X). Full papers are indexed in PubMed/PMC, which covers 1977 onward under earlier titles. Poster abstracts have not been archived since 2006.
candidates.size: Large: multi-track, thousands of attendees (exact count unverified because amia.org blocked my fetch).
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: C (interdisciplinary, p.72, verified in the CCF PDF). ICORE2026 'National: USA' is the orchestrator's figure; I could not re-check it because the CORE portal blocked my fetch. Not in the Google Scholar Medical Informatics top 20 (cut-off h5 = 46).
candidates.next_meeting: AMIA 2026: Dallas, Nov 2026 (dates from an aggregator, unverified). AMIA 2027: unknown (San Diego is reported but unverified).
candidates.next_deadline: AMIA 2027 full papers and podium abstracts: about mid-March 2027 (estimated from past cycles).
candidates.why_fit: Its clinical NLP, EHR machine learning, decision support and health data science overlap directly with the tracked MLHC, CHIL, ML4H, AIME and IEEE BHI.
candidates.concerns: Much of the programme is health-IT implementation and policy rather than ML methods. It is US-centric. Papers, podium abstracts, posters and panels each have their own gate. amia.org returned 403, so no dates or deadlines were confirmed officially. My web-search budget ran out before I started this review.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Major professional society, proceedings archived in PMC since the 1970s, and CCF-listed.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Information Processing in Medical Imaging
candidates.verdict_reason: It has run since 1969 with a named board of leading researchers. It is small, highly selective, double-blind and published in LNCS, and it is central to biomedical-imaging methods.
candidates.subtopics: Mathematical, statistical and ML foundations of medical image analysis; shape; reconstruction
candidates.organizer: IPMI Board (Noble, Duncan, Golland, Wells, Prince, Ourselin, de Bruijne and others). 2027 general chairs: Lombaert and Schnabel.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS proceedings
candidates.size: 51 accepted papers (2025), 63 (2023). Single-track residential meeting.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (highly selective; about 50-60 papers per edition)
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: not listed (verified). ICORE2026: not re-checked (portal blocked my fetch); the orchestrator found no entry. Not in the Google Scholar Radiology & Medical Imaging top 20.
candidates.next_meeting: 30th IPMI: 27 Jun-2 Jul 2027, Jouvence Center, Lake Stukely, Orford, Quebec
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract 7 Dec 2026; full paper 14 Dec 2026, AoE, no extensions
candidates.why_fit: The methods-oriented elite medical-imaging meeting, and a natural companion to the tracked MICCAI, MIDL and ISBI.
candidates.concerns: No ICORE or CCF rank because it is small and biennial. In-person attendance is mandatory, with one registration per paper, and the fee includes accommodation.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: About 60-year history, long-standing board, Erbsmann Prize, LNCS, double-blind review.

candidates.full_name: SPIE Medical Imaging
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, long-running meeting run by a recognised society, but acceptance is abstract-based and manuscripts get light review. Much of the content is imaging physics and engineering, so it is a weaker fit than IPMI or MICCAI.
candidates.subtopics: Medical image processing, CAD, digital pathology, imaging informatics, image-guided interventions, imaging physics
candidates.organizer: SPIE (the international society for optics and photonics)
candidates.publication: Proceedings of SPIE (SPIE Digital Library), one volume per sub-conference
candidates.size: Eight parallel conferences: Image Processing, CAD/Clinical and Biomedical Imaging, Digital and Computational Pathology, Imaging Informatics, Physics, Perception, Ultrasound, Image-Guided Interventions. Attendance unknown because SPIE pages blocked my fetch.
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: not listed (verified). ICORE2026: not re-checked (portal blocked my fetch). Not in the Google Scholar Radiology & Medical Imaging top 20.
candidates.next_meeting: 14-18 Feb 2027, Vancouver, BC, Canada
candidates.next_deadline: MI 2027 abstracts very likely closed (about Aug 2026). MI 2028 abstracts about Aug 2027 (estimated).
candidates.why_fit: A large applied medical-imaging community (CAD, pathology, image processing) that overlaps with ISBI and MICCAI topics.
candidates.concerns: Acceptance rests on the abstract, and the proceedings manuscript is not reviewed as strictly as a conference paper. The topics are broad and include optics and physics. The SPIE deadline pages sit behind bot detection, so no 2027 deadlines could be confirmed.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by a long-established scientific society, with proceedings in the SPIE Digital Library.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Research in Computational Molecular Biology
candidates.verdict_reason: A clearly top-tier computational-biology venue, but its scope is algorithmic and molecular, not clinical. The catalog's taxonomy has no bioinformatics topic, so the fit is adjacent.
candidates.subtopics: Algorithms for computational biology, genomics, ML for molecular biology
candidates.organizer: RECOMB Steering Committee
candidates.publication: Papers posted on the conference site and indexed in DBLP, with no separate proceedings volume in 2027. Invited extended versions go to Cell Systems, Genome Research or the Journal of Computational Biology.
candidates.size: Unknown (not on the official pages I fetched). 6 satellite meetings.
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: B (interdisciplinary, p.71, verified). ICORE2026 B is the orchestrator's figure; not re-checked (portal blocked my fetch). Not in the Google Scholar Bioinformatics top 20 (journal-heavy list).
candidates.next_meeting: 31st RECOMB: 17-20 May 2027, Toronto (satellites 15-16 May)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper 4 Nov 2026 AoE, open only to abstracts registered by 28 Oct 2026 (that registration has already closed). Posters TBA.
candidates.why_fit: Its ML for molecular biology and genomics overlaps with the catalog's ML-for-biomedicine interests.
candidates.concerns: Molecular and genomic rather than clinical, so it would bring a new domain with no matching topic. The 2027 paper cycle is effectively closed to new entries. Review is single-blind, papers are limited to 10 pages, and code is required.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-standing steering committee, partner journals, CCF B.

candidates.full_name: Intelligent Systems for Molecular Biology (joint ISMB/ECCB in odd years)
candidates.verdict_reason: The ISCB flagship and clearly elite, but its centre is bioinformatics and systems biology. The catalog lacks a computational-biology topic, so only its ML and text-mining tracks overlap.
candidates.subtopics: Bioinformatics, ML in computational and systems biology, biomedical text mining, translational bioinformatics
candidates.organizer: International Society for Computational Biology (ISCB), jointly with ECCB in odd years
candidates.publication: Proceedings papers appear in an open-access, online-only special issue of the journal Bioinformatics. Talks and posters are selected from abstracts.
candidates.size: Over 1,500 attendees (ISCB). More than 600 talks expected in 2027.
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: B (interdisciplinary, p.71, verified). ICORE2026 A is the orchestrator's figure; not re-checked (portal blocked my fetch). Bioinformatics journal h5 = 137 (Google Scholar; journal-level, not conference-specific).
candidates.next_meeting: 35th ISMB / 26th ECCB: 18-22 Jul 2027, Bella Center Copenhagen (virtual option)
candidates.next_deadline: Proceedings full paper 14 Jan 2027, AoE, no extensions. Talk and poster abstract deadlines TBA.
candidates.why_fit: Its ML-in-computational-biology, biomedical text-mining and translational-bioinformatics tracks overlap with ML for health.
candidates.concerns: Very large. Proceedings, track talks and posters each have separate gates. The official key-dates page is still empty, and the central scope is molecular, not clinical.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Flagship of a major scientific society, with proceedings in a high-impact journal.

candidates.full_name: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, respected 32-year archival venue indexed in PubMed. Its topics follow each year's session proposals and lean to biocomputing, so it fits the catalog only part of the time.
candidates.subtopics: Biomedical informatics, clinical AI, clinical NLP/LLMs, precision medicine, systems biology (sessions change each year)
candidates.organizer: PSB organizing committee (Stanford-hosted). Each year's sessions are proposed by field leaders.
candidates.publication: Peer-reviewed full-paper proceedings, 12 pages, published electronically (World Scientific), open access, indexed in PubMed/PMC
candidates.size: 6 paper sessions in 2027. Attendance and paper count unknown.
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: not listed (verified). ICORE2026 'National: USA' is the orchestrator's figure; not re-checked (portal blocked my fetch). Not in the Google Scholar Bioinformatics top 20.
candidates.next_meeting: 3-7 Jan 2027, Big Island of Hawaii
candidates.next_deadline: Poster abstracts 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 PM PT (confirmed). PSB 2028 full papers about early Aug 2027 (estimated).
candidates.why_fit: The 2027 sessions include clinical AI/ML deployment, NLP/LLMs for clinical knowledge and precision medicine, which overlap with MLHC and CHIL.
candidates.concerns: Topics rotate each year and are mostly molecular or systems biology. The 2027 paper deadline was 3 Aug 2026; 8 Sep was the notification date, not the deadline the orchestrator listed. The meeting is in Hawaii only.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 32 years of proceedings online since 1996, PubMed indexing, and peer-reviewed full papers.

candidates.full_name: Machine Learning in Computational Biology
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, well-regarded small meeting with strong organisers and PMLR proceedings. Its genomics and protein core sits next to the catalog's healthcare family rather than inside it: the taxonomy has no computational-biology topic.
candidates.subtopics: ML for genomics, single-cell, proteins, and biomedical and molecular data
candidates.organizer: Organising committee: general chairs D. Knowles (Columbia/NYGC) and P. Koo (CSHL), with Su-In Lee, G. Quon, J. Zou and S. Mostafavi. No formal society or steering committee is listed.
candidates.publication: PMLR, opt-in for full papers: v165 (2021), v200, v240, v261, v311 (2025). Two-page abstracts are poster-only and non-archival.
candidates.size: 23 PMLR papers in 2025 (v311) and 10 in 2024 (v261), plus poster abstracts. In-person capacity is limited; the virtual years had about 1,000 Zoom registrants.
candidates.rankings: None found. Not in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026; Google Scholar h5 not checked.
candidates.cadence: Annual. The 2023-2025 editions were in September; 2026 moved to November.
candidates.founded: 2004, as a NeurIPS workshop; independent conference since 2019
candidates.next_meeting: 21st MLCB: 16-17 Nov 2026, New York Genome Center, NYC (hybrid, streamed on YouTube).
candidates.next_deadline: 2027 edition: full paper (8 pp) and abstract (2 pp), estimated around early July 2027. The 2026 deadline was 3 Jul 2026.
candidates.why_fit: The ML-for-biology counterpart of the tracked ML4H and LoG. Its methods focus fits ml-ai; biomedical data overlaps healthcare.
candidates.concerns: No ICORE or CCF rank. Small, no formal society, single-blind review, and dates have shifted between September and November. Mapping it needs a comp-bio framing that the topic list lacks.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 20+ year history, PMLR proceedings since 2021, peer review through CMT, and well-known PIs as organisers. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing / International Symposium on Wearable Computers
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier and unquestionably legitimate, but the main track is journal-first: IMWUT has rolling quarterly deadlines. Its HCI and systems scope is close to the HCI venues (CSCW, UIST, IUI, ICMI, ASSETS) the owner previously deferred.
candidates.subtopics: Wearable and mobile sensing, mHealth, activity recognition, physiological sensing
candidates.organizer: Joint UbiComp/ISWC conference under ACM; the 2026 submissions ran through PCS under the SIGCHI society (ACM, SIGCHI and SIGMOBILE are listed as supporters). No steering committee is shown.
candidates.publication: Main papers are IMWUT journal articles (ACM). ISWC Notes (6 pp) and Briefs (3 pp), posters and demos are archived in the ACM DL.
candidates.size: No official attendance figure found. Large ACM conference with a multi-track programme, workshops and a design exhibition.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (main track is IMWUT journal review)
candidates.rankings: CCF 2026: A (HCI & pervasive, p.64). ICORE2026: 'journal published' for both UbiComp and ISWC (Wearables). IMWUT Google Scholar h5 is 64 (HCI).
candidates.cadence: Annual, usually September or October; joint UbiComp/ISWC since 2013.
candidates.founded: HUC 1999, UbiComp 2001, Pervasive 2002; merged into UbiComp and joint with ISWC since 2013
candidates.next_meeting: 2026 edition: Shanghai, 13-15 Oct 2026 (workshops 11-12 Oct), already past. The 2027 city and dates were not found.
candidates.next_deadline: IMWUT journal paper due 1 Nov 2026 (journal deadlines 1 Feb, 1 May and 1 Nov). The ISWC Notes/Briefs route is estimated around May 2027 (2026: 24 May).
candidates.why_fit: The leading venue for wearable and mobile human sensing, mHealth and activity recognition. It matches 'Biometrics & Human Sensing' and sensor time series.
candidates.concerns: Journal-first deadlines do not map to one edition. HCI-leaning scope. Identity trap: this ISWC (Wearable Computers) is not the tracked ISWC (Semantic Web). 2027 venue unknown; web search budget ran out.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM conference with ACM DL archiving, CCF A, top Google Scholar h5 in HCI, and a 25-year history.

candidates.full_name: AMIA Amplify Informatics Conference (merger of the AMIA Informatics Summit and the Clinical Informatics Conference, from 2026)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and society-run, but newly restructured and unranked. AMIA's ranked flagship is the November Annual Symposium (CCF C), not this spring meeting. 2027 facts could not be verified.
candidates.subtopics: Translational bioinformatics, clinical research informatics, data science and AI for health
candidates.organizer: AMIA (American Medical Informatics Association), founded 1989, with about 5,500 members
candidates.publication: Summit papers are in 'AMIA Summits on Translational Science Proceedings' (PMC, v.2011 to v.2026). Whether 2027 keeps a proceedings route under Amplify is unverified.
candidates.size: unknown (amia.org returned 403)
candidates.rankings: None for this meeting. The separate AMIA Annual Symposium is CCF 2026 C and ICORE2026 'National: USA'.
candidates.founded: AMIA 1989. Summits since 2008 (TBI); Amplify brand since 2026.
candidates.next_meeting: Reported as Atlanta, 12-15 Apr 2027. Not verified because the official page returned 403.
candidates.next_deadline: Papers and podium abstracts estimated around early December 2026 (the 2026 cycle was reported as 2 Dec 2025). Not verified.
candidates.why_fit: Translational bioinformatics, clinical research informatics and health data science overlap 'Healthcare & Clinical AI'.
candidates.concerns: The 2026 merger makes series identity and routes unstable. US-centric, practitioner-heavy informatics. Consider the AMIA Annual Symposium instead or as well. Official pages were blocked and the search budget ran out.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Major professional society; the Summit proceedings are indexed in PMC through v.2026.

candidates.full_name: World Congress on Medical and Health Informatics
candidates.verdict_reason: An unquestionably legitimate IMIA flagship with a 50-year history. It is broad health informatics with inclusive acceptance (about 56% of items), so it sits below the catalog's ML-level venues.
candidates.subtopics: Health data science and AI, clinical decision support, global and public health informatics
candidates.organizer: IMIA (international host) with local hosts EHIS and the Emirates Medical Association. The professional congress organiser is MCI.
candidates.publication: IOS Press Studies in Health Technology and Informatics, open access (MEDINFO 2025 = SHTI vol 329)
candidates.size: 2025 (Taipei): 1,039 submissions and 578 accepted items (277 full papers, 34 student papers, 267 posters). Attendance not found.
candidates.acceptance_rate: 2025: about 56% of all items (578/1,039); the full-paper-only rate is not stated
candidates.rankings: None found in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026
candidates.next_meeting: 21st MEDINFO: Dubai, UAE, 29 Aug-2 Sep 2027, hybrid. IMIA pages give slightly different dates.
candidates.next_deadline: Papers, posters, panels and workshops due 4 Dec 2026; the call opens 2 Nov 2026. The Emerging Tech/AI track is due 2 Apr 2027.
candidates.why_fit: A global health-informatics flagship with a dedicated 'Health Data Science & AI' track and an Agentic AI spotlight.
candidates.concerns: Broad scope, high acceptance, and remote presentation allowed. Only biennial. Informatics rather than ML.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IMIA (WHO NGO partner, IFIP affiliate) flagship, host chosen by the General Assembly, 573 reviewers in 2025, IOS Press proceedings

candidates.full_name: Medical Informatics Europe
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, long-running EFMI society conference. It is informatics-focused with a fairly inclusive acceptance rate (63% for full papers in 2025), so lower tier relative to the catalog's ML venues.
candidates.subtopics: Health informatics, clinical AI, health data spaces, interoperability
candidates.organizer: EFMI (European Federation for Medical Informatics) with ESTMIA (Estonian Medical Informatics Association)
candidates.publication: IOS Press Studies in Health Technology and Informatics (MIE 2025 = SHTI vol 327)
candidates.size: 2025 (Glasgow): over 570 submissions; 230 full papers, 60 short communications and 96 posters accepted
candidates.rankings: None found in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026
candidates.next_meeting: MIE 2027: Tallinn, Estonia, 26-30 Apr 2027
candidates.next_deadline: Full papers (5 pp), short communications and posters: 3 Nov 2026 (extended from 20 Oct). Panels, workshops, tutorials and demos: 26 Jan 2027.
candidates.why_fit: The European society meeting for medical informatics, covering clinical AI, health data spaces and interoperability.
candidates.concerns: 63% full-paper acceptance. Informatics rather than ML focus. Overlaps heavily with MEDINFO; the owner may want at most one of the two. The current deadline is only 3 days away.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Federation of national societies, scientific programme committee and editorial board, IOS Press SHTI proceedings, two-stage decision with resubmission

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, and Health Informatics
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate ACM SIGBio flagship with ACM DL proceedings and selective regular papers (about 19%). It is unranked by ICORE and CCF, mid-tier in reputation, and centred on bioinformatics, which is adjacent to the catalog's healthcare scope.
candidates.subtopics: Bioinformatics, health informatics, biomedical ML and LLMs, health data standards
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGBio (flagship conference)
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings in the ACM Digital Library for regular and short papers. Highlights and posters are presentation-only.
candidates.size: 2025: 170 submissions; 33 regular and 32 short papers published
candidates.acceptance_rate: 2025: about 38% overall (65/170); about 19% for regular papers
candidates.rankings: None found (not in ICORE2026 or CCF 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: 2026 edition (17th): Calabria, Italy, 30 Jun-3 Jul 2026, already past. The 2027 edition has not been announced.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper estimated around late February to early March 2027 (2026: abstract 20 Feb, paper 27 Feb, extended to 8 Mar).
candidates.why_fit: Explicitly spans health informatics, biomedical ML, medical imaging and wearables alongside bioinformatics.
candidates.concerns: No ICORE or CCF rank. Much of the programme is genomics and bioinformatics, which the taxonomy lacks. The 2027 edition is unannounced.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM SIG flagship, double-blind two-phase review, ACM DL proceedings, 17 consecutive editions

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate, with the strongest metrics in this batch (CCF B, h5 31). About half its scope (genomics, protein structure) is bioinformatics, which lies outside the catalog, and the volume is high.
candidates.subtopics: Bioinformatics, medical informatics, biomedical ML, healthcare data mining
candidates.organizer: IEEE; steering committee chaired by Xiaohua Tony Hu (Drexel). 2026 hosted by Texas universities (UTRGV, UNT and others). The TC sponsorship claim was not verified.
candidates.publication: IEEE conference proceedings (IEEE Xplore). Full papers up to 8 pages, IEEE two-column, double-blind.
candidates.size: Unknown. High-volume main track plus many workshops, a poster call and a doctoral forum; counts not verified.
candidates.acceptance_rate: About 19-22% for regular papers (aggregator figure; not verified)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed (checked on the CORE portal). CCF 2026: B (Cross/Comprehensive/Emerging, p.71). GS h5-index 31 (#16 in Bioinformatics & Computational Biology).
candidates.next_meeting: BIBM 2026: 1-4 Dec 2026, Hyatt Regency Dallas, Dallas, TX, USA. 2027 not announced (ieeebibm.org/BIBM2027 returns 404).
candidates.next_deadline: BIBM 2027 full paper, about early July 2027 (estimated from 5 Jul 2026). The 2026 deadline has passed.
candidates.why_fit: A major venue for biomedical and health ML and medical informatics. It complements the tracked IEEE BHI, EMBC, CHIL and MLHC.
candidates.concerns: Very large and partly sequence/structure bioinformatics, adjacent to the catalog rather than central. Not ICORE-ranked. The roughly 19-22% regular-paper acceptance rate is from aggregators and was not verified on official pages. No predatory signals found.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE series running since 2007, with a named steering-committee chair, IEEE Xplore proceedings, CCF B and GS h5 31.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Conference on Healthcare Informatics
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate IEEE health-informatics series with Xplore proceedings and GS h5 19. It is lower tier, though: unranked, with no stable series site, no visible steering committee or sponsoring society, and no 2027 edition announced.
candidates.subtopics: Healthcare informatics, clinical ML, health NLP, human factors, health systems
candidates.organizer: IEEE-branded. 2026 general chairs: Rui Zhang (Univ. of Minnesota) and Cui Tao (Mayo Clinic). Sponsoring society and steering committee are not shown on the edition site.
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings (ICHI 2026 is online). Regular papers 10 pages, short papers 6 pages. Selected papers get a fast-track to the Journal of Healthcare Informatics Research.
candidates.size: Unknown. Three tracks (analytics, human factors, systems) plus posters, demos, industry track, workshops and a doctoral consortium.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed. CCF 2026: not listed. GS h5-index 19.
candidates.cadence: Annual (June). 13th edition 2025 in Calabria; 14th edition 2026 in Minneapolis, 1-3/4 Jun.
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown: no ICHI 2027 site or call found (WikiCFP lists only 2026).
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. The 2026 regular-paper deadline was 7 Feb 2026, with an early round on 29 Sep 2025. No 2027 call found.
candidates.why_fit: Clinical ML and health data analytics; an IEEE peer of the tracked IEEE BHI.
candidates.concerns: Each edition has its own ad hoc site, and the sponsor and steering committee were unverified. WASET 'ICHI'/'ICCHI' look-alikes reportedly exist; check identity by IEEE Xplore and the General Chairs, not by acronym. I could not run name+predatory web searches (search budget exhausted).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 14 consecutive IEEE editions, IEEE Xplore proceedings, a journal fast-track (JHIR), a two-layer single-blind review with senior PC meta-reviews, and h5 19.

candidates.full_name: Medical Image Understanding and Analysis
candidates.verdict_reason: A genuine, society-run community meeting (BMVA, since 1997), the same society that runs the tracked BMVC. It is regional, small and inclusive (historic acceptance 47-97%), so it sits below the MICCAI/MIDL/ISBI tier.
candidates.subtopics: Medical image analysis, computational pathology, clinical imaging AI
