candidates.organizer: BMVA (British Machine Vision Association and Society for Pattern Recognition). A steering committee of past chairs reports to the BMVA Executive and picks hosts by bidding.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS for regular papers (8-15 pp, double-blind). Short abstracts were published by Frontiers in 2024. Best papers are invited to the Annals of the BMVA.
candidates.size: 24-81 LNCS papers per year over 2017-2025 (67 in 2025, in 3 volumes). 53-150 attendees in 2016-2021 (411 virtual in 2020).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed. CCF 2026: not listed. GS h5-index 18.
candidates.cadence: Annual (July). 2024 Manchester, 2025 Leeds, 2026 UCD Dublin (20-22 Jul), 2027 Warwick (31st edition).
candidates.next_meeting: MIUA 2027 (31st): The Oculus, University of Warwick, Coventry, UK. Dates TBA (typically July).
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (LNCS), about March-April 2027 (estimated; 2024 was 15 Apr). The Warwick call for papers says 'coming soon'.
candidates.why_fit: A dedicated medical image analysis community, alongside the tracked MICCAI, MIDL and ISBI.
candidates.concerns: High acceptance rates: 47-49% in 2020-21 and 61-97% in 2016-19 (BMVA table). Mostly UK and Ireland. No 2027 dates. The UCD 2026 site blocked automated access, so the 2026 deadlines were not verified.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Official BMVA conference with a documented steering structure, about 30 editions, and Springer LNCS proceedings since 2017.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Information Processing in Computer-Assisted Interventions
candidates.verdict_reason: A small, selective venue that is clearly well regarded in its community. Its steering committee includes Navab, Taylor, Maier-Hein, Kikinis, Hawkes and Padoy. It has run annually since 2010 and is central to the catalog's imaging and robotics overlap.
candidates.subtopics: Computer-assisted surgery, surgical data science, image-guided interventions, medical robotics
candidates.organizer: IPCAI steering committee (about 22 leading CAI researchers). Held in conjunction with CARS. 2027 general chairs: Goksel, Essert and Hacihaliloglu.
candidates.publication: Regular papers (12 pp) go through a final IJCARS review round and appear in the IPCAI-IJCARS special issue (Springer). Late-breaking long abstracts can become IJCARS short communications.
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: None found (ICORE 2026 and CCF 2026 not listed). Output is indexed as the IJCARS journal, so there is no separate GS h5.
candidates.next_meeting: IPCAI 2027: 28-30 Jun 2027, Langenbeck-Virchow-Haus, Berlin, Germany (with CARS).
candidates.next_deadline: Long abstract (late-breaking or journal-presentation track): 15 Jan 2027. The regular full-paper deadline (30 Oct 2026, PT, no extension) has just passed.
candidates.why_fit: Surgical data science, image-guided interventions and medical robotics: the interventional side of the tracked MICCAI, plus ICRA.
candidates.concerns: The publication route is a journal special issue rather than conference proceedings. No public acceptance rates or ranking. Narrow subfield, and the main 2027 deadline has already closed.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-standing, highly credible steering committee; 17 consecutive editions; publication in IJCARS (Springer); co-location with CARS.

candidates.full_name: Computing in Cardiology
candidates.verdict_reason: Very long-standing, society-run and respected (since 1974; it hosts the PhysioNet/CinC Challenge). Its scope is cardiology-specific, though, and selection is abstract-based and fairly inclusive.
candidates.subtopics: ECG and physiological signal processing, cardiac modeling, clinical ML, PhysioNet Challenge
candidates.organizer: Computing in Cardiology, Inc.: a non-profit international society with an elected board of directors and bylaws, plus local hosts.
candidates.publication: Open-access 'Computing in Cardiology' proceedings (CC-BY since vol. 33, 2006; COPE-based ethics statement). 4-page papers are reviewed and edited after the conference.
candidates.size: 350+ presentations per meeting (official About page)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not listed. CCF 2026: not listed. GS h5-index 20.
candidates.next_meeting: CinC 2027: 19-22 Sep 2027, Auckland, New Zealand (official upcoming-conferences page).
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract, about 15 Apr 2027. The official standing rule is 'no later than April 15' each year; an optional 4-page full paper is due the same date for the YIA. No 2027-specific call yet.
candidates.why_fit: Physiological time series, ECG and cardiac modeling, and a standard benchmark challenge. It sits next to the tracked TS4H, EMBC and BHI.
candidates.concerns: Organ-specific scope. Two-reviewer abstract selection (3 for YIA) is fairly inclusive, and no acceptance rate is published. It is an abstract meeting with post-conference 4-page papers rather than a selective paper venue.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A membership society with an elected board and bylaws, 50+ years of meetings, open-access proceedings under COPE guidelines, and the PhysioNet/CinC Challenge.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and society-run (AAAC; ICORE2026 B; h5 23; 2027 confirmed). Its centre is affective computing and HCI, adjacent to the catalog much like the deferred ICMI, rather than core healthcare.
candidates.subtopics: Affective and physiological sensing, emotion recognition, multimodal behaviour analysis, mental-health sensing
candidates.organizer: AAAC (Association for the Advancement of Affective Computing), with local co-hosts. IEEE Computer Society is a technical co-sponsor.
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore proceedings (IEEE CS technical co-sponsorship stated for 2025).
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: B (checked on the CORE portal). CCF 2026: not listed. GS h5-index 23 ('ACII and Workshops').
candidates.cadence: Annual. 2025 Canberra (13th, Oct); 2026 Puebla (7-10 Sep, with IVA); 2027 Dublin.
candidates.next_meeting: ACII 2027: 1-4 Sep 2027, Dublin City University, Dublin, Ireland (workshops 1 Sep; main conference 2-4 Sep).
candidates.next_deadline: Main-track full paper, about late March to April 2027 (estimated; 2026 was 27 Mar, extended to 24 Apr).
candidates.why_fit: Physiological and affective sensing and multimodal behaviour analysis. It complements the tracked FG and IJCB (Biometrics & Human Sensing).
candidates.concerns: Healthcare overlap is partial (mental-health sensing); the core is HCI and emotion AI. A WASET 'ICACII' look-alike reportedly exists, so verify by AAAC and acii-conf.net. Acceptance rates were not found.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The official conference of the AAAC society (linked to IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing), ICORE B, IEEE Xplore proceedings, and credible keynotes (e.g. Batja Mesquita, Antonia Hamilton in 2026).

candidates.full_name: International Conference of the Biometrics Special Interest Group
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and central to the Biometrics & Human Sensing topic: a long-running European biometrics research meeting backed by EAB, BSI and the IEEE Biometrics Council. It is small but well regarded, the kind of meeting the catalog already accepts.
candidates.subtopics: Biometric recognition, presentation and morphing attack detection, biometric privacy, sample quality
candidates.organizer: GI BIOSIG special interest group with CAST, BSI, EAB, NBL, ATHENE, UniBw München and Fraunhofer IGD; the IEEE Biometrics Council is a technical co-sponsor
candidates.publication: IEEE Xplore (accepted papers are submitted for inclusion). Earlier volumes also appeared in GI LNI (from memory, not re-checked)
candidates.size: 2023: 87 participants, with 18 oral and 15 poster presentations
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026; not in CCF)
candidates.cadence: Annual, at Fraunhofer IGD in Darmstadt (virtual in 2021)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 edition not announced. The 25th edition is 25-26 Nov 2026 in Darmstadt.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper, about Jul-Aug 2027, estimated (the 2026 deadline was extended to 16 Aug 2026)
candidates.why_fit: Its core is biometric recognition, presentation-attack detection and biometric privacy, the same space as the tracked IJCB and FG, seen from Europe.
candidates.concerns: Unranked and single-track. Mostly European, government and industry audience in a fixed location. The 2026 site reported CMT notification problems. Review model and acceptance rate not verified.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Society-run (GI special interest group) with EAB, BSI and IEEE Biometrics Council backing. 2023 keynotes included Arun Ross (MSU) and Google. Hosts the EAB research awards.

candidates.full_name: International Workshop on Biometrics and Forensics
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, EAB-anchored standalone workshop with a credible programme committee and double-blind IEEE-format review. It is workshop-scale, unranked and leans toward forensics and deepfakes, so the scope fit is weaker than BIOSIG's.
candidates.subtopics: Forensic biometrics, presentation-attack and deepfake detection, multimedia forensics, privacy-preserving biometrics
candidates.organizer: EAB SIG Academia (series coordination), with a different host university each year; 2027 host is RMIT
candidates.publication: IEEE proceedings (IEEE eCF copyright; up to 6 pages, double-blind)
candidates.size: Unknown counts. 2026 was a two-day single track with 5 oral sessions, posters and 3 keynotes.
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026; not in CCF)
candidates.cadence: Annual (spring); EAB has fixed hosts through 2028 (Bologna)
candidates.next_meeting: 15th IWBF, 1-2 Apr 2027, RMIT, Melbourne (listed as expected dates)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (up to 6 pages), 15 Jan 2027, listed as expected on the RMIT event page
candidates.why_fit: Forensic biometrics, presentation-attack and deepfake detection, and fairness in biometrics. These overlap the Biometrics & Human Sensing topic.
candidates.concerns: Small, workshop-scale and unranked. About half its scope is multimedia forensics and security rather than ML or health. No 2027 CfP page yet; only expected dates.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: EAB-coordinated series since 2013. 2026 PC chairs: Dantcheva, De Marsico, Marcialis, Peinado. Advisory board includes Evans and Verdoliva. Arun Ross and Christoph Busch chaired sessions.

candidates.full_name: Odyssey: The Speaker and Language Recognition Workshop
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate ISCA event and the reference venue for speaker recognition. But the scope is narrow and biennial, and the next (2028) edition is unannounced, so for now only an estimated entry is possible.
candidates.subtopics: Speaker recognition and verification, language recognition, anti-spoofing, speaker characterization including health
candidates.organizer: ISCA, with the Speaker and Language Characterization (SpLC) SIG
candidates.publication: ISCA Archive proceedings
candidates.size: 52 papers plus 4 keynotes (2026); 44 papers (2024, Quebec)
candidates.rankings: none found (not in ICORE2026; not in CCF); GS h5 not verified
candidates.cadence: Biennial (even years). Editions: 1994 Martigny, 1998 Avignon, 2001 Crete, then roughly every two years (2024 Quebec, 2026 Lisbon).
candidates.next_meeting: 2028 edition not announced. 2026 was Lisbon (IST), 23-26 Jun 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract plus full paper, about mid-March 2028, estimated (2026: abstract 15 Mar, full paper 22 Mar after extensions)
candidates.why_fit: Voice biometrics, anti-spoofing and speaker characterization, with a 2026 special session on speech for healthcare. It comes from the same community as the tracked Interspeech.
candidates.concerns: Narrow, speech-only scope. Small, with gaps of two years or more between editions. The suggested signals-vision family does not fit speech; healthcare plus dynamics-control (signal processing) fits better.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: An official ISCA tutorial and research workshop run with the ISCA SpLC SIG for about 30 years. Proceedings are in the ISCA Archive.

candidates.full_name: IEEE International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-running and ICORE B, with a credible 2027 committee and a confirmed deadline. It is a mid-tier, broad and special-track-heavy venue with unknown selectivity, so it adds coverage more than standing.
candidates.subtopics: Clinical decision support, healthcare ML and foundation models, biomedical image and signal processing, digital health and telemedicine
candidates.organizer: CBMS steering community; 2027 hosted by Università Campus Bio-Medico di Roma (event agency Pragma Congressi); IEEE sponsorship is listed as pending approval
candidates.publication: IEEE conference proceedings (IEEE two-column; regular papers up to 6 pages, short up to 4, posters up to 2), plus a journal special issue
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B; not in CCF (no ccfddl entry); GS h5 not verified
candidates.next_meeting: 40th CBMS, 23-25 Jun 2027, Rome (Università Campus Bio-Medico), in person only
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (regular up to 6 pages), 20 Jan 2027, confirmed on the official 2027 site. The 15 Nov 2026 date is for special-track proposals, not papers.
candidates.why_fit: Its CfP is clinical AI, decision support, biomedical image and signal processing, and digital health. This sits squarely in Healthcare & Clinical AI, at the level of AIME or BHI.
candidates.concerns: Very broad topic list (from bioinformatics to robotics to public health) and many special tracks with their own chairs. Acceptance rate unknown. IEEE sponsorship for 2027 is still pending.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ICORE2026 B and 40 editions. 2027 chairs include Pierre Baldi (UCI) and programme chair Björn Schuller (TUM). Organisers state the IEEE has not yet approved sponsorship.

candidates.full_name: IEEE-EMBS International Conference on Body Sensor Networks
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate EMBS conference and the established wearables-sensing venue. It is ICORE C with 4-page papers, and the 2027 edition is unannounced, so it is lower tier than what the catalog already holds.
candidates.subtopics: Wearable and implantable sensors, physiological signal analysis, digital health, body-area networks
candidates.organizer: IEEE EMBS (the EMBS-hosted BSN site); 2026 organised with FCUP in Porto
candidates.publication: 4-page papers in IEEE proceedings (historically IEEE Xplore). 2025 accepted papers were also posted on OpenReview. The best papers are fast-tracked to IEEE OJEMB.
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 C; not in CCF; GS h5 not verified
candidates.cadence: Annual (Oct-Nov recently: 2025 Los Angeles 3-5 Nov; 2026 Porto 10-12 Oct)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 edition not announced; it is not on the EMBS conference list
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper (4 pages), about mid-June 2027, estimated (2026 deadline: 15 Jun 2026)
candidates.why_fit: Wearable and implantable physiological sensing and its ML. This overlaps Biometrics & Human Sensing and digital health, next to the tracked EMBC and BHI. Signal-processing and time-series work fits dynamics-control better than signals-vision.
candidates.concerns: Small meeting with 4-page papers, partly engineering and hardware oriented. The 2026 page lists conflicting deadline dates. The EMBS conference list does not show 2027.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by IEEE EMBS since 2004, with an IEEE OJEMB fast track. ICORE2026 C.

candidates.full_name: Asia Pacific Bioinformatics Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate (ICORE B, CCF C, running since 2003), but bioinformatics and omics are outside the catalog's eight families, which cover clinical AI, imaging and biometrics. If a bioinformatics line were opened, ISMB or RECOMB should come first.
candidates.subtopics: Bioinformatics, multi-omics, single-cell, structural bioinformatics, precision medicine
candidates.organizer: Annual host institution (2026: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University) within the APBioNet / ISCB Asia-Pacific community
candidates.publication: No proceedings. Accepted papers are invited to journals (2026: TCBB, Briefings in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology and Chemistry, J Microbiol Immunol Infect, JISE). The PC chair may reassign journals.
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE2026 B; CCF C (per ccfddl); GS h5 not verified
candidates.cadence: Annual, rotating across Asia-Pacific (2025 Nanjing; 2026 Hsinchu)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 edition not announced. The 24th APBC was 21-24 Oct 2026 in Hsinchu.
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper, about mid-2027, estimated (2026: 15 Jun, extended twice to 17 Jul 2026)
candidates.why_fit: Only adjacent: computational biology and omics, with some precision-medicine and biomedical-informatics topics.
candidates.concerns: Its core is bio rather than clinical, and there is no bioinformatics topic in the taxonomy. The journal-invitation model mixes strong and weak outlets. Two deadline extensions suggest soft demand. No 2027 information. The APBioNet site lists no upcoming events.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Annual since 2003. ICORE2026 B and CCF C. Credible keynotes in 2026, such as Seiya Imoto (University of Tokyo).

candidates.full_name: Hamlyn Symposium on Medical Robotics
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate and long-running meeting that its community respects, with no predatory signs. Its centre is surgical and medical robotics hardware, which sits next to the catalog's ML, healthcare-AI and neuro core rather than inside it. Papers are only 2 pages and it has no ranking.
candidates.subtopics: Surgical and medical robotics, surgical AI and vision, micro-robotics, clinical translation
candidates.organizer: Helen Hamlyn Centre for Robotic Surgery, Imperial College London. The 2027 edition is run jointly with the Multi-Scale Medical Robotics Center (MRC), an InnoHK centre at CUHK.
candidates.publication: Peer-reviewed 2-page papers go into the Hamlyn Symposium proceedings, self-published by Imperial College London with Crossref DOIs (prefix 10.31256, e.g. 10.31256/hsmr26.xx). There are 14 volumes covering 2010-2026, with no known Scopus or WoS indexing.
candidates.size: 500+ delegates (2024, per the organiser). Crossref holds about 72 DOIs for 2024 and 81 for 2026, so roughly 70-80 registered papers per edition. It started in 2007 with about 50 delegates.
candidates.rankings: None found. The ICORE 2026 portal returned 403, so I could not check it directly; I know of no CORE rank. Not in the CCF lists. No GS h5-index found.
candidates.cadence: Annual since 2007, normally in London in June. 2027 is a joint edition in Hong Kong; 2028 returns to London as the 20th edition.
candidates.next_meeting: 30 May-2 Jun 2027, Hong Kong: workshops at Hong Kong Science Park, symposium at Hyatt Regency Sha Tin. It is timed right after ICRA 2027 in Seoul.
candidates.next_deadline: 14 Jan 2027 (2-page paper; notification 10 Mar 2027, camera-ready 31 Mar 2027)
candidates.why_fit: It is the main specialised meeting for surgical and medical robotics. It links the tracked ICRA and MICCAI communities and includes surgical AI/vision work, so it fits the healthcare family and partly fits rl-control.
candidates.concerns: Papers are 2-page extended abstracts in self-published proceedings with no ranking. The scope is mostly robotics hardware and clinical translation rather than ML or neuroscience. It is centred on one institute (Imperial's Hamlyn Centre), and the programme committee is not public. Note: WebSearch hit its limit, so this rests on official pages and Crossref only.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: It is run by a major university research centre and has 19 editions since 2007. Each paper gets a Crossref DOI under Imperial College London. It grew from about 50 to over 500 delegates. I saw no event-company, guaranteed-Scopus or multi-city warning signs.

candidates.full_name: Cognitive Neuroscience Society Annual Meeting
candidates.verdict_reason: A long-running society meeting that is central to cognitive neuroscience, with confirmed 2027 dates and deadlines. The main caveat is that only members can submit.
candidates.subtopics: cognitive neuroscience; neuroimaging; EEG/MEG; memory, attention, language
candidates.organizer: Cognitive Neuroscience Society
candidates.publication: Poster and symposium abstracts appear in the meeting program only; there are no archival proceedings.
candidates.size: More than 1,500 participants from 30+ countries expected (2027 exhibitor page). The candidate's 'several thousand' claim is overstated.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (a review committee screens poster abstracts)
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting, outside ICORE/CCF scope)
candidates.founded: Society and meeting date from about 1994 (meetings run every year since)
candidates.next_meeting: CNS 2027: Mar 20-23 2027, Boston, MA, USA
candidates.next_deadline: Poster abstract Nov 3 2026, anywhere-on-earth, no extension. Late-breaking posters Dec 8 2026 to Jan 19 2027. Symposia closed Sep 22 2026.
candidates.why_fit: The flagship meeting of cognitive neuroscience, sitting next to OHBM, CCN, CogSci and COSYNE. Identity check passed: this is the Cognitive Neuroscience Society, not OCNS's CNS* (already tracked).
candidates.concerns: Only current members can submit, one first-authored poster each. The poster deadline is 4 days away, and the official page calls the dates 'tentative'. Use a distinct display name so it is not confused with CNS*.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A scholarly society with its own awards, a code of conduct and named committees. The meeting has run annually for about 30 years (2026 Vancouver, 2027 Boston). No predatory signals found.

candidates.full_name: FENS Forum of Neuroscience
candidates.verdict_reason: Europe's largest general neuroscience meeting, run by the federation of European neuroscience societies. The 2028 edition is confirmed and it is a natural counterpart to SfN, which is tracked.
candidates.subtopics: systems, cellular, cognitive and computational neuroscience; neurotechnology
candidates.organizer: Federation of European Neuroscience Societies (FENS), partnered with the British Neuroscience Association for 2028
candidates.publication: Abstracts only (online abstract listing); no archival proceedings.
candidates.size: More than 8,000 international delegates (FENS). 2026 was billed as the largest Forum so far.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting, outside ICORE/CCF scope)
candidates.founded: FENS and the Forum date from 1998
candidates.next_meeting: FENS Forum 2028: Jul 8-12 2028, Glasgow, UK
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract deadline expected in early February 2028. The 2026 regular abstract call closed Feb 5 2026 (not Jan 27 as the candidate stated) and late-breaking abstracts closed Apr 27 2026.
candidates.why_fit: The European flagship general neuroscience meeting, matching SfN Neuroscience (tracked) and filling the catalog's European gap.
candidates.concerns: Very broad neuroscience scope, much of it cellular and molecular rather than computational. The next edition is 20 months away and its abstract deadline is not yet published.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by a federation of national neuroscience societies with a programme committee. It is held every two years and rotates around Europe (2026 Barcelona, 2028 Glasgow).

candidates.full_name: From Neuroscience to Artificially Intelligent Systems (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory meeting)
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL) meeting with open abstract submission. It is the reference NeuroAI meeting, between COSYNE/CCN and NeurIPS, and the 2027 dates and deadline are confirmed. The 'past event' banner is a non-issue.
candidates.subtopics: NeuroAI; brain-inspired architectures; spiking networks; learning algorithms; active perception
candidates.organizer: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Meetings & Courses; organizers Blake Richards, Doris Tsao and Anthony Zador
candidates.publication: CSHL abstract book only; non-archival.
candidates.size: unknown (no attendance figures published)
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown; organizers pick talks from the one-page abstracts
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.next_meeting: NAISys 2027 (4th): Sep 27-Oct 1 2027, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA (hybrid, with virtual packages)
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract (one page) due Jul 9 2027
candidates.why_fit: Directly bridges the neuroscience and ml-ai families, much like CCN and COSYNE.
candidates.concerns: Irregular cadence. Attendance is not published. Presenters are expected to attend in person. The 'You are viewing a past event' text is a hidden template element (class d-none) that appears on every year's page, so it is not a real warning.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Part of the CSHL meetings programme. It is linked to CSHL's NeuroAI Scholars Program, and the organizers are prominent. Editions: 2020, Apr 2022, Sep-Oct 2024, and the 4th in Sep-Oct 2027.

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Society for Mathematical Psychology, joint with the International Conference on Cognitive Modeling
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and long-standing. However, its centre is mathematical psychology rather than the catalog's neuroscience/ML core, the 2027 edition is not announced, and the joint MathPsych-ICCM format only dates from 2020.
candidates.subtopics: computational cognition; cognitive modelling and architectures; Bayesian and statistical models of behaviour
candidates.organizer: Society for Mathematical Psychology (incorporated 1977), jointly with the ICCM steering committee (Taatgen, Lebiere, Laird, van Rijn, Salvucci and others)
candidates.publication: ICCM has peer-reviewed 6-page full papers and 2-page poster papers in open online proceedings. MathPsych itself is abstract-based.
candidates.size: 165 talks and posters at MathPsych/ICCM 2026 (Montreal)
candidates.rankings: none found. The ICORE portal returned 403, so the ICCM rank is unverified.
candidates.cadence: annual (July), plus a separate virtual edition and a satellite at the Psychonomic Society meeting (Psychonomics) in November
candidates.founded: MathPsych meetings since 1968-69; ICCM since about 1996-2000; joint since 2020
candidates.next_meeting: MathPsych/ICCM 2027: dates and location not announced. The 2026 edition was Jul 17-21 2026 in Montreal.
candidates.next_deadline: General submissions (abstract, or ICCM full paper) expected late February 2027. In 2026: symposia Feb 14, general Feb 28, ICCM final papers Mar 13.
candidates.why_fit: The core venue for formal and computational models of cognition, complementing CogSci and CCN (both tracked).
candidates.concerns: Scope sits closer to psychology than to neuroscience. Several same-brand events (virtual MathPsych, Psychonomics satellite, Australian AMPC) need care to track only the main July meeting. The standalone ICCM site is stale (last updated 2023).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A learned society that grew out of the Journal of Mathematical Psychology community. ICCM has a named steering committee of senior cognitive-architecture researchers and peer-reviews its papers.

candidates.full_name: Computational Psychiatry Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, with peer-reviewed abstracts and a credible standing committee. But it is young (since 2023), small (300+), and the 2027 host, dates and deadline are not announced.
candidates.subtopics: computational psychiatry; RL and Bayesian models of mental illness; clinical computational cognition
candidates.organizer: CPC standing committee (Xiaosi Gu, Rick Adams, Sonia Bishop, Tobias Hauser, Quentin Huys, Claire Gillan, Robb Rutledge), with a paid membership; host institutions rotate
candidates.publication: none (abstracts and posters only)
candidates.size: Over 300 attendees in 2025 (official page). The candidate's figure of about 400 is unverified.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.next_meeting: CPC 2027: host, dates and location not announced. The 2026 edition was Jul 14-16 2026 at Yale, New Haven.
candidates.next_deadline: unknown. Symposium and poster abstracts are likely due in early 2027, but the 2026 deadline was not found on the site.
candidates.why_fit: Links the neuroscience and healthcare families through computational modelling; it is the reference meeting of its niche.
candidates.concerns: Young and niche. There is no permanent archive of past editions; the site is rewritten every year. Do not confuse it with the older Zurich Computational Psychiatry Course, which is a course and not a conference.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The committee are leading computational-psychiatry researchers. Abstracts are peer-reviewed through Microsoft CMT. Editions: Dublin 2023, Minneapolis 2024, Tübingen 2025, Yale 2026.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Mathematical Neuroscience
candidates.verdict_reason: A small but well-regarded theory meeting with a 20-member international steering committee and a permanent website (new in Oct 2026). 2027 and 2028 hosts are already fixed, and it fits next to CNS*, Bernstein and Dynamics Days.
candidates.subtopics: mathematical neuroscience; neural dynamics and bifurcations; stochastic and network models; neural field theory
candidates.organizer: ICMNS steering committee (e.g. Avitabile, Montbrió, Roxin, Huguet, Rubin, Khadra, Kirk, Coombes's network), with a host institution each year
candidates.publication: none (abstracts). There have been occasional special issues of the Journal of Mathematical Neuroscience.
candidates.size: More than 150 participants from 25+ countries (Barcelona 2025)
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.founded: 2015 (Juan-les-Pins; founded by Olivier Faugeras, Stephen Coombes and Paul Bressloff)
candidates.next_meeting: ICMNS 2027 (12th): Jun 1-4 2027, Montpellier, France (Inria). ICMNS 2028 will be in Shanghai (SJTU).
candidates.next_deadline: Poster and minisymposium abstracts expected late February 2027 (the 2026 deadline was Feb 28 2026). The 2027 call is not yet published.
candidates.why_fit: A core theory and dynamics venue overlapping the CNS*, Bernstein, AREADNE and Dynamics Days audience.
candidates.concerns: Small. The 2027 call and deadline are not yet posted. Use icmns.org rather than the mailing-list URL in the candidate entry. Beware look-alike 'ICCMN'/'ICMN' listings on aggregator sites.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 11 editions since 2015 (Juan-les-Pins x3, Boulder, Copenhagen, online 2020-22, Dublin, Barcelona, Montreal). Work presented there has appeared in special issues of the Journal of Mathematical Neuroscience, and the 2027 keynotes include Rinzel and Goriely.

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Society for the Neurobiology of Language
candidates.verdict_reason: An established learned-society meeting, held annually since 2009, with peer-reviewed abstracts and a society journal. It fits the neuroscience family well and links to the language family.
candidates.subtopics: neurobiology of language; neuroimaging and EEG/MEG of speech and language; computational and LLM-based models of language in the brain
candidates.organizer: Society for the Neurobiology of Language (founded November 2010; the meetings began as NLC in 2009)
candidates.publication: Peer-reviewed abstracts, searchable on the meeting site. The society journal is Neurobiology of Language (MIT Press; GS h5 29). Nothing is archival.
candidates.size: Over 350 attendees in 2009, 430 in 2010, 450 in 2011 and 400 in 2012. No counts are published for recent years.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (abstracts are peer-reviewed; the rate is not published)
candidates.rankings: Not applicable to ICORE or CCF (0 ICORE hits). The society journal has GS h5 29. None found for the meeting itself.
candidates.cadence: Annual, late September or early October
candidates.next_meeting: SNL 2027: Hong Kong, 24–27 Sep 2027 (official future-meetings page). The 18th meeting was in Geneva, 29 Sep–2 Oct 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract, about late May 2027; in 2026 abstracts were due 26 May (extended) and symposia 25 Mar. The 2027 dates are not posted.
candidates.why_fit: It is the specialist cognitive-neuroscience meeting for language (fMRI, EEG/MEG, lesion work), with growing work on aligning brains and LLMs. It complements CCN, OHBM and CogSci.
candidates.concerns: The first author must be an SNL member. Most work is experimental neuroimaging, not computational, so the link to the NLP family is secondary.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The society has bylaws, an elected board, career and dissertation awards and its own journal. 2026 keynotes included John O'Keefe and Yanchao Bi. There are no predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society
candidates.verdict_reason: Highly legitimate and prestigious, but it is a flagship experimental-psychology meeting. It fits the neuroscience family weakly; its natural neighbour in the catalog is CogSci.
candidates.subtopics: cognitive psychology; memory, attention, perception; psycholinguistics; computational cognition
candidates.organizer: Psychonomic Society (founded 1959; over 4,500 members; publishes seven journals, including Psychonomic Bulletin & Review)
candidates.publication: Abstract book only. Nothing is archival.
candidates.size: About 2,600 attendees and about 1,300 talks and posters per meeting (Wikipedia)
candidates.rankings: Not applicable to ICORE or CCF. None found for the meeting. The flagship journal PB&R has GS h5 56.
candidates.next_meeting: 2026: San Diego, 19–22 Nov (the deadline has passed). 2027: New Orleans, 18–21 Nov. Both are candidate data I could not verify, because the official site blocks automated access with a bot check.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract, about late spring 2027; in 2026 abstracts were reportedly due 1 Jun (unverified).
candidates.why_fit: It is the core venue for cognitive psychology (memory, attention, perception, computational cognition). It complements CogSci and CCN.
candidates.concerns: Submission requires membership or a member sponsor. The scope is psychology more than neuroscience, and acceptance is broadly inclusive for members. None of the edition facts could be verified on the official site.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A long-standing society that publishes seven Springer journals, with a large and stable meeting. There are no predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: Society for NeuroEconomics Annual Meeting
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate: the field's flagship society meeting, held every year since 2003. It is small and niche, a subfield adjacent to the core of the neuroscience family, and 2027 deadlines are not posted.
candidates.subtopics: decision neuroscience; value-based choice; reinforcement-learning models of behaviour; consumer neuroscience
candidates.organizer: Society for NeuroEconomics (secretariat: Podium Conference Specialists)
candidates.publication: Abstract book and programme PDFs on the society site. Nothing is archival.
candidates.size: Small (likely a few hundred); attendance figures are not published. Two satellite symposia (Consumer Neuroscience, Cognitive Economics) run alongside.
candidates.rankings: Not applicable to ICORE or CCF. None found.
candidates.next_meeting: SNE 2027: Sitges, Spain, 9–11 Sep 2027 (official upcoming-meetings page). 2026 was Pasadena, 9–11 Oct.
candidates.next_deadline: Poster and symposium abstracts, about May 2027; the 2026 deadline was reportedly 4 May (not verified on the site). The 2027 call is not posted.
candidates.why_fit: Decision neuroscience and value-based choice, with heavy use of RL and computational models of behaviour. It overlaps with CCN, COSYNE and computational psychiatry.
candidates.concerns: A niche meeting rooted in economics and psychology. Founding details are thin on the site, and the deadline is unverified.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: An unbroken annual series since 2003, alternating between the US and Europe, with an elected board and awards. Abstract books are archived. There are no predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: IBRO World Congress of Neuroscience
candidates.verdict_reason: Fully legitimate: the world federation's flagship congress. But it is held only every four years, its scope is broad and mostly wet-lab, and the abstract deadline is not yet published.
candidates.subtopics: all of neuroscience; global and regional neuroscience
candidates.organizer: International Brain Research Organization (founded 1961). The regional host is the Southern African Neuroscience Society (SANS).
candidates.publication: Abstracts only. Nothing is archival.
candidates.size: About 2,800 participants in Granada 2023 and about 4,400 in Daegu 2019 (Wikipedia). Attendees came from 83 countries in 2023.
candidates.rankings: Not applicable to ICORE or CCF. None found.
candidates.cadence: Every 4 years (2015 Rio, 2019 Daegu, 2023 Granada, 2027 Cape Town)
candidates.founded: Congress series since the 1980s; IBRO founded 1961
candidates.next_meeting: 12th IBRO World Congress: Cape Town (CTICC), South Africa, 13–16 Sep 2027 (official site)
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract: submission opens January 2027, but no deadline is published. The symposium call closed on 7 Aug 2026.
candidates.why_fit: A general neuroscience flagship comparable in kind to SfN (tracked), with a strong global and training remit.
candidates.concerns: Only one edition falls in the planning window. Computational content is a small fraction, and the scope is very broad.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: The scientific programme committee is co-chaired by Arumugam and Josselyn and represents all five IBRO regions. IBRO is the world federation of neuroscience societies.

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Society for Psychophysiological Research
candidates.verdict_reason: Very legitimate: annual since 1959, with a respected society and journal. The fit is a narrow one, with the EEG/ERP and neural-signals subtopic, rather than central computational neuroscience.
candidates.subtopics: EEG/ERP and psychophysiological signals; cognitive and affective neuroscience; signal-processing methods
candidates.organizer: Society for Psychophysiological Research (founded 1960; about 1,000 members)
candidates.publication: Abstracts, historically in a Psychophysiology supplement (Wiley) — not re-verified for 2026. The society journal Psychophysiology has GS h5 58.
candidates.size: About 500–600 attendees: 505 in 2023, 490 in 2022 and 733 in Vienna 2017 (SPR exhibitor page)
candidates.rankings: Not applicable to ICORE or CCF. The journal has GS h5 58. None found for the meeting.
candidates.cadence: Annual, September or October, alternating between North America and Europe
candidates.next_meeting: 67th meeting: Rotterdam (Postillion WTC), Netherlands, 13–16 Oct 2027 (official future-meetings page). The 66th was Halifax, 14–17 Oct 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Symposia about early March 2027 and poster abstracts about late April 2027, estimated from past cycles. Not posted.
candidates.why_fit: The core community for EEG/ERP and peripheral psychophysiology methods. It strengthens the EEG/MEG and neural-signals subtopic.
candidates.concerns: Much of the content is psychological or clinical (autonomic measures), not computational. Submission rules and deadlines could not be confirmed online.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: An unbroken annual series of 66 meetings, a Wiley society journal and methodological guideline papers. There are no predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: ACM International Conference on Neuromorphic Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate archival venue with ACM proceedings, technical co-sponsorship from SIGAI and SIGDA, a credible steering committee, and GS h5 19, the top neuromorphic conference in Scholar Metrics. It is the natural companion to NICE (tracked).
candidates.subtopics: neuromorphic computing; spiking neural networks; brain-inspired hardware, algorithms and software
candidates.organizer: Steering committee: Potok (ORNL), Chen (Duke), Pino (DOE), Payvand (INI Zurich), Aimone (Sandia), Schuman (U Tennessee). Technical co-sponsors: ACM, SIGAI and SIGDA.
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings in the ACM Digital Library: full papers up to 8 pages, short papers up to 4. Open access from 2026.
candidates.size: Small. Accepted-paper and attendance counts are not published on the site.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: not ranked (0 hits). CCF: none found. GS h5-index 19, h5-median 26.
candidates.cadence: Annual, late July or early August (since 2018)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 not announced. The 9th edition was Chicago (Naperville), 4–6 Aug 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Full and short papers, about early April 2027; the 2026 deadline was 8 Apr, with no extension. Not posted.
candidates.why_fit: The main archival venue for neuromorphic computing, spiking networks and brain-inspired hardware, alongside NICE. It matches the catalog's existing neuromorphic subtopic.
candidates.concerns: Not ranked in ICORE. The site is a WordPress page with copy-paste inconsistencies (for example in 2025 dates and venue). Rooted in the US national labs, with modest size; acceptance rate unknown.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM-branded, with a review cycle that includes rebuttal. The steering committee comes from DOE labs and major universities, plus the INI Zurich neuromorphic group. There are no predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: Neural Interfaces Conference (NI 2027)
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate society meeting with a 50-year lineage, central to the BCI and neurotech niche the catalog already covers (BCI Meeting, BCI Winter, IEEE NER), with a confirmed open abstract call.
candidates.subtopics: BCI and neural interfaces; neuroprosthetics; neuromodulation; neural engineering; data/AI for neurotech
candidates.organizer: North American Neuromodulation Society (NANS)
candidates.publication: Not stated on the official page; abstract publication is unknown.
candidates.size: Unknown; the official page gives no attendance figures.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.cadence: Biennial per NANS. A 2023 edition is evidenced; no 2025 edition page was found.
candidates.founded: 1970, as the NIH Neural Prosthesis Workshop
candidates.next_meeting: May 20-22 2027, Arlington, Virginia, USA
candidates.next_deadline: Abstracts (call opens Nov 12 2026) close Feb 17 2027, 1:00 PM CDT. Speaker proposals closed Oct 12 2026.
candidates.why_fit: Topic areas include neuroprosthetics, neural engineering, 'data, AI and systems' and BCI translation, the same community as the tracked BCI Meeting and IEEE NER.
candidates.concerns: Clinical, industry and investor-oriented mix. Abstract review and publication are not documented. Size is unknown. The cadence history is unclear (no 2025 edition found).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by NANS, an established clinical society affiliated with INS. Descends from the 1970 NIH Neural Prosthesis Workshop. The programme is built through an open call for proposals and abstracts.

candidates.full_name: Biennial Meeting of the Society for functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS 20XX)
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and the reference meeting for its modality, but a narrow imaging-method meeting with limited computational/ML centre; the 2028 edition has no city or dates yet.
candidates.subtopics: fNIRS and optical neuroimaging; hyperscanning; fNIRS signal processing and BCI
candidates.organizer: Society for fNIRS (non-profit, elected board)
candidates.publication: Abstract-based meeting; no proceedings or journal tie is documented.
candidates.size: 2010: 149 registrations and 49 abstracts. 2014: 279 registrations and 221 abstracts. Later editions grew; recent figures are unknown.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.cadence: Biennial (even years; online 2021 exception), rotating Americas/Europe/Asia
candidates.founded: First meeting in Boston in 2010; the society was incorporated in 2014.
candidates.next_meeting: fNIRS 2028 in the Americas; city and dates are not announced. The latest edition was Macau, Oct 16-19 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstracts, estimated around Jan-Mar 2028. The 2026 cycle ran from Jan 15 to Mar 31 2026.
candidates.why_fit: Main meeting for a non-invasive neuroimaging modality; analogous to the tracked BIOMAG for MEG, and relevant to BCI and neuroimaging signal processing.
candidates.concerns: Narrow, single-modality scope and mostly experimental/clinical work. Size and abstract publication are undocumented. The 2028 host is not announced.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Society-run with an elected board, standing committees, an open-science/standardization committee and a 16-year meeting history (Boston, London, Montreal, Paris, Tokyo, Boston, Birmingham, Macau).

candidates.full_name: ISMRM & ISMRT Annual Meeting & Exhibition
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier and unquestionably legitimate, but the core scope is MR physics, acquisition and clinical MRI, so neuroscience and ML are only a part of it; the 2027 call has already closed.
candidates.subtopics: MRI physics and methods; image reconstruction and ML for MR; neuroimaging acquisition and analysis
candidates.organizer: International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (with ISMRT)
candidates.publication: Peer-reviewed abstracts (750 words, up to 5 figures), reviewed by an AMPC-appointed panel, are published in the electronic ISMRM Proceedings.
candidates.size: 5,000+ in-person attendees annually, per ismrm.org.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.founded: Current society formed in 1994 from predecessor societies with meetings since the early 1980s (from memory; unverified this session).
candidates.next_meeting: May 8-13 2027, Vancouver. Then May 13-18 2028 in Copenhagen (joint with ESMRMB) and May 5-10 2029 in Montreal.
candidates.next_deadline: The 2027 abstract window (Oct 1-28 2026) is closed. The next main call is the 2028 Copenhagen abstracts, estimated around late Oct or early Nov 2027.
candidates.why_fit: A major venue for neuroimaging methods and ML-based MR reconstruction; overlaps with the tracked MICCAI, ISBI and OHBM.
candidates.concerns: Mostly physics, engineering and clinical; computational neuroscience is peripheral. Very large and expensive. The 2027 deadline already passed (confirmed Oct 28 2026), so the first actionable cycle is 2028.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Large international society with 38 study groups, 20+ chapters and 65+ countries. It owns journals (MRM, JMRI) and runs formal peer review of abstracts by expert reviewers.

candidates.full_name: Neuroadaptive Technology Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Not predatory, and has real peer review, but it is lab-centred, industry-flavoured and irregular, with no next edition announced. Defer until one is announced, or treat as a weak 'consider'.
candidates.subtopics: passive BCI; neuroadaptive and physiological/affective computing; neurofeedback; neuroergonomics
candidates.organizer: Society for Neuroadaptive Technology. Chairs are Thorsten O. Zander (BTU Cottbus / Zander Labs) and Stephen Fairclough (LJMU).
candidates.publication: Peer-reviewed short (2-page) and full (6-page) papers via CMT. Proceedings are on a university repository (opus4.kobv.de, BTU) with a DOI.
candidates.size: Unknown; small, single-track. Day 3 is a public, industry-translation day.
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.cadence: Irregular; nominally biennial, but 2025 and 2026 were consecutive.
candidates.founded: 2017, per a venue image on the NAT'25 page; editions in 2019, 2022, 2025 and 2026.
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown; not announced. The last edition was NAT'26, Weizenbaum Institute, Berlin, Apr 22-24 2026.
candidates.next_deadline: unknown (NAT'26 papers were due Feb 28 2026 after two extensions)
candidates.why_fit: Small, focused passive-BCI/neuroadaptive meeting, adjacent to the tracked BCI Meeting and BCI Winter.
candidates.concerns: The 'society' is essentially the organising lab. No independent programme or steering committee is listed. The meeting is tied to a company (Zander Labs). Fees are high (EUR 500-900), deadlines were repeatedly extended, the cadence is irregular and there is no announced next edition.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Peer review via CMT, credible keynotes (for example Grosse-Wentrup, Zuidema, Bach) and published proceedings. The organisers are known passive-BCI researchers.

candidates.full_name: Conference of the European Society for Cognitive Psychology (25th ESCoP)
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, long-running society conference with confirmed 2027 deadlines, but mainly experimental cognitive psychology, so it is adjacent to the catalog's computational and neuro core (closest tracked analogue: CogSci).
candidates.subtopics: cognitive psychology; memory, attention, language, decision making; cognitive neuroscience
candidates.organizer: European Society for Cognitive Psychology (publishes Journal of Cognition)
candidates.publication: Abstract-based; no proceedings documented. The society journal is Journal of Cognition.
candidates.size: Unknown; official pages give no attendance figures.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting)
candidates.founded: Society around 1985 (from memory; unverified). 25 numbered conferences, in odd years.
candidates.next_meeting: Aug 30-Sep 4 2027, Babes-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania
candidates.next_deadline: Individual abstracts (talks, blitz talks, posters): Jan 15-Mar 15 2027. Symposium proposals: Oct 15-Nov 30 2026.
candidates.why_fit: The European cognitive-psychology society meeting; overlaps the cognitive side of the tracked CogSci and CCN.
candidates.concerns: Psychology-heavy, with little computational modelling or ML focus. Size is undocumented. The founding year was not verified on the official site.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Pan-European scientific society with an owned open-access journal, summer schools and awards, and a numbered conference series in rotating European universities (Porto 2023, then Cluj 2027).

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Brain Informatics
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate academic series since 2006, archival and on-topic (AI meets brain data), but low tier: no ranking verified, small, hybrid and with extended deadlines. Comparable to the tracked IDEAL and ADMA.
candidates.subtopics: brain informatics; ML for neuroimaging and EEG; brain-inspired AI
candidates.organizer: Web Intelligence Consortium (WIC); co-located with IEEE/WIC WI-IAT
candidates.publication: Springer LNAI (Brain Informatics subseries). Top papers are invited to the Brain Informatics journal (Springer OA).
candidates.size: Unknown; accepted-paper counts are not published on the official pages.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: could not verify (portal returned 403); not known to be ranked. No CCF 2026 entry known. GS h5 unknown.
candidates.founded: 2006 (as WImBI). Annual since 2009; called Brain Informatics and Health from 2013 to 2016.
candidates.next_meeting: BI 2026: Dec 3-6 2026, Brisbane (hybrid, with WI-IAT). The BI 2027 venue and dates are unknown.
candidates.next_deadline: Full papers for BI 2027, estimated around July-Aug 2027. BI 2026 papers were due Jul 15 2026 (extended); BI 2025, Aug 20 2025.
candidates.why_fit: An archival venue at the intersection of ML/AI and brain data, the overlap of the catalog's neuroscience and ML families.
candidates.concerns: Low-tier. The organizing committee is not named on the official pages. Hybrid format, extended deadlines and promotional framing. LNAI alone is not quality evidence, and a ranking was not confirmed.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: 20-year history across Asia, Europe and North America, with peer-reviewed LNAI proceedings, an associated journal and credible keynotes (2026: Brassard, Minmin Luo, Pankaj Sah).

candidates.full_name: Annual Meeting of the Japan Neuroscience Society (50th Annual Meeting, Neuroscience 2027, with the 4th CJK International Neuroscience Meeting)
candidates.verdict_reason: A genuine, long-running national society meeting with English abstracts and an open abstract route. It is a regional, SfN-style broad meeting weighted toward cellular and molecular work, and presenting requires society membership, so it fits less centrally than COSYNE, CNS* or Bernstein.
candidates.subtopics: Systems, cellular, molecular and computational neuroscience; neurochemistry and neural networks in joint NEURO years
candidates.organizer: Japan Neuroscience Society (founded 1974 as the Japan Neuroscience Association, about 6,100 members); the secretariat is a professional organiser, A&E Planning
candidates.publication: Abstract book only (online abstract search). The society journal, Neuroscience Research (Elsevier), is separate and not proceedings.
candidates.size: Attendance not published on the pages checked. The society has about 6,100 members and the 2026 site reports only 'a large number of attendees'.
candidates.rankings: none found (abstract meeting; not ICORE/CCF-ranked)
candidates.cadence: Annual (July/August); some years it runs jointly as NEURO20xx with the Japanese Society for Neurochemistry and the Japanese Neural Network Society (e.g. 2022, 2024, 2026)
candidates.next_meeting: July 20-23, 2027, Makuhari Messe, Chiba, Japan (50th anniversary, joint with the 4th CJK International Neuroscience Meeting)
candidates.next_deadline: General abstract, estimated early-to-mid February 2027 (2026 ran Dec 1, 2025 to Feb 5, 2026, later extended; 2025 closed Feb 14). The symposium call (Aug 3 to Oct 8, 2026) is an organiser proposal, not a contribution route.
candidates.why_fit: Asia-Pacific flagship neuroscience meeting, comparable in style to SfN or FENS, with English abstracts, talks and posters. Joint years with JNNS add computational and neural-network content.
candidates.concerns: The first author must be a member of JNS (or JSN/JNNS in joint years) and must register before submitting. The meeting is Japan-centred and broad, weighted toward cellular and molecular work. The 2027 abstract call is not yet posted. The web search budget ran out, so attendance figures could not be checked.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A national scientific society publishing an Elsevier journal. Plenary speakers for 2027 include Gord Fishell, Viviana Gradinaru, Kelsey Martin and Marco Prinz. The programme committee selects abstracts (rejections possible), and presentations are in English.

candidates.full_name: Graz Brain-Computer Interface Conference (10th edition 2026; successor 'European BCI Conference 2028' unconfirmed)
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and well regarded in the BCI community (affiliated event of the International BCI Society, strong international programme committee). But the 2026 edition has passed and neither TU Graz nor the BCI Society announces any next edition or successor, so treat it as a watchlist item rather than an addition now.
candidates.subtopics: EEG- and invasive BCI, neurofeedback, neuroprosthetics, passive BCI, neural engineering
candidates.organizer: Institute of Neural Engineering, TU Graz (chair Gernot Müller-Putz); affiliated/partnered event of the International BCI Society
candidates.publication: Open-access proceedings with per-contribution DOIs from Verlag der TU Graz (e.g. GBCIC2024: doi:10.3217/978-3-85125-682-6)
candidates.size: 2026: 80 posters in three sessions plus talks and 5 keynotes. The '190+ participants / 100+ papers' figure is from a secondary source and was not verified.
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.founded: Before 2006 (3rd edition held in 2006); the Graz BCI lab dates back about 35 years
candidates.next_meeting: unknown. The 10th edition ran Sep 14-17, 2026 in Graz (TU Graz, Petersgasse 16). No 11th edition or successor appears on official pages as of 2026-10-31.
candidates.next_deadline: unknown (no next edition announced; the submission format for short or extended-abstract papers was not visible on official pages)
candidates.why_fit: Europe's main dedicated BCI and neurotechnology meeting, a natural complement to the tracked International BCI Meeting, BCI Winter and IEEE NER, in the catalog's standalone-meeting style.
candidates.concerns: No scheduled next edition. The reported successor (European BCI Conference 2028) is unconfirmed by TU Graz or BCI Society pages. Cadence is irregular and the meeting is single-institution hosted. The topic overlaps with already tracked BCI venues. The web search budget ran out before the successor claim could be checked further.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: International programme committee and review board includes Krusienski, Collinger, Lotte, Tangermann, Grosse-Wentrup, Vaughan, Mattia, Congedo and Coyle. It is listed on the BCI Society's events page, offers BCI Society member fees and has industry exhibitors. Proceedings are DOI-registered with the university press.

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Equity and Access in Algorithms, Mechanisms, and Optimization
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate ACM venue that is central to fairness and equity. It is young, unranked and small (32 papers in 2025, half non-archival), it leans towards economics and operations research, and its 2027 host is not yet chosen.
candidates.subtopics: Algorithmic fairness, mechanism design for social good, equity and access, policy
candidates.organizer: EAAMO organization, which grew out of MD4SG. It is an ACM-branded conference with proceedings in the ACM Digital Library; ACM and SIGAI were among the 2026 sponsors, and LMU Munich hosts 2026.
candidates.publication: ACM Digital Library proceedings for archival papers (camera-ready up to 14 pages); a non-archival option is also offered
candidates.size: 2025: 32 accepted papers across 5 tracks (16 archival, 16 non-archival), plus posters; attendance unknown
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE 2026 (portal search returned no match), not in CCF; Scholar h5 not checked
candidates.founded: 2021 (virtual); then Arlington 2022, Boston 2023, San Luis Potosí 2024, Pittsburgh 2025
candidates.next_meeting: Nov 5-7, 2026 at LMU Munich (6th edition). 2027 dates and host are not announced; a call for host proposals is open.
candidates.next_deadline: EAAMO 2027 full paper, about mid-May 2027 (estimated; in 2026 the abstract was due May 8 and the paper May 15)
candidates.why_fit: Close sibling of FAccT and AIES, adding mechanism-design and optimization angles on fairness and access
candidates.concerns: Small and young with no ranking; half the programme is non-archival; scope is economics/OR-heavy; 2027 host and dates are unknown, so the deadline is an estimate
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM DL proceedings, OpenReview double-blind review, six named tracks; accepted authors include Kleinberg, Procaccia and Abebe; no predatory signals

candidates.full_name: Symposium on Foundations of Responsible Computing
candidates.verdict_reason: A small but clearly well-regarded theory venue for fairness and privacy. Its steering committee is top tier, it has published LIPIcs proceedings since 2020, and its deadlines are confirmed.
candidates.subtopics: Theory of fairness, privacy, accountability and society-facing algorithms
candidates.organizer: FORC steering committee co-chaired by Katrina Ligett and Aaron Roth (members include Dwork, Kleinberg, Goldwasser, Vadhan, Reingold and Pitassi). 2026 was supported by the Simons Collaboration on the Theory of Algorithmic Fairness.
candidates.publication: LIPIcs (Dagstuhl) proceedings: 10-page papers, or a 1-page abstract that links to the full paper; plus a non-archival highlights track
candidates.size: About 25 archival papers a year (LIPIcs vols 329 and 368 have 26-27 entries including front matter); registration was free in 2026; attendance unknown
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE 2026 or CCF; Scholar h5 not checked
candidates.next_meeting: Jun 2-4, 2027 at Stanford University
candidates.next_deadline: Nov 11, 2026 full paper (cycle 1); Feb 17, 2027 full paper (cycle 2) and highlights nominations
candidates.why_fit: The theory home for fairness and privacy, complementing FAccT/AIES and close to the COLT community already tracked
candidates.concerns: Small and theory-only, with no ICORE or CCF rank. Its two submission cycles need two deadline entries, and authors may publish only a 1-page abstract.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Its steering committee includes the founders of differential privacy and of algorithmic fairness theory; proceedings in LIPIcs since 2020; hosted by Harvard (2026) and Stanford (2027)

candidates.full_name: Privacy Enhancing Technologies Symposium (proceedings: PoPETs)
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier and unquestionably legitimate, but its central scope is privacy and security systems broadly, with ML only a part. Its four journal-style deadlines a year also fit the single-deadline model poorly.
candidates.subtopics: Privacy-enhancing technologies, differential privacy, ML privacy attacks and defences, anonymity, usable privacy
candidates.organizer: PETS/PoPETs community with an advisory board; self-published since 2022
candidates.publication: Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PoPETs), an open-access journal-style proceedings with no APC or submission fees
candidates.size: PETS 2026: 160 accepted papers across four issues (30/34/39/57); attendance unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A; CCF C (via ccfddl, not checked against an official 2026 list); Scholar h5 56 (Security & Cryptography, ranked 13th)
candidates.cadence: annual symposium (July), four submission deadlines a year
candidates.founded: 2000 as a workshop; now a symposium with PoPETs journal-style proceedings
candidates.next_meeting: Jul 19-24, 2027, Delft, Netherlands
candidates.next_deadline: Nov 30, 2026 full paper (PoPETs 2027 Issue 3); then Feb 28, 2027 (Issue 4)
candidates.why_fit: The premier privacy venue, covering the privacy-preserving ML and differential privacy subtopics next to SaTML
candidates.concerns: Its quarterly, journal-like deadlines strain the one-deadline schema. Most of the programme is non-ML (Tor, censorship, usable privacy). It is only CCF C.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ICORE A, Scholar h5 56, a 25-year history, an open-access model without fees, and a large accepted-paper count

candidates.full_name: European Conference on Algorithmic Fairness (European Workshop on Algorithmic Fairness, EWAF, until 2025)
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, association-run European fairness meeting of about 200 people, with PMLR proceedings. It is young, unranked and interdisciplinary (law and philosophy), and its 2027 deadline is still TBA.
candidates.subtopics: Algorithmic fairness, EU regulation, interdisciplinary responsible AI
candidates.organizer: European Association for Algorithmic Fairness (EAAF), a Swiss non-profit founded in 2023. Its elected board is led by president Christoph Heitz and includes Pechenizkiy, Zehlike, Weerts, Fabris, Hertweck and Cerrato.
candidates.publication: A PMLR volume for archival full papers (up to 15 pages) and extended abstracts; a non-archival option; OpenReview submission
candidates.size: About 200 participants expected for 2027 (EAAF host call); 2026 had several oral and spotlight sessions plus posters; paper count unknown
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE 2026 or CCF; Scholar h5 not checked
candidates.founded: 2022 as EWAF (Winterthur 2023, Mainz 2024, Eindhoven 2025); renamed ECAF for Ghent 2026
candidates.next_meeting: Aug 25-27, 2027, Vilnius, Lithuania (6th edition)
candidates.next_deadline: ECAF 2027 full paper or extended abstract: TBA on the official page; about late April 2027 by analogy (2026 deadline Apr 30, extended from Apr 17)
candidates.why_fit: The European community meeting for algorithmic fairness, complementing FAccT for EU and regulatory work
candidates.concerns: Young and unranked. It still calls its own proceedings 'workshop proceedings', and the 2026 rename means the series key and UID need care. Part of the programme is non-technical (law, philosophy). The 2027 deadline is not yet posted.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by a non-profit association with bylaws and an elected board of active fairness researchers; PMLR proceedings; competitive open host calls; no predatory signals

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
candidates.verdict_reason: A long-running, well-ranked ACM venue (ICORE A, h5 50, about 113 papers) at the intersection of AI and HCI, covering human-AI interaction and explainability. It was deferred earlier for focus reasons, not quality.
candidates.subtopics: Human-AI interaction, explainable and interactive ML, human-centred AI, LLM-based interfaces
candidates.organizer: ACM IUI steering committee; an ACM conference following SIGCHI policies (historically sponsored by SIGCHI with SIGAI)
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings in the ACM Digital Library (open access from 2026)
candidates.size: IUI 2026: 113 accepted papers listed; attendance unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A; CCF B (via ccfddl, not checked against an official 2026 list); Scholar h5 50 (Human Computer Interaction, ranked 16th)
candidates.cadence: annual; the month moves (Mar 2023-25, Jul 2026, Feb 2027)
candidates.next_meeting: Feb 8-11, 2027, Helsinki, Finland
candidates.next_deadline: The IUI 2028 full-paper deadline is unknown. The IUI 2027 paper cycle closed Aug 20, 2026; IUI 2027 posters and demos are due Nov 10, 2026.
candidates.why_fit: The core venue for human-AI interaction and explainable or interactive ML; complements CHI, which is already under responsible-ai
candidates.concerns: Previously deferred, as HCI was outside the current research focus. Its scope is broader than responsible AI. The schedule is unstable (July 2026, then February 2027), so the next main deadline cannot be estimated reliably.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ICORE A, Scholar h5 50, 30+ years of ACM history, and a steering committee with a test-of-time award

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Hybrid Human-Artificial Intelligence
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, with a credible European steering committee and IOS Press proceedings. It is small and lower tier, though: about 31 main-track papers, overall acceptance of 34-50%, falling submissions, and no ranking.
candidates.subtopics: Human-AI collaboration, hybrid intelligence, human-centred and responsible AI, ethics
candidates.organizer: HHAI steering committee (van Harmelen, Jonker, Shawe-Taylor, Lukowicz, Dignum, Tiddi and others) plus an executive committee chaired by Janin Koch; rooted in the European hybrid-intelligence community
candidates.publication: IOS Press, Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications (FAIA), open access under CC BY-NC
candidates.size: 2024: 31 of 62 main-track submissions accepted (9 of 29 full papers); 2022-2023: 33-34 papers; no figures posted for 2025-26
candidates.acceptance_rate: Full papers 31-41%, all main-track papers 34-50% (2022-2024, official stats page)
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE 2026 (only the unrelated HAIS and HIS match) or CCF; a Scholar h5 of about 13 was claimed but not verified
candidates.founded: 2022 (Amsterdam), then Munich, Malmö, Pisa and Brussels (2026)
candidates.next_meeting: Jun 14-18, 2027, University of Oulu, Finland (6th edition)
candidates.next_deadline: Jan 21, 2027 abstract; Jan 28, 2027 full paper (blue-sky and working papers on the same dates)
candidates.why_fit: A European meeting on human-AI collaboration and human-centred, responsible AI
candidates.concerns: Small, with submissions falling (96, 78, 62 in 2022-24) and a high acceptance rate. It is unranked. The 2027 call still says 'Fifth' conference (a template slip). Its scope is adjacent to, not central to, fairness and accountability.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Senior steering committee, double-blind review with at least 3 reviewers, published acceptance statistics, and FAIA proceedings; no predatory signals

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Human-AI Complementarity and Alignment (HCOMP; formerly the AAAI Conference on Human Computation and Crowdsourcing)
candidates.verdict_reason: It is legitimate, long-running and ICORE B. It is also changing: it moved from AAAI to ACM in 2026 and was renamed, the official list shows no 2025 edition, and the 2027 dates are not out yet. Reassess once the 2027 call for papers is posted.
candidates.subtopics: Crowdsourcing, human-AI complementarity and alignment, human-in-the-loop ML, data labelling
candidates.organizer: ACM (2026 sponsors include SIGCHI and SIGWEB); the series ran as an AAAI conference from 2013 to 2024
candidates.publication: Archival full papers in the ACM Digital Library, with DOIs, since 2026; AAAI proceedings 2013-2024. Talks, posters and demos are non-archival.
candidates.size: Unknown. In 2026 it was held jointly with ACM Collective Intelligence, Sep 27-30, 2026, near Washington DC.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 B (listed under its old AAAI name); not found in CCF; Google Scholar h5 not found
candidates.founded: 2013 as a conference (workshops at KDD and AAAI 2009-2012)
candidates.next_meeting: September 2027, Azabudai Hills, Tokyo, Japan (exact dates to be announced)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper, around early to mid June 2027 (estimated from 2026: abstracts Jun 8, papers Jun 15)
candidates.why_fit: Human-in-the-loop ML, crowdsourcing and, under the new name, human-AI alignment. It sits next to CHI, FAccT and AIES.
candidates.concerns: humancomputation.com is on registrar clientHold, so it no longer resolves. Use hcomp.acm.org. The ICORE B rank was given under the AAAI name. The scope leans HCI, much like the deferred IUI and CSCW.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Twelve AAAI editions with AAAI-published proceedings. Now ACM, sponsored by SIGCHI and SIGWEB with NSF support. Double-blind review with three external reviewers plus a meta-review. Keynote by Diyi Yang (Stanford).

candidates.full_name: World Conference on eXplainable Artificial Intelligence
candidates.verdict_reason: The steering committee includes credible XAI researchers. Against that, it is young (2023), unranked, publishes in Springer CCIS (a lower-tier series) and has a modest h5 of 14. Its scope is central to explainability.
candidates.subtopics: Explainability, interpretability, neuro-symbolic XAI, evaluating XAI
candidates.organizer: Founder-led steering committee (L. Longo, S. Lapuschkin, G. Montavon, C. Seifert, R. Guidotti, P. Giudici, S. Barbon Junior); no sponsoring society
candidates.publication: Springer CCIS for main-track and special-session papers; CEUR-WS for late-breaking work, demos and the doctoral consortium
candidates.size: About 95 papers per edition according to Springer's listing (95 in 2023, 95 in 2024, 96 in 2025), in 3-5 CCIS volumes
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026: none found; CCF: none found; Google Scholar h5 14 (h5-median 20)
candidates.next_meeting: 5th edition, Jul 7-9, 2027, Bari, Italy
candidates.next_deadline: Full or short paper, Feb 1, 2027 AoE (EasyChair opens Jan 15)
candidates.why_fit: The only standalone conference devoted to XAI and interpretability. It is close to the responsible-AI and ML families.
candidates.concerns: No society behind it, many special sessions, CCIS proceedings and a review window of about one month. The 2027 dates page lists 'April 31' (an invalid date). Searches for predatory flags were not run because the web search budget was used up.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Recognised XAI researchers on the steering committee and as PC chairs (Ceci, Kampffmeyer, Choi). Four editions so far, with Springer-indexed proceedings.

candidates.full_name: IASEAI Conference of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate nonprofit with prominent founders and peer-reviewed papers that will appear in AAAI Press proceedings. It is very young (2025), mixes policy with research, and has no ranking.
candidates.subtopics: AI safety, ethics, governance and policy
candidates.organizer: International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, a nonprofit incorporated in Nov 2024 (officers: Banifatemi, Nitzberg, Stuart Russell)
candidates.publication: Optional archival track: the IASEAI'27 Proceedings from AAAI Press. Non-archival papers and talks are presentation-only.
candidates.size: About 700 in person (65 countries) and 1,400 online in 2025; paper counts unknown
candidates.rankings: none found
candidates.next_meeting: 3rd edition, Feb 9-12, 2027 (main conference Feb 9-10, workshops Feb 11-12), UNESCO House, Paris
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper for IASEAI'28, around early October 2027 (estimated). The 2027 paper deadline (Oct 5, 2026) has passed; only non-research talk proposals stay open, until Jan 8, 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Central to AI safety, ethics and governance, alongside AIES and FAccT
candidates.concerns: Policy-heavy with many invited talks. Attendance goes through statements of interest and invitations. Only two editions so far, and the 2026 proceedings were not verified.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Double-blind review on OpenReview, AAAI Press proceedings and a funding-disclosure policy. Invited speakers have included Geoffrey Hinton and Anca Dragan.

candidates.full_name: ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate ACM symposium with a strong steering committee. It is small and unranked, and its scope is CS and law broadly rather than AI.
candidates.subtopics: AI governance, the law of algorithms, privacy law, technical accountability
candidates.organizer: ACM symposium; steering committee includes Joan Feigenbaum, Daniel Weitzner, Jon Crowcroft and Christopher Yoo
candidates.publication: ACM Digital Library proceedings (open via OpenTOC). Archival full papers; non-archival papers appear only as a one-page summary.
candidates.size: 2026: 20 archival papers, 9 non-archival papers and 39 posters
candidates.rankings: none found (no ICORE 2026 or Scholar match)
candidates.next_meeting: 6th edition, Mar 23-25, 2027, Northwestern University (downtown campus), Chicago
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper for 2028, around October 2027 (estimated; the 2027 deadline was Oct 20, 2026). One-page poster summaries for 2027 are due Feb 9, 2027 (confirmed).
candidates.why_fit: Matches the governance and accountability subtopic: technical work on privacy, algorithms and the law
candidates.concerns: Most content is law and policy rather than ML. Small, with no rank or acceptance rate published. Presenting in person is mandatory.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM-published proceedings and senior CS and law scholars on the steering committee and as PC chairs (Kobbi Nissim, Aniket Kesari)

candidates.full_name: Theory and Practice of Differential Privacy
candidates.verdict_reason: The leading community meeting on differential privacy, with a strong steering committee and long history. It is a non-archival abstract workshop whose fit is limited to the privacy subtopic, and the 2027 edition has not been announced.
candidates.subtopics: Differential privacy, private ML, synthetic data
candidates.organizer: Steering committee of Kamath, McMillan, Nikolov, Slavkovic and Ullman, linked to the Journal of Privacy and Confidentiality
candidates.publication: None (no formal proceedings). Selected papers are invited to a special issue of the Journal of Privacy and Confidentiality.
candidates.size: About 106 accepted abstracts plus 16 contributed talks (2025); about 139 listed entries (2026)
candidates.rankings: none found (non-archival)
candidates.founded: 2015 (co-located with ETAPS); later with CCS and ICML; standalone since 2023
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown. Not announced; probably June 2027. 2026 was Jun 1-2 in Boston at Northeastern, co-located with FORC.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract of up to 4 pages, not anonymised, around February-March 2027 (estimated; Feb 18 in 2026, Mar 20 in 2025)
candidates.why_fit: An established standalone meeting on private ML and data, in the same style as TS4H or AALTD
candidates.concerns: Light review and non-archival. DP theory is only partly ML or responsible AI. The co-located FORC (Foundations of Responsible Computing) may fit the family better.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by leading DP researchers, with JPC special issues since 2015 and hosts such as Google and Northeastern

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing
candidates.verdict_reason: A top-tier, clearly legitimate ACM SIGCHI venue. Its scope is broad HCI, and the journal-first rolling submission model fits the calendar's deadline model poorly. It was previously deferred.
candidates.subtopics: Social computing, algorithmic harms, human-AI collaboration, future of work
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGCHI
candidates.publication: Papers in PACM HCI (CSCW track, open access); posters in the ACM DL companion proceedings
candidates.size: Large; paper counts not checked. PACM HCI h5 is 88.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A; CCF A (per ccfddl); Google Scholar h5 27 for the companion proceedings and 88 for PACM HCI
candidates.next_meeting: 30th edition, Oct 16-20, 2027, Philadelphia
candidates.next_deadline: No fixed paper deadline: rolling PACM HCI submissions are open now. Posters estimated around mid-May 2027 (May 15 in 2026).
candidates.why_fit: Strong work on algorithmic harms, fairness and human-AI collaboration, much like CHI, which the catalog tags responsible-ai
candidates.concerns: Previously deferred. The scope is mostly HCI and social computing. Rolling submissions give no single cut-off; only posters have a clear deadline.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Flagship ACM SIGCHI conference. Review is tiered (SPC, PC and two external reviewers) with revise-and-resubmit, and papers appear in PACM HCI.

candidates.full_name: International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media
candidates.verdict_reason: Long-running AAAI conference with an A rank and h5 59. It sits between the tracked WWW, NetSci/CCS and FAccT/AIES. Its one weakness is that it is only partly about AI, which is why it was deferred before.
candidates.subtopics: Social media analysis, misinformation, online harms, computational social science, datasets
candidates.organizer: AAAI, with a large community steering committee. The 2027 general chairs are Björn Ross and Walid Magdy.
candidates.publication: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (AAAI Press, open access). The Social Science track publishes abstracts only.
candidates.size: Accepted-paper counts not verified. The official site gives a full-paper acceptance rate of about 20-30%.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A (verified on the CORE portal); CCF B (per ccfddl's CCF data); GS h5-index 59 (verified)
candidates.cadence: Annual (late May/June), with three rolling full-paper rounds a year (May, September, January)
candidates.next_meeting: 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland; dates not yet announced ('coming soon')
candidates.next_deadline: 15 Jan 2027 (AoE): the 3rd full-paper round, also the only round for posters, demos and dataset papers
