candidates.why_fit: Covers computational social science, misinformation, online harms and platform auditing. That overlaps the tracked WWW, NetSci and the responsible-AI venues.
candidates.concerns: Previously deferred (previously_deferred=true) as outside the research focus. It has several deadlines a year, and much of its work is social science rather than ML.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: AAAI-sponsored, with a named 36-member steering committee and AAAI Press proceedings. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security
candidates.verdict_reason: Highly regarded (ICORE A, about 20% acceptance), but its core is the human factors of security and privacy. Little of its work is AI or ML, so it falls outside this catalog's scope.
candidates.subtopics: Usable security, privacy user studies, authentication, privacy attitudes
candidates.organizer: USENIX, with a SOUPS steering committee. The 2026 edition was run from soups.page.
candidates.publication: USENIX open-access proceedings
candidates.size: About 30-37 full papers a year (30/157 in 2025)
candidates.acceptance_rate: 19.1% (30/157) in 2025; 21-28% in 2021-2024 (from ccfddl, citing USENIX chairs' messages)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A (verified); CCF C (per ccfddl); GS h5-index 35 (verified)
candidates.cadence: Annual (August), usually co-located with or near USENIX Security

candidates.concerns: Mostly non-ML. If a security or privacy slice were wanted, SaTML (already tracked) or the security flagships come first. No 2027 details on any official page.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by USENIX, a long-standing nonprofit, with USENIX proceedings. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably top tier (A*, h5 110) and a major home for adversarial-ML and ML-privacy papers. But it is a general security flagship, and most of its programme is not ML.

candidates.organizer: IEEE Computer Society Technical Community on Security and Privacy, in cooperation with IACR. 2027 PC chairs are Michelle Mazurek and Nicolas Papernot.
candidates.publication: IEEE Computer Society proceedings (IEEE Xplore)
candidates.size: 253 accepted out of 1,995 reviewed submissions in 2026 (about 12.7%)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A* (verified); CCF A (per ccfddl); GS h5-index 110 (verified)
candidates.cadence: Annual (May), with two submission cycles per edition
candidates.next_meeting: 48th edition: May 17-19, 2027 (workshops May 20), Le Centre Sheraton, Montreal, Canada
candidates.next_deadline: Cycle 2: abstract registration Nov 10, 2026 and full paper Nov 17, 2026 (AoE)
candidates.why_fit: The CFP lists four explicit ML topics: privacy, integrity, attacks and verification of ML systems. It is a sibling venue to the tracked SaTML.
candidates.concerns: Mostly non-ML. The next deadline is in about 2.5 weeks. If security flagships are added, ACM CCS and NDSS are the natural siblings. ACM CCS's acronym clashes with the tracked CCS (Complex Systems).
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE Computer Society Technical Community on Security and Privacy, with decades of history. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: USENIX Security Symposium
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier (A*, h5 116) with explicit Security-of-ML and Privacy-of-ML topics. But it is a systems-security venue that requires ML papers to matter to systems security, so it is mostly non-ML.
candidates.subtopics: Security and privacy of ML, LLM attacks, and general systems security
candidates.organizer: USENIX. 2027 PC co-chairs are Adam Doupé and Andrei Sabelfeld; there is also an AI Integrity Chair.
candidates.publication: USENIX open-access proceedings
candidates.size: 362 accepted out of 3,028 submissions in 2026 (about 12%)
candidates.acceptance_rate: About 12% (362/3028) in 2026; 17% (407/2385) in 2025. Figures are from ccfddl, citing the USENIX chairs' messages.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A* (verified); CCF A (per ccfddl); GS h5-index 116 (verified)
candidates.next_meeting: 36th edition: Aug 11-13, 2027, Hyatt Regency Denver at Colorado Convention Center, Denver, CO
candidates.next_deadline: Cycle 2: mandatory registration Jan 19, 2027 and full paper Jan 26, 2027 (AoE)
candidates.why_fit: Publishes many ML-security, ML-privacy and LLM-attack papers next to the tracked SaTML. It is adjacent rather than central.
candidates.concerns: General security flagship, mostly non-ML, and the CFP warns that ML work must be relevant to systems security. Overlaps IEEE S&P; adding one without the other (and ACM CCS/NDSS) may look arbitrary.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Run by USENIX, with an ethics committee and artifact evaluation. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: Privacy in Statistical Databases
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate, long-standing niche venue with LNCS proceedings, but small (about 23-28 papers) and ICORE C. Its focus is official-statistics disclosure control, a weak fit, and the next edition is not until 2028. Low priority.
candidates.subtopics: Statistical disclosure control, differential privacy, synthetic data
candidates.organizer: UNESCO Chair in Data Privacy, Universitat Rovira i Virgili (Josep Domingo-Ferrer's group, CRISES)
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS proceedings
candidates.size: 23 papers (2026, Cádiz), 28 (2024, Antibes), 25 (2022, Paris)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 C (verified); CCF none found; no Google Scholar Metrics entry found
candidates.next_meeting: PSD 2026 already took place on Sep 30 - Oct 2, 2026 in Cádiz, Spain. PSD 2028 is unannounced.
candidates.next_deadline: unknown (2028 edition not announced)
candidates.why_fit: Covers differential privacy, synthetic data and disclosure risk. It is adjacent to the privacy part of responsible AI and to SaTML.
candidates.concerns: The official site fails TLS (hostname mismatch), and its redirect target returns 403, so details are unverifiable from the organiser page. It mainly serves statistics agencies, and there is nothing to add to the calendar before 2028.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Academic UNESCO Chair, consistent Springer LNCS series. No predatory signals.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Law
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate society conference (IAAIL since 1987, ACM proceedings), but niche and ICORE C. It is closer to legal reasoning, argumentation and legal NLP than to responsible-AI governance, and the 2027 host is unannounced.
candidates.subtopics: Legal reasoning, legal NLP, AI regulation, argumentation
candidates.organizer: International Association for Artificial Intelligence and Law (IAAIL), a non-profit founded in 1987
candidates.publication: ACM conference proceedings (open access required from 2026, authors pay the fee)
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 C (verified); CCF none found; GS h5-index 24 (verified)
candidates.next_meeting: unknown. The 21st edition was Jun 8-12, 2026 in Singapore. IAAIL's call for bids to host the 22nd ICAIL in 2027 (Aug 2025) has no announced outcome.
candidates.next_deadline: unknown. The 2026 long/short paper deadline was 31 Jan 2026 (extended), so expect around late Jan 2027 if 2027 goes ahead.
candidates.why_fit: An AI-and-law community covering legal NLP, AI regulation and argumentation. It touches the governance side of responsible AI and the tracked KR/NLP venues.
candidates.concerns: Niche and lower tier. The IAAIL site has no news since Dec 2025 and no 2027 host or dates. The governance overlap is partial; much of its work is legal informatics.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Long-standing scholarly society with an associated Springer journal (Artificial Intelligence and Law), and ACM proceedings. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Legal Knowledge and Information Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate society conference held every year since 1988, but it is a C-ranked legal-informatics niche. It sits next to responsible AI and NLP rather than at their centre.
candidates.subtopics: Legal AI, legal NLP/LLMs, argumentation, XAI and fairness in legal AI, AI regulation
candidates.organizer: JURIX Foundation for Legal Knowledge Based Systems (Netherlands/Flanders; board president Katie Atkinson)
candidates.publication: IOS Press, Frontiers in AI and Applications (FAIA), gold open access
candidates.size: 39th edition in 2026; long (10 pp), short (5 pp) and poster (2 pp) papers. Accepted-paper counts not found.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 C; CCF 2026 none found; GS h5-index 18 (h5-median 25)
candidates.next_meeting: Dec 8-10, 2026, Toulouse, France (39th; Université Toulouse Capitole/IRIT)
candidates.next_deadline: 2026 deadlines have passed (recommended abstract Aug 28, full paper Sept 5, 2026). JURIX 2027 full paper estimated for early Sept 2027.
candidates.why_fit: The 2026 CFP explicitly lists fairness and bias in legal AI, explainable AI, AI regulation and governance, legal NLP and LLMs, and argumentation/KR. It is the European sister venue to ICAIL.
candidates.concerns: Applied legal-domain niche with C tier. Most papers are legal reasoning or argumentation, not general responsible-AI methods. Single-blind review; acceptance rate not published.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Computer Safety, Reliability and Security
candidates.verdict_reason: Very well established (since 1979, run by EWICS TC7, ICORE B, LNCS), but it is safety-critical systems engineering. ML or AI safety appears mainly through the WAISE workshop and the 2027 autonomy theme.
candidates.subtopics: Safety assurance, dependability, security of critical and autonomous systems; AI safety engineering via WAISE
candidates.organizer: EWICS TC7 (European Workshop on Industrial Computer Systems), which acts as the steering committee; 2027 hosted by the University of York
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (14-page papers via EasyChair)
candidates.size: 45th edition in 2026 (Valencia), 46th in 2027. Paper counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 B; CCF 2026 none found; GS h5-index 20 (h5-median 29)
candidates.next_meeting: Sept 6-9, 2027, York, UK (workshops Sept 6, main conference Sept 7-9)
candidates.next_deadline: Full paper Mar 1, 2027, preceded by a paper abstract on Feb 22, 2027
candidates.why_fit: Covers the robustness, safety and assurance side of the Robustness & Safety subtopic. The 2027 theme is safety assurance for complex autonomous systems, and the WAISE AI-safety workshop is co-located.
candidates.concerns: Mostly dependability, formal methods and safety cases, with little ML research. The old safecomp.org address redirects to a stale Google Site, so use ewics.org or the per-year sites. Acceptance rate not published.

candidates.full_name: IEEE/ACM International Conference on AI Engineering – Software Engineering for AI
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and fairly well cited for its age (ICORE B, credible steering committee), but it is a young software-engineering venue. It covers only the deployment edge of responsible AI.
candidates.subtopics: SE for ML systems, MLOps, AI quality assurance, safety and security of AI components, agentic SE
candidates.organizer: Steering committee chaired by Helena Holmström Olsson (members include Kästner, Cleland-Huang, Bosch); co-hosted with ICSE
candidates.publication: ICSE co-located event proceedings in the IEEE and ACM Digital Libraries (IEEE template in 2027)
candidates.size: About 60 research-track entries listed for CAIN 2026 (Rio de Janeiro). Attendance unknown.
candidates.acceptance_rate: unknown (CFP says no limit on accepted papers)
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 B; CCF 2026 none found; GS h5-index 19 (h5-median 23)
candidates.next_meeting: 6th edition within ICSE 2027 week, Apr 25-May 1, 2027, Dublin, Ireland. CAIN's own dates are still TBA.
candidates.next_deadline: Research-track full/short paper deadline was Oct 30, 2026 (firm, now passed). Industry, poster/demo and doctoral tracks close Nov 6, 2026. CAIN 2028 research papers estimated for late Oct 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Covers quality assurance, safety and security engineering, and requirements for ML-enabled systems. This matches the Human-AI Interaction & Deployment and Robustness & Safety subtopics, and partly ML Systems.
candidates.concerns: Software-engineering community and methods rather than ML research. Founded in 2022. The CFP states no limit on accepted papers, and no acceptance rate is published. It does not use responsible or trustworthy AI as headline topics.

candidates.full_name: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility
candidates.verdict_reason: Premier and highly legitimate accessibility venue (ACM SIGACCESS, ICORE A), but its central scope is assistive technology, not responsible-AI methods. Fit is adjacent at best.
candidates.subtopics: Accessibility, assistive technology, inclusive and AI-for-accessibility systems
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGACCESS
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings (ACM Digital Library)
candidates.size: 29th edition in 2027. Paper counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A; CCF C (per ccfddl; not checked against the 2026 CCF PDF); GS h5-index 36 (h5-median 46)
candidates.next_meeting: Oct 24-27, 2027, Tokyo, Japan (29th)
candidates.next_deadline: Technical paper deadline estimated for late April 2027, based on Apr 22, 2026 (AoE)
candidates.why_fit: Inclusion and accessibility side of human-centred and human-AI interaction, with a growing body of inclusive-AI and AI-for-accessibility work.
candidates.concerns: Little overlap with fairness, XAI, governance, privacy or robustness. The 2027 CFP and deadlines are not posted yet. Previously deferred by the owner.

candidates.full_name: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
candidates.verdict_reason: Top-tier and unquestionably legitimate (ICORE A*, GS h5 53), but its core is interaction techniques, sensing, fabrication and AR/VR. It is the weakest responsible-AI fit in this batch and worth adding only for HCI-systems coverage alongside CHI.
candidates.subtopics: Interaction techniques, AI/LLM-powered interfaces, sensing, AR/VR, fabrication
candidates.organizer: ACM (SIGCHI with SIGGRAPH)
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings (ACM Digital Library)
candidates.size: 39th edition in 2026. Paper counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A*; CCF A (per ccfddl; not checked against the 2026 CCF PDF); GS h5-index 53 (h5-median 79)
candidates.next_meeting: Nov 2-5, 2026, Detroit, USA. The 2027 site only says details are coming soon.
candidates.next_deadline: UIST 2027 abstract estimated for late March 2027 and full paper for about a week later, based on 2026 (Mar 24 and Mar 31, AoE)
candidates.why_fit: Overlap is limited to the Human-AI Interaction & Deployment subtopic: AI- and LLM-powered interfaces and tools.
candidates.concerns: Its central scope does not overlap fairness, explainability, governance, privacy or robustness. The 2026 CFP lists no AI topics. The 2027 venue and dates are TBA. Previously deferred by the owner.

candidates.full_name: ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate ACM venue (ICORE B, GS h5 34), but its fit is multimodal ML and human sensing rather than responsible AI. It would sit better in signals-vision/healthcare next to the tracked FG. The 2027 edition is not announced.
candidates.subtopics: Multimodal ML and fusion, affective computing, social signal processing, human-centred AI
candidates.organizer: ACM (SIGCHI-sponsored) with the ICMI steering committee
candidates.publication: ACM proceedings for long and short papers; workshop papers in adjunct proceedings. APC of $250-350 in 2026 under ACM Open.
candidates.size: 28th edition in 2026. Paper counts not verified.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 B; CCF C (per ccfddl; not checked against the 2026 CCF PDF); GS h5-index 34 (h5-median 47)
candidates.next_meeting: Oct 5-9, 2026 in Naples, Italy, has already passed. The 2027 edition is not announced on icmi.acm.org.
candidates.next_deadline: ICMI 2027 abstract estimated for mid-April 2027 and full paper for late April 2027, based on 2026 (Apr 13 and Apr 23 extended, AoE)
candidates.why_fit: Multimodal ML and fusion, affective computing, and social-behaviour sensing overlap the Biometrics & Human Sensing and multimodal topics. The CFP also lists human-centred AI and ethics.
candidates.concerns: Responsible AI is a minor CFP topic, so the proposed family mapping should be signals-vision/healthcare. The 2027 page is not live, and no acceptance statistics were found. Previously deferred by the owner.

candidates.full_name: Conference of the European Study Group on Cardiovascular Oscillations
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, methods-heavy niche meeting run by strong physiological-signal groups. But the series site was unreachable, so the next edition, dates and deadline could not be verified.
candidates.subtopics: HRV and blood-pressure variability; cardiorespiratory coupling; complexity and entropy of physiological series; physiological networks; autonomic modelling.
candidates.organizer: ESGCO community with an ESGCO board; each edition is run by a host lab. The 2024 host was the BSICoS group at I3A, University of Zaragoza (Bailón, Laguna and others), and the 2020 host was Valenza's Pisa group.
candidates.publication: Two-page IEEE-style papers, indexed in IEEE Xplore and Scopus according to the 2024 site. Selected papers are invited to journal special issues.
candidates.size: Small, with a single-track programme plus posters, 5 keynotes and a data challenge (2024). Attendee and paper counts are not stated.
candidates.rankings: None found: not in ICORE or CORE, not in CCF, no GS h5.
candidates.founded: 13th edition in 2024. Earlier history is unverified (from memory, around 2000).
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown. The biennial pattern implies a 14th ESGCO in 2026, but esgco.org refused connections, so I could not verify it or tell whether it has already happened.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. In 2024 the 2-page paper was due in mid or late May for an October meeting.
candidates.why_fit: Genuine overlap with the healthcare signal venues (EMBC, BHI) and the nonlinear time-series and dynamics venues (Dynamics Days, ITISE).
candidates.concerns: Official series site down (ECONNREFUSED), so the current edition is unverifiable. Very small and specialised; the 2024 site carried copy-paste errors from 2020.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Credible academic hosts and keynotes (Valenza, Corino, Mincholé). IEEE Xplore proceedings, an ESGCO board meeting and a yearly data challenge. No predatory pattern.

candidates.full_name: ERNSI Workshop on System Identification (European Research Network System Identification)
candidates.verdict_reason: No open submission route. ERNSI 2026 registration was 'by invitation only', and contributions are collected through the network's local team leaders.
candidates.subtopics: System identification; data-driven modelling; kernel and Bayesian identification; learning dynamical models.
candidates.organizer: European Research Network System Identification, launched by the EC in 1992 and coordinated by A. Chiuso (Padova). 2026 local chairs: Tóth, Schoukens and Batselier (TU/e); programme chair Campi.
candidates.publication: None (talks and posters only).
candidates.size: Unknown; a small residential network workshop with 30-minute talks and posters.
candidates.rankings: None found (not in ICORE or CCF).
candidates.next_meeting: Unknown for 2027. The 2026 edition was 20-23 Sept 2026 in Deurne, Netherlands.
candidates.next_deadline: Unknown. In 2026, abstracts were due 1 Jul 2026 and registration by 1 Aug 2026, both for invited registrants.
candidates.why_fit: Central to the system-identification leaf, between IFAC SYSID and L4DC.
candidates.concerns: Invitation-only registration, and submissions only from registered participants via ERNSI team leaders. This matches the catalog's exclusion of events with no open submission route.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Highly reputable European sysid network with more than 30 years of continuity and strong plenary speakers.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Workshop on Applications of Signal Processing to Audio and Acoustics
candidates.verdict_reason: The flagship workshop of the IEEE SPS AASP Technical Committee, running since 1986 with double-blind archival papers. It is central to the catalog's audio and signal-processing leaf next to ICASSP and Interspeech.
candidates.subtopics: Audio and acoustic SP; source separation; speech and audio enhancement; spatial audio; machine listening; music signal processing.
candidates.organizer: Audio and Acoustic Signal Processing TC of the IEEE Signal Processing Society. 2027 general chairs: A. Mesaros (Tampere) and G. Peeters (Télécom Paris).
candidates.publication: 4-page papers plus 1 page of references, double-blind with at least 3 reviewers. IEEE proceedings, from memory in IEEE Xplore; the current site does not state this.
candidates.size: Unknown; a small single-venue workshop, with paper counts not posted on the site.
candidates.rankings: Not in ICORE 2026 or CCF. GS h5 is below 25 (absent from the GS Acoustics & Sound top-20, whose cutoff is 25).
candidates.next_meeting: 19-22 Sept 2027 in Levi, Finland (dates tentative per the official site).
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract registration 14 Apr 2027; full 4-page paper 21 Apr 2027 (official but labelled tentative).
candidates.why_fit: Directly complements the tracked ICASSP, EUSIPCO, MLSP, SSP and Interspeech.
candidates.concerns: Low citation metrics typical of a biennial workshop. The 2027 dates and deadlines are still tentative, and Xplore indexing was not confirmed on the current site.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: IEEE SPS technical-committee workshop with a long chair lineage (Kellermann, Ellis, Naylor/Müller, Le Roux/Gerkmann). Double-blind review with meta-reviewers.

candidates.full_name: ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security
candidates.verdict_reason: Unquestionably top-tier (A*, CCF A), but only its 'Security and Privacy of ML' track overlaps the catalog. Most of the programme is systems and network security outside its scope.
candidates.subtopics: Security and privacy of ML (dedicated track); privacy and anonymity; applied cryptography; adversarial ML.
candidates.organizer: ACM SIGSAC
candidates.publication: ACM conference proceedings (ACM Digital Library); 12-page sigconf papers.
candidates.size: 234 accepted of 1222 submissions (2023); 196 of 880 (2021).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 A*; CCF A; GS h5 90 (Computer Security & Cryptography, #5).
candidates.next_meeting: 11-15 Oct 2027 in Atlanta, USA (official CCS2027 placeholder page). CCS 2026 is 15-19 Nov 2026 in The Hague.
candidates.next_deadline: CCS 2027 Cycle A full paper: estimated early-to-mid Jan 2027 (2026 pattern: abstract 7 Jan, paper 14 Jan). Not yet posted.
candidates.why_fit: Adjacent: a major venue for ML privacy and adversarial ML, overlapping the tracked SaTML and the responsible-ai family.
candidates.concerns: Identity trap: needs the series name 'ACM CCS', distinct from the tracked CCS (Complex Systems). Weak central fit, and the CCS 2027 deadlines are not yet posted.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: ACM SIGSAC flagship and one of the 'big four' security conferences; credible acceptance rates.

candidates.full_name: International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate world congress of applied mathematics under the ICIAM council. But the scope is extremely broad, it meets only every four years, and individual contributions are limited to posters or minisymposium proposals.
candidates.subtopics: Topic areas include dynamical systems/ODEs; control and optimisation; mathematical foundations of ML; UQ and inverse problems; mathematics in biology.
candidates.organizer: Held under the auspices of the International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (member societies include SIAM, GAMM and SMAI, from memory). Run by a local organizing committee with the congress agency Congress by Design.
candidates.publication: None archival (abstracts only).
candidates.size: 4000+ participants from 70+ countries (official expected figure); 25+ invited speakers.
candidates.rankings: Not in ICORE 2026 (only a historical ERA2010 B); not CCF; no GS h5.
candidates.next_meeting: 12-16 July 2027 in The Hague, Netherlands (iciam.org says 12-17 July).
candidates.next_deadline: 7 Dec 2026: minisymposium proposals and poster abstracts (200 words). There is no individual contributed-talk category.
candidates.why_fit: Same community as the tracked SIAM DS, with dedicated dynamics, control and ML-foundations topic areas, though these are a small part of a huge programme.
candidates.concerns: Very broad multi-field scope, one edition per four years, and talks only via organised minisymposia. The deadline is about five weeks away.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Flagship congress of the ICIAM council of applied-mathematics societies; long history.

candidates.full_name: SNUFA: Spiking Neural networks as Universal Function Approximators (online workshop)
candidates.verdict_reason: Well regarded in the spiking-network community, with open abstract submission. But it is a tiny online-only event with no proceedings and no society.
candidates.subtopics: Spiking neural networks; surrogate-gradient training; neuromorphic computing; spiking models of neural circuits.
candidates.organizer: Community-run by S. van Albada, J. Eshraghian, D. Goodman and F. Zenke (2026).
candidates.publication: None (abstracts posted online; talks on YouTube).
candidates.size: Two half-days with 4 invited talks, 7 contributed talks, flash talks and a virtual poster session (2024-2026). Attendance not stated.
candidates.rankings: None found
candidates.next_meeting: 4-5 Nov 2026, online (abstracts closed). The next edition is expected around early Nov 2027, online.
candidates.next_deadline: Around late Sept 2027 for abstracts, estimated from SNUFA 2024 (deadline 27 Sept).
candidates.why_fit: Bridges the computational-neuroscience venues (CNS*, COSYNE, Bernstein) and neuromorphic computing (NICE).
candidates.concerns: Online only, very small, and deadlines are not posted in advance. Free registration with no archival output.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Leading SNN researchers organise and speak (e.g. Izhikevich, Petrovici, Schreiber in 2026). Abstracts are selected by blinded public rating.

candidates.full_name: Workshop on Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events
candidates.verdict_reason: This is the strongest candidate in the batch: a legitimate, community-run workshop that is the main venue for machine listening, with archival proceedings. It is a narrow sub-niche next to ICASSP and Interspeech, it is tied to the challenge, and its ICORE, CCF and h5 standing could not be verified.
candidates.subtopics: Sound event detection, acoustic scene classification, bioacoustics, audio representation learning, anomalous sound detection.
candidates.organizer: Run by the DCASE community steering group (Mesaros, Serizel, Cartwright, Font, Stowell, Harada, Kong and others; earlier members include Plumbley, Virtanen, Ellis, Bello, Richard). Bose, MIT and Tufts were only the local co-organisers for 2026.
candidates.publication: Self-published archival proceedings with an ISBN and a Zenodo DOI each year (2025: ISBN 978-84-09-77652-8; 2026: ISBN 979-8-234-25461-0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22954971).
candidates.size: About 50 papers in the 2025 proceedings (229 pp) and about 55-60 in 2026 (more than 260 pp). The DCASE2026 challenge received 421 entries. Attendance is not published.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (the portal blocked automated access); not found in CCF; GS h5 not verified.
candidates.cadence: Annual (Oct-Nov). Workshops since 2016 (the first was a EUSIPCO satellite); the challenge started in 2013.
candidates.next_meeting: DCASE 2026 was held 27-29 Oct 2026 in Cambridge/Medford, MA (AIR workshop on the 27th, main workshop 28-29). The 2027 edition is not announced; only its task-proposal call is out.
candidates.next_deadline: Estimated around early July 2027 (abstract) and mid-July 2027 (full paper), based on 5/12 Jul 2026 and 4/11 Jul 2025.
candidates.why_fit: Central for audio and bioacoustic ML and sound event detection, sitting between ICASSP, Interspeech and EUSIPCO. Its standalone-workshop style matches AALTD and TS4H.
candidates.concerns: Many papers are expanded challenge system reports, and the CFP gives no page or review details. Selectivity is unknown. The scope is a narrow audio niche.

candidates.full_name: IAPR-TC15 International Workshop on Graph-Based Representations in Pattern Recognition
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and long-running: an IAPR technical-committee workshop with a credible graph-PR programme committee. It is very small, its cadence is irregular, the 2027 edition is not announced, and its standing could not be verified.
candidates.subtopics: Graph matching, graph edit distance, graph kernels, GNNs for pattern recognition.
candidates.organizer: IAPR Technical Committee 15 (Graph-based Representations). 2025 chairs: Brun, Gaüzère, Bougleux, Carletti. The PC includes Vento, Foggia, Riesen, Torsello, Micheli, Escolano, Kropatsch and C.-L. Liu.
candidates.size: Small, probably a few dozen papers (not verified). Single-track, three days.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (portal blocked); not found in CCF; GS h5 not verified.
candidates.cadence: Roughly biennial in odd years, but irregular: 12th Tours 2019, 13th Salerno 2023, 14th Caen 2025 (no 2021 edition).
candidates.next_meeting: unknown (a 15th edition in 2027 is likely but not announced).
candidates.next_deadline: unknown. 2025 decisions went out in May 2025, which implies a full-paper deadline around Feb-Mar.
candidates.why_fit: Graph matching, kernels and GNNs from the pattern-recognition side. It complements LoG and the IAPR family (ICPR, ACPR, S+SSPR).
candidates.concerns: A tiny niche venue; LNCS alone is not evidence of quality. Its topics overlap heavily with S+SSPR (which is co-run with IAPR TC1/TC2) and LoG. The next edition is not announced.

candidates.full_name: IEEE Pacific Visualization Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and IEEE VGTC sponsored, with a TVCG journal track. Visualization lies outside the catalog's current core, and this is the second-tier regional venue, so it only makes sense after IEEE VIS or EuroVis open a visualization leaf.
candidates.subtopics: Visualization, visual analytics, graph/network visualization, scientific visualization, AI for vis.
candidates.organizer: Sponsored by IEEE VGTC (IEEE Computer Society). Annual, rotating around the Asia-Pacific.
candidates.publication: Journal track published in IEEE TVCG; conference papers and VisNotes in IEEE proceedings.
candidates.size: unknown (regional, single-digit hundreds of attendees likely; not verified).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (portal blocked). CCF C in the 2022 list (recalled; 2026 list not verified). GS h5 not verified.
candidates.next_meeting: 19-22 Apr 2027, Busan, South Korea (20th edition).
candidates.next_deadline: Conference Paper track: abstract 2 Nov 2026, full paper 9 Nov 2026 (AoE). VisNotes short papers: 4 Jan 2027. The TVCG track closed 8 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_fit: Visualization and visual analytics, including graph/network visualization and vis for ML. This is adjacent to CHI and complex networks, not central.
candidates.concerns: No visualization leaf exists yet, and it ranks below IEEE VIS and EuroVis. Its ML and network overlap is partial.

candidates.full_name: Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and very long-running: the national society's flagship since 1976, now published in PMLR. It is a regional, general-AI venue with modest selectivity that adds little beyond the tracked AAAI, IJCAI and ECAI, and its rank could not be verified.
candidates.subtopics: General AI/ML, NLP, RL, responsible AI, applied AI.
candidates.organizer: Canadian Artificial Intelligence Association (CAIAC, formerly CSCSI). 2027 PC chairs: Sirisha Rambhatla (Waterloo) and Yiwei Lu (Ottawa).
candidates.publication: PMLR from 2026 (v318), CAIAC open access on PubPub 2021-2025, Springer LNAI 1996-2020.
candidates.size: 125 papers in PMLR v318 (2026; long and short papers). 2026 was held jointly with CRV as AI/CRV.
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (portal blocked); not found in CCF; GS h5 not verified.
candidates.next_meeting: 40th edition, 2027. Dates and venue not announced ('content forthcoming'); a banner hints at Vancouver, but this is unconfirmed.
candidates.next_deadline: Estimated two-round full-paper deadlines: round 1 around late Dec 2026, round 2 around Feb 2027, based on 22 Dec 2025 and 20 Feb 2026. The 2027 CFP is not yet posted.
candidates.why_fit: A general AI and ML national flagship, comparable in role to ACML. Its overlap with the catalog is broad but shallow.
candidates.concerns: Regional, with a moderate tier and broad scope. Two-round deadlines complicate the calendar. The 2027 location and dates are unknown.

candidates.full_name: Asia-Pacific Signal and Information Processing Association Annual Summit and Conference
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate society-run conference, technically co-sponsored by IEEE and IEEE SPS. It is large, broad, regional and mid-tier, and largely overlaps the tracked ICASSP, EUSIPCO and ICIP. Low priority.
candidates.subtopics: Speech/audio, image/video, biomedical signal processing, ML for signals, multimedia security.
candidates.organizer: APSIPA (society; 18th ASC in 2026). Local organisation for 2026 by the ECTI Association, with general co-chairs including C.-C. Jay Kuo (USC).
candidates.publication: Conference proceedings, technically co-sponsored by IEEE and IEEE SPS. The pages fetched do not state IEEE Xplore indexing.
candidates.size: unknown (multi-track, likely several hundred papers; not verified).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (portal blocked); not found in CCF; GS h5 not verified.
candidates.next_meeting: 10-12 Nov 2026, Bangkok (winter school 9 Nov). The 2027 edition is not announced.
candidates.next_deadline: 2026 deadlines have passed (full paper 30 Jun, late-breaking 2-page 31 Aug 2026). Next estimated: full paper around mid/late June 2027.
candidates.why_fit: An Asia-Pacific signal and information processing flagship covering speech, audio, image/video and biomedical signals. It is a partial complement to ICASSP and EUSIPCO.
candidates.concerns: The scope is very broad, including communications and security. Selectivity is moderate, the proceedings publisher is not stated, and the 2027 host is unknown.

candidates.full_name: International Conference on Geometric Science of Information
candidates.verdict_reason: A legitimate, well-known niche conference for information geometry, with credible keynotes (e.g. F. Bach, B. Sturmfels in 2023) and institutional partners. It is mathematically adjacent to ML rather than central, runs through special sessions, has no verifiable rank, and its 2027 edition is not announced.
candidates.subtopics: Information geometry, statistical manifolds, geometric statistics, geometric deep learning, quantum information geometry.
candidates.organizer: SEE (a French learned society for electrical and information engineering). General co-chairs: Frédéric Barbaresco (Thales) and Frank Nielsen (Sony CSL). Partners include Inria, CNRS GDR IASIS, ELLIS and SMAI.
candidates.publication: Springer LNCS (8-page papers).
candidates.size: unknown (probably on the order of 100 short papers per edition; not verified).
candidates.rankings: ICORE 2026 not verified (portal blocked); not found in CCF; GS h5 not verified.
candidates.cadence: Biennial, odd years, confirmed by the 2013-2025 edition list (7 editions).
candidates.next_meeting: unknown. GSI'27 is not announced; the last two editions were held in Saint-Malo in autumn.
candidates.next_deadline: Estimated: 8-page LNCS paper around late April 2027, based on 22 Apr 2025.
candidates.why_fit: Information geometry, geometric statistics and geometric deep learning. This is the mathematical side of ML theory and links to the catalog's dynamics venues.
candidates.concerns: Organised largely via invited special sessions and chaired from industry, so it has a narrow, math-heavy audience. LNCS alone is not evidence of quality. Fit with the catalog is adjacent.

candidates.full_name: European Conference on Computational Biology
candidates.verdict_reason: Clearly legitimate and high-level, with its proceedings track in the journal Bioinformatics. Molecular bioinformatics is adjacent to the catalog rather than central. Odd-year editions are joint ISMB/ECCB, a duplicate if ISMB is added, and the 2028 standalone edition is unannounced.
candidates.subtopics: Computational biology; ML for genomics and proteins; systems biology; biomedical data integration.
candidates.organizer: European comp-bio community with a rotating national host. 2026: SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics with ELIXIR. Odd years are co-organised with ISCB as ISMB/ECCB. No standalone steering-committee page found.
candidates.publication: The proceedings track is a supplement of Bioinformatics (OUP). The 2027 joint edition publishes in an open-access Bioinformatics issue. Posters and highlight talks are non-archival.
candidates.size: 2026: the site advertises 1,000 to 1,500+ attendees. ISMB/ECCB 2027 expects more than 600 talks.
candidates.acceptance_rate: Unknown. The ISMB/ECCB call says only 'very competitive'.
candidates.rankings: Not verified in this run: the ICORE portal returned 403 and the CCF PDF was unreadable. There is no separate GS h5, because papers appear in Bioinformatics.
candidates.cadence: Biennial standalone in even years; joint ISMB/ECCB in odd years (official About page).
candidates.founded: About 2002, inferred from edition numbering (11th in 2012, counting joint editions).
candidates.next_meeting: Joint ISMB/ECCB 2027: 18-22 July 2027, Bella Center Copenhagen, Denmark. The next standalone ECCB (2028) is not announced.
candidates.next_deadline: ISMB/ECCB 2027 proceedings full paper: 14 Jan 2027 AoE ('no extension'). Abstract and poster dates are not shown on the Key Dates page.
candidates.why_fit: ML for genomics and proteins and biomedical data integration overlap the healthcare and ML families (MICCAI, CHIL, ISBI-adjacent).
candidates.concerns: Its centre of gravity is molecular biology, not clinical ML or neuroscience. Overlap with ISMB means only the even-year editions would add value. There is no deadline for a standalone edition until 2028.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Hosted by national bioinformatics institutes, partnered with ISCB, with proceedings in a leading OUP journal. 2026 scientific chairs: A.-F. Bitbol (EPFL) and N. Beerenwinkel (ETH).

candidates.full_name: BayesComp: Biennial Conference of the ISBA Bayesian Computation Section
candidates.verdict_reason: Identity verified: the flagship meeting of the ISBA Bayesian Computation Section, descended from MCMSki (2005). It has a confirmed 2027 edition and deadline and the strongest fit of the Bayesian candidates. It is still a statistics-side, non-archival meeting adjacent to ProbML and AISTATS rather than core ML.
candidates.subtopics: MCMC and SMC; variational inference; scalable Bayesian computation; probabilistic programming.
candidates.organizer: BayesComp-ISBA, the Bayesian Computation Section of the International Society for Bayesian Analysis. The ASA Section on Bayesian Statistical Science endorsed the 2025 edition.
candidates.publication: None: contributed talks and posters only.
candidates.size: Unknown; official pages give no attendance figures. 2027 has three keynotes, including Chris Oates and Lester Mackey.
candidates.rankings: None found; this is a statistics meeting outside ICORE and CCF scope.
candidates.next_meeting: 18-20 May 2027, Annenberg Presidential Conference Center, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA.
candidates.next_deadline: Contributed-talk abstract: 15 Nov 2026. Poster abstract: 3 Jan 2027. Talk decisions are due by the end of Dec 2026.
candidates.why_fit: MCMC, SMC, variational inference and probabilistic programming are the computational core of the tracked ProbML (ex-AABI), and the meeting draws ML speakers.
candidates.concerns: Statistics-centred and abstract-only with no proceedings. Attendance is unpublished. The candidate's URL (bayesian.org homepage) was wrong; the series pages are bayescomp-isba.github.io and bayescomp2027.org.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: Official ISBA section meeting with about 20 years of continuity and well-known keynotes (Oates, Mackey; 2025: Frühwirth-Schnatter, Jacob, Khan). No red flags.

candidates.full_name: ISBA World Meeting (International Society for Bayesian Analysis)
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and large society flagship, but scope is broad Bayesian statistics, including applied modelling, so the fit with the catalog is weak. The 2028 edition is unannounced, so nothing can be added now. BayesComp is the better-fitting Bayesian venue.
candidates.subtopics: Bayesian methodology; Bayesian ML and computation; nonparametrics; applied Bayesian modelling.
candidates.organizer: International Society for Bayesian Analysis (ISBA). 2026: LOC chaired by K. Kakamu (Nagoya City Univ.), Scientific Committee chaired by S. Deshpande (UW-Madison).
candidates.publication: None: contributed talks and posters only.
candidates.size: 2026 (18th meeting, Nagoya): 874 participants, 265 talks, 398 posters, 11 plenary sessions.
candidates.rankings: None found; this is a statistics meeting outside ICORE and CCF scope.
candidates.cadence: Biennial in even years (2026 was the 18th). Earlier editions (2022 Montreal, 2024 Venice) are from memory, not verified.
candidates.founded: ISBA 1992 (from memory, not verified); 18th World Meeting in 2026.
candidates.next_meeting: 2028 edition: unknown (not announced on bayesian.org or the 2026 site).
candidates.next_deadline: unknown
candidates.why_fit: Bayesian ML, computation and nonparametrics are adjacent to the tracked ProbML, UAI and AISTATS.
candidates.concerns: Broad statistics scope with a large applied share. The catalog tracks no pure-statistics meetings. No proceedings. No 2028 dates or deadlines.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A long-standing international scientific society with a well-attended flagship and named academic committees. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: International Congress of Neuroethology
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate and well regarded: run by the International Society for Neuroethology (founded 1981), with congresses since 1986 and a selective talk programme. It is organism- and behaviour-centred rather than computational, which is adjacent to the catalog's neuroscience core, and the 2028 congress is unannounced.
candidates.subtopics: Neuroethology; sensorimotor integration; vocal learning and birdsong; quantitative natural behaviour.
candidates.organizer: International Society for Neuroethology (ISN), founded 1981 in Kassel, Germany. 2026 hosted at the University of British Columbia.
candidates.publication: None. ISN states that ICN abstracts are not citable.
candidates.size: 2026: 114 talk slots selected from abstracts, plus 15 invited symposia and 4 special sessions. Registration was capped below Berlin 2024. Total attendance is not published.
candidates.acceptance_rate: Unknown; 114 talk slots were selected from all abstracts in 2026.
candidates.rankings: None found (not applicable).
candidates.cadence: Biennial since 2014 (2014, 2016, 2018, 2022, 2024, 2026; 2020 skipped); about triennial before 2010.
candidates.next_meeting: 17th ICN (2028): not announced. The last congress was 26-31 July 2026 in Vancouver.
candidates.next_deadline: Abstract (poster or short talk): about March 2028, estimated from the 22 Mar 2026 deadline. Not announced.
candidates.why_fit: Sensorimotor integration, vocal learning and quantitative natural behaviour complement the catalog's systems-neuroscience meetings (SfN, COSYNE, Bernstein).
candidates.concerns: Low computational content and organism-specific framing. It partly overlaps SfN in content. No 2028 information yet.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: A 40-year society with 16 congresses across major universities and cities, and Program Committee review of abstracts. No red flags.

candidates.full_name: IFAC Conference on Modelling, Identification and Control of Nonlinear Systems
candidates.verdict_reason: Legitimate IFAC conference (main sponsor TC2.3) with a strong 2027 programme committee and organisers, and a good fit beside IFAC SYSID and NODYCON. It is a small, second-tier meeting compared with CDC and ECC, with unpublished size and a deadline listed as tentative.
candidates.subtopics: Nonlinear system identification; nonlinear control and stability; modelling of biological and medical systems.
candidates.organizer: IFAC: main sponsor TC2.3 Non-Linear Control Systems; co-sponsors TC1.1, 2.1, 2.6, 6.1, 8.2 and 9.4. 2027: TU Eindhoven (NOC chair M. Lazar, co-chairs R. Tóth and M. Schoukens); IPC chair L. Zaccarian (Trento).
candidates.publication: IFAC-PapersOnLine (Elsevier) for regular papers (4-8 pages at submission, 6 final). 4-page discussion extended abstracts appear in the preprints only. A journal option exists, journal not named.
candidates.size: unknown
candidates.rankings: None found; this is a control venue outside ICORE and CCF scope (not verified this run).
candidates.cadence: Triennial, inferred from the 5th edition in 2027. Earlier editions (2015, 2018, 2021, 2024) are from memory; the official site does not list them.
candidates.founded: About 2015, inferred from the triennial 5th edition in 2027.
candidates.next_meeting: 5th MICNON: 7-10 Sept 2027 (workshops 6 Sept), High Tech Campus Conference Center, Eindhoven, Netherlands.
candidates.next_deadline: Regular full paper: 1 Feb 2027 (journal option 8 Jan 2027; submission opens 15 Nov 2026). The site marks these tentative, and the IFAC calendar says 25 Jan 2027.
candidates.why_fit: Nonlinear system identification, modelling and control, including biological and medical systems, extend the catalog's control and system-identification coverage (IFAC SYSID, CDC, ECC, NODYCON).
candidates.concerns: Small and lower tier. IFAC sponsorship alone is weak evidence. Paper counts and attendance are unpublished. Deadline dates are tentative and conflict between official pages.
candidates.legitimacy_evidence: An official IFAC technical-committee conference with peer review by the IPC and recognised nonlinear-control and system-identification researchers chairing. No predatory signals.
